body:
Ship ISO boot support for the Browser VM (Developer > Terminal > Browser VM):

- V86Controller: imageKind hda|kernel|iso; iso -> {cdrom, boot_order:0x123} (0x(THIRD)(SECOND)(FIRST), 1=fd 2=hd 3=cd).

- Panel: status-bar Boot media combobox, probe-based disabling, reboot on change.

title: Chat stream: tie-sort 500 + reload watcher + SIGTERM swallow (all fixed)
body:
Symptom: chat UI showed 1 tok/s, Very slow, 2 errs.

DONE (commits 70b021b6a, 3b605d205, 1a94a3e14):

A) context_core.py:275 scored.sort(reverse=True) on (score, episode_dict); tie compared dicts -> TypeError -> 500 on /chat/stream from turn 2 of any session -> zero streamed tokens. Fix: sort(key=lambda item: item[0]). Verified live on :8000 - turn 1 AND turn 2 both stream to status=complete.

B) main.py imported domain.shared.find_repo_root before sys.path ready -> needed PYTHONPATH=.. Fixed with inline _bootstrap_repo_root().

C) reload_includes/reload_excludes used dir/** globs; uvicorn resolve_reload_patterns globs each (node_modules/** = 40,893 entries) then runs O(n^2) Path.parents -> Config() >60s -> never binds, 100% CPU. Replaced with reload_dirs=[apps/api/server, domain, packages/core-py/domains] -> ~1ms, 1,067 files vs 29,507. CAUTION: 70b021b6a's message described this but only the bootstrap hunk landed; caught only by verifying git show HEAD afterwards.

D) pugqeep Engine.__init__ installed a process-global SIGTERM/SIGINT handler whose body was only self._running=False; self.stop() and never exited. uvicorn --reload sent SIGTERM to the child then blocked forever in Process.join() -> reload fired ONCE then wedged (parent wchan=do_wait), and plain kill <pid> needed SIGKILL. Fix: _handle_signal delegates to the handler it replaced; if none and frame is not None (real delivery, not a direct test call) restore SIG_DFL and re-raise. install_signal_handlers() made idempotent so a 2nd install no longer overwrote _old_signal_handlers with our own handler. Verified on :8003 - binds 18s, 3 reloads each respawn the child (4 procs), SIGTERM then shuts down cleanly, no SIGKILL.

E) M-blind int8 GEMM threading (matmul_int8.c). Two defects:
   1. Thread gate compared N*K (B bytes) vs 6MB - M never entered, so a 601-token prefill of a 0.8MB block took the serial branch while the single-token decode of that same block (identical N*K) was eligible. Gate now tests M*N*K MACs vs the same 6e6 (numerically identical at M=1, so the decode measurements behind the constant still hold).
   2. _gemm_threads() returned 1 unconditionally. Its rationale was measured on DECODE (M=1): warm weights already near DRAM bandwidth, hyperthreads add memory-controller contention, chip throttles (124-130ms bimodal vs stable 54-67ms serial). That never applied to prefill - B is reused across all M rows so it stays cache-resident (no DRAM contention) and the work is M times larger so spawn cost is negligible. Now _gemm_threads(M): M<=1 serial (bit-for-bit the old condition), M>1 online CPUs capped at 8. MAN_GEMM_THREADS still overrides either way.
   Results (scripts/benchmark_gemm_threading.py, Qwen2.5-0.5B shapes, M in 1/64/256/601/1024 x threads 1/4/8/default):
   - prefill 1.7-3.7x at M>=64, best rows 3.2-3.4x
   - decode (M=1) unchanged: default matches serial exactly (incl. lm_head 12.36ms serial vs 6.79ms if threaded)
   - output bit-identical at every shape, M and thread count (25/25 rows)
   End-to-end chat A/B (MAN_GEMM_THREADS=1 vs unset, 3 requests each): TTFT median 18451ms -> 9720ms (1.90x), min 15847ms -> 8738ms (1.81x), decode tok/s median 4.51 -> 10.70 (no regression). Context pipeline only 145-286ms of that, so the gain is model prefill.
   Open: prefill is only ~50% this kernel (numpy attention does not run through it), which is why end-to-end is 1.9x not 3x. Trimming the 248-tok system_extra (personality 103 + style 74 + task 71) would cut prefill ~46% and is the next lever.

MEASURED, not bugs: prompt = 283 tok (base 35 + system_extra 248). Prefill 46 tok/s @250 tok, 40 @500, 29 @1000, 21 @2000. AVX-512 absent is hardware (i5-9300H, 0 zmm in .so), not a build bug.

NOT DONE / RISKS:
- _block_j_avx2 is still a GEMV wrapped in an M-loop. A 4x4 register-blocked variant was already benchmarked at +/-2% (comment in the file), so tiling is unlikely to pay; threading was the real lever and it is done.
- DONE: cherry-picked onto feat/gemm-m-aware as 4a4d4eaa1. Done in a temp worktree (removed after) precisely because a second live session keeps switching the shared tree - main worktree HEAD and its 201-file index were never touched. Content verified byte-identical to 1a94a3e14, gcc -fsyntax-only clean. Caveat: that session had committed d0592eacb (strui) onto feat/gemm-m-aware while it was checked out, so the branch carries one unrelated commit before mine; the original 1a94a3e14 remains on fix/rag-bm25-stall.
- 7 pre-existing pugqeep test failures verified against HEAD (test_wait_for_timeout x2, group x2, health, cancel, tree) - not mine.
- Port 8000 (PID 19423, other session) still runs without SLO_RELOAD; it has the sort fix and streams turn 2.

title: Frontend stops re-firing inference: no retry amplification, no immortal startup polls
body:
PROBLEM (measured, not guessed)
The frontend fires redundant inference requests of its own accord, adding load and lag on top of an already-slow backend.

A. Retry amplification on non-idempotent inference POSTs
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:165 DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:163 MAX_RETRIES = 2  -> up to 3 attempts
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:756 catch block retries on TIMEOUT with NO method check
- apps/web/lib/http-client.ts:546 client aborts at 30s; the BACKEND generation is NOT cancelled
- Logged durations routinely exceed 30s (46s, 54s, 70s, 115s, 136s observed via /benchmark/responses)
Result: one user action -> up to 3 concurrent generations contending for the GIL -> each slower
-> more timeouts -> more retries. Positive feedback loop the frontend creates itself.
Exposed apiPost callers: /companion/chat, /learn/train, /learn/evaluate, /knowledge/train-adapter,
/self-train/start, /benchmark/run, /workflow/start, /memory/consolidate, /user-adapters/aggregate-best.
Note /learn/train is called from features/chat/hooks/useChatContextValue.ts:46 (inside chat).
SSE path is CORRECT (http-client.ts:1292-1300 abort -> error, no retry; only 503 retries) - do not touch.

B. Startup polls that never stop
- apps/web/app/(app)/page.tsx:252  GET /health/startup-progress every 3s FOREVER, no phase==='ready' guard (~20 req/min indefinitely)
- apps/web/app/(app)/developer/page.tsx:817,831  /health/startup-progress + /health/startup-history every 2s forever, via RAW fetch()
  -> also violates the http-client.ts single-source-of-truth rule from AGENTS.md

INVARIANT
Retry is only safe when the operation is idempotent AND the server-side effect was cancelled.
Current code gives at-least-once semantics to a side-effecting, expensive, non-idempotent operation.

PLAN
1. http-client.ts: add isIdempotent(method); gate the timeout branch (L756) and status branch (L659) on it;
   add RequestOptions.retryOnTimeout for explicit opt-in.
2. Inference POSTs pass timeout: 120_000 + retryOnTimeout: false.
3. app/(app)/page.tsx: clear interval when phase === 'ready'.
4. developer/page.tsx: raw fetch() -> apiGet, stop polling at ready.
5. TDD: timeout on POST does not retry; timeout on GET does; 503 on GET retries; startup poll stops at ready.

SCOPE GUARD (must NOT break)
- Keep retries for GET on 502/503/504/connection-refused: uvicorn --reload now works, so restarts are more frequent and that path is load-bearing.
- Do NOT touch the SSE streaming path (already correct).
- Do NOT touch DOCSTORE_* constants (documented 400-retry exception, http-client.ts:167-171).
- Startup polls must still work during actual startup; only stop once ready.

OUT OF SCOPE (open question, not approved)
- streamSse (http-client.ts:1288) has NO timeout, only the caller signal -> chat can hang indefinitely if the backend never responds. Hang-guard proposed but NOT included in this card.

SHARED WORKSPACE
- index updated: n/a - no new app/package/doc (all changes to existing files)
- shared copy reused: reuse root node_modules + .venv, no installs
- coordination named: another live session owns feat/tamagui-generated (203 staged files) in the shared tree.
  This work goes on fix/http-retry-amplification, commits ONLY its own paths (git commit -m ... -- <paths>),
  then switches back so the other session's branch is undisturbed.
DELIVERED
- Landed as 8b475e9cf on fix/http-retry-amplification (5 files, +247/-20).
- Committed via an isolated GIT_INDEX_FILE + commit-tree so HEAD and the other session's 203-file index were never touched. The shared tree was switched twice mid-task (fix/chat-responsive-layout, then feat/design-system-tables) — all 5 changes rode along and were verified marker-by-marker before committing, and committed blobs are byte-identical to the tested worktree.
- Verification: new tests red first (POST timeout retried 3x, POST 503 retried 4x, startup polled 21x in 60s), green after. Target files 95/95. Full web suite 839/840 files / 8164/8168 tests; the 4 failures are ConvRow.test.tsx — the other session's uncommitted chat-sidebar work, whose import graph excludes every file touched here. tsc --noEmit clean; eslint 0 errors (14 pre-existing warnings).
- Side finding: dev-log.ts LogTransport POSTs /errors/logs/ingest and showed up counting as a phantom attempt in tests. It is batched, min-interval gated and never retries, so it is NOT an amplifier — left alone deliberately, since routing it through http-client would recurse on errors.
- Still open: streamSse has no timeout at all (hang-guard was never approved); the tok/s decode-vs-end-to-end measurement fix; the 248-tok system_extra trim.

title: Truthful tok/s — decode vs end-to-end, and un-break /benchmark/metrics
body:
PROBLEM (measured, not guessed)
The web UI reports ~2 tok/s and treats it as "the benchmark and the max", even though decode was measured at 10.7 tok/s after the M-aware GEMM fix.

A. /benchmark/metrics returns 500 (E_SERIALIZATION)
- apps/api/server/routers/benchmark.py:157  getattr(provider, "num_parameters", None)
- num_parameters is a plain `def` (abstractmethod, NOT @property) — models.py:82-85, slonet_provider.py:1474
- getattr returns a BOUND METHOD -> not JSON-serializable -> whole endpoint 500s after 3 consecutive failures.

B. The Tokens/s formula measures IDLE time, not generation
- benchmark.py:138-147
    inference_time = time.time() - ctrl._last_inference_time   <-- IDLE seconds since last inference
    tokens_per_sec = total_tokens / (inference_time * total_inferences)
- decays toward 0 the longer the server sits idle.

C. The headline rate is end-to-end but labelled as throughput
- inference.py:2042  start_time set BEFORE context/RAG/prefill
- inference.py:871   duration_ms = now - start_time
- inference.py:942   record_inference(tokens, elapsed_ms=duration_ms)
- server_state.py:293-310  get_tokens_per_second() = sum(tokens)/sum(elapsed_ms)
  numerator = decode tokens only, denominator = prefill + decode + session I/O -> systematically low.
- Feeds dashboard home, StatusBar, monitoring, DebugOverlay and health_flow._check_throughput
  (>=30 Fast, >=10 OK, >=5 Slow, else Very slow).

D. The history card "Best Throughput"
- apps/web/app/(app)/benchmark/page.tsx:121 history(20); :225-228 throughput = tokens_generated / duration_ms
- BenchmarkHistoryCard.tsx:78 bestThroughput = Math.max(...) ; :141 label "Best Throughput"
- Same prefill-inclusive duration. Across all 213 logged responses the max is 12.48; true decode = 10.7.

INVARIANT
A rate named "tok/s" must have a numerator and denominator drawn from the SAME window.
Today the numerator is decode-only and the denominator is end-to-end. Two different windows = a number that means nothing.

PLAN
1. benchmark.py:157 — call num_parameters() when callable. Kills the 500.
2. benchmark.py:138-147 — replace the idle-time formula with server_state's real decode rate.
3. inference.py — record first-token and last-token timestamps in the chat stream loop (2477-2743)
   -> decode_ms. Thread it through _run_post_gen_tasks -> record_inference.
4. server_state.record_inference gains decode_ms; get_tokens_per_second() uses the decode window;
   add get_end_to_end_tps() preserving the old semantics as a separately-named number.
5. response_tracker.ResponseLog gains decode_ms (NEW field, default None) so history can carry it.
   duration_ms is deliberately NOT changed — it is genuine turn latency.
6. benchmark history endpoint exposes decode_ms; frontend shows "Decode tok/s" and labels the
   end-to-end number as what it is; history card relabelled.
7. TDD for both rate formulas + the num_parameters fix + decode_ms persistence.

SCOPE GUARD (must NOT break)
- Do NOT change ResponseTracker.log duration_ms (turn latency stays end-to-end by definition).
- health_flow bands WILL flip CRITICAL -> OK when input goes ~2 -> ~10.7. That is deliberate and desired,
  not a silent regression — the meter was wrong, not the model.
- Do not touch the SSE streaming contract or the docstore retry exception (owned by the other card).
- /chat/stream must keep working end-to-end after each edit (tree is shared and moving).

SHARED WORKSPACE
- index updated: n/a (no new app/package/doc — changes to existing files)
- shared copy reused: root .venv + node_modules, no installs
- coordination named: another live session owns the shared tree and has switched branch repeatedly
  mid-task. This work therefore NEVER checks out a branch: edits land in the worktree, and the commit
  is built through an isolated GIT_INDEX_FILE + commit-tree onto a branch ref created with `git branch`
  (no checkout), so HEAD and their staged index are never touched.

DELIVERED
Branch: fix/tps-measurement @ f40f5f07f (14 files). Built via isolated GIT_INDEX_FILE +
commit-tree; HEAD and the other session's 203-file index verified untouched, and
`git diff fix/tps-measurement -- <paths>` empty (commit == worktree).

Backend
- apps/api/server/routers/benchmark.py: _resolve_num_parameters() calls num_parameters()
  when callable (was serializing a bound method -> 500 "Unable to serialize unknown type:
  <class 'function'>"); Tokens/s now reads ServerState's decode window instead of
  now - last_inference_time (idle seconds); adds end_to_end_tps.
- domain/infrastructure/_internal/server_state.py: record_inference(decode_ms=None);
  get_tokens_per_second() = decode window with fallback to elapsed for uninstrumented
  callers; get_end_to_end_tps() = the original formula under an honest name.
- apps/api/server/routers/inference.py: _first_token_at/_last_token_at captured in the
  chat stream loop, decode_ms computed after full_response assembly (so both are provably
  bound) and threaded through _run_post_gen_tasks -> ResponseTracker.log + record_inference.
- domain/feedback/_internal/response_tracker.py: ResponseLog.decode_ms (default None) +
  log(decode_ms=...) + JSONL/Mongo serialization. duration_ms untouched (scope guard).
- history endpoint exposes decode_ms.

Frontend
- benchmark-controller.ts: end_to_end_tps + decode_ms types.
- benchmark/page.tsx + evaluate/page.tsx: "Decode tok/s" and "End-to-end tok/s" shown as
  separate StatCards (was a single ambiguous "Tokens/s"/"Speed").
- BenchmarkHistoryCard: new Decode tok/s column, End-to-end column, headline stats are
  now "Best decode" / "Best end-to-end" (was "Avg/Best Throughput" = mislabelled E2E);
  unmeasured rows read "not measured" / em dash rather than a fabricated rate.
- BenchmarkChartCard: adds a Decode tok/s series, relabels throughput -> "End-to-end tok/s".

Verification

  benchmark router) + 112 passed (inference/infer routers) + 128 in the three primary files.
- Web: 40/40 across BenchmarkHistoryCard, BenchmarkChartCard, benchmark page, evaluate page,
  benchmark-controller; tsc --noEmit clean; eslint 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings).
- Full web suite run for regressions.

Known / handed off

  fails. PROVEN PRE-EXISTING: fails identically at HEAD with my server_state.py change
  removed (exit=1 both ways), and the test mocks get_server_state entirely.
- health_flow throughput bands flip CRITICAL -> OK as input goes ~2 -> ~10.7 (intended).
- OPEN: streamSse hang-guard (http-client.ts:1288) still not approved.
- OPEN: 248-tok system_extra trim ordering.
- WARNING for the other session: these 14 files are uncommitted relative to
  feat/design-system-tables, so their next commit would sweep them in.

FINAL STATE (branch fix/tps-measurement, tip 2281af0be, 4 commits, 15 files)
  f40f5f07f  main fix (14 files)
  04cf85d7c  restore the stream-capture edits
  4825d318b  TestDecodeWindowForwarding (2 tests)

LIVE BEFORE-PROOF
  GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/benchmark/metrics -> HTTP 500
  {"code":"E_SERIALIZATION"} after 41.0s, with a model resident
  (Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct). This is root cause A reproduced against the
  running production server, not just a code read. The other session's server
  was only ever read from (GET), never restarted or disturbed.

PARTIAL-REVERT INCIDENT (why there are 4 commits)
  A concurrent branch switch by the other session reverted 6 of my files back
  to HEAD mid-task, and hit inference.py BETWEEN two edit batches — so the
  commit had the decode_ms plumbing (init + both sinks) but not the four edits
  that actually capture and compute the window. decode_ms would have been

  `git show branch:path`, never against the worktree.

HOT-LOOP COST: zero added clock reads. The first-token read is stored in

  already existed for _token_gen_start and is reused for _last_token_at.

VERIFICATION

    response_tracker, health router) + 2 new decode-forwarding tests.

title: workspace search: server-side q filtering, stop full-dump + client includes()
body:
PROBLEM
GET /workspaces/{id}/search (workspaces.py:1235, route :1531) accepts NO query param despite its name: it returns every member, training job, dataset and knowledge fact (datasets branch even lists ALL workspaces' datasets, no scoping). The web page (apps/web/app/(app)/workspace/data/search/page.tsx) fetches that full dump on every keystroke (300ms debounce) and does title/detail includes() client-side. Search semantics split across layers: frontend has its own query engine; API is a firehose.

INVARIANT
Query semantics live with the data. The UI renders answers; it does not re-implement matching. Every other search endpoint in the codebase already follows this (/files/search, /datasets/search, /kb/search, /vector/search, /memory/search all take q server-side).

PLAN (agreed with user)
1. Backend: add q: str = "" and limit: int = 50 to search_workspace; filter each section server-side with a shared case-insensitive helper; scope datasets to the workspace; flag partial results instead of masking failures in try/except; return {results, total, query}.
2. Frontend: pass ?q= through existing apiGet (http-client.ts contract kept); delete the client-side includes() loop; keep debounce.
3. Tests: extend apps/api/server/tests/test_workspaces_router.py (~:460) for ?q filtering, empty q, workspace scoping, auth.
4. Lint + typecheck + pytest.

SCOPE GUARD
- No new search abstraction/service — conform this endpoint to the existing q convention only.
- Rendering/grouping/icons/navigation stay in the frontend (legitimate presentation).
- Do not touch other search endpoints.

SHARED WORKSPACE
- index updated: n/a (no new app/package/doc)
- shared copy reused: root .venv + node_modules, no installs
- coordination named: none found owning this endpoint

title: L2: SubprocessProcess start method fork -> forkserver (kill BLAS fork-deadlock class)
body:
Background: card 20260928_075 full-suite hang root-caused 2026-09-28..10-01: (1) leaked daemon pretrain threads doing BLAS compute -> os.fork() deadlock in SubprocessProcess.start(); (2) TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow unbounded follow loop; (3) test_tracking import-patch self-recursion. L1 fixed (1) via dedupe + stop_pretrain + cooperative cancel + conftest teardown (branch fix/pretrain-thread-leak). L2 = remove the whole fork hazard class: forkserver start method. Review SubprocessProcess.start in domain/shell (or core) before implementing; platform-gate to Linux; verify children still inherit needed fds/state or explicitly pass them.

## Live evidence from gate run7 (2026-10-02)

60 children of the pytest process spawned by a leaked pugqeep engine each got
the parent cmdline (fork preserves argv) and ALL deadlocked in futex_do_wait —
fork-into-multithreaded-pytest reproduced at scale, exactly the hazard this
card removes (fork -> forkserver). Batch pattern: every 180s, 1-7 per batch,
20:11->21:08; main thread then blocked 9h in waitpid at exit. Also worth
noting SubprocessProcess.monitor() still waits with no timeout.

---

## LANDED EVIDENCE (2026-10-11, foreman)

LANDED: 851b19fa5 on branch feat/forkserver-start-method (worktree .wt-modular), parent 1eb96c08a. NOT merged to main — main is 371/212 commits diverged and does not contain packages/core-py/domains/infrastructure/pugqeep/ at all, so this is a branch-line landing.

WHAT LANDED (4 files, +330/-106)

1. engine.py — _subprocess_worker lifted from a closure nested inside start() to module level. forkserver/spawn must pickle the target, and a local function raised "AttributeError: Can't get local object 'SubprocessProcess.start.<locals>._worker'". Body moved verbatim; only self.config->config, self.proc->proc.
2. engine.py — Process.__getstate__/__setstate__ null the two threading.Event fields (_thread.lock is never picklable) and rebuild them fresh on the far side. They are parent-side synchronisation only; the child reads fn/args/kwargs. Pickling never mutates the live object.
3. config.py — SubprocessConfig.start_method default "fork" -> "forkserver", plus the "or 'fork'" fallback in start().
4. engine.py — _require_picklable_target() preflight. An unpicklable fn used to fail SILENTLY: start() raised, the proc never ran, engine.wait() timed out, and it was reported CANCELLED with the real cause discarded — the exact silent-failure shape this subsystem exists to avoid. It now raises TypeError before spawning and names start_method='fork' as the opt-out, which stays supported because fork inherits memory instead of pickling.

CORRECTION TO THE CARD'S EARLIER PORT-DON'T-REBUILD NOTE

That note (options A/B/C, "DECISION NEEDED") describes branch fix/db-pool-root-and-download-progress, which carries 18c720be5 "pugqeep: replace multiprocessing with an owned fork + framed channel" (raw os.fork + socketpair frames). Verified: 18c720be5 is NOT an ancestor of this branch, and NOT in main or origin/main. On THIS branch the pugqeep package contains zero os.fork() — SubprocessProcess.start() uses multiprocessing.get_context(start_method) at engine.py:728 — and there is no GuardPool class, only GuardTree. So the card's literal request was exactly satisfiable on this line and has been satisfied; the A/B/C architecture decision does not apply here.

GATES (packages/core-py/tests/test_pugqeep*.py, 20 files)

- With change: 21 failed / 1735 passed.
- Baseline (change reverted): 21 failed / 1727 passed.
- Identical failure set; all 21 pre-existing: 13 test_pugqeep_checkpoint.py (model/points loading, environmental), 6 test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py (timing-sensitive: wait_for_timeout, group_elapsed, health_snapshot, guard_tree_health, cancel_manager_deregister, group_no_engine_raises), 1 test_pugqeep_engine.py::test_wait_for_timeout, 1 test_pugqeep_enums.py::test_stream_results_returns_copy. The two that could plausibly have interacted with the change were re-verified at baseline and fail there too. +8 = the 8 new tests. ruff + py_compile clean.
- The card's acceptance names the FULL packages/core-py/tests gate. That was not re-run: blast radius was proven zero outside pugqeep by grep (no guarded=True, run_subprocess, subprocess=True, or SubprocessProcess user in any other pugqeep test file), and the broader core-py suite carries pre-existing failures on this campaign line unrelated to this change.

LATENCY (card acceptance: no latency-benchmark regression)

- Steady state at load ~5, median per child start: fork 3.4 ms -> forkserver 21.4 ms (+18 ms, 6.2x). spawn 115.5 ms, rejected as too costly.
- The earlier 1 GiB / 344 ms figure does NOT transfer: SubprocessProcess children need only proc + config, not the parent's full address space.
- Production reach is zero today: guarded=True and run_subprocess have no production callers, and the server's startup jobs branch through a plain Tree, so no user-facing path changes.

KNOWN CHARACTERISTIC (deliberately not papered over)

Subprocess tests are more load-sensitive under forkserver. At loadavg ~34, four TestSubprocessCwdAndCapture tests raced engine.wait(timeout=5) and went CANCELLED; stable 6/6 at load 2-5. The timeouts were left unchanged rather than raised, so the characteristic stays visible.

TESTS BEYOND THE ADDITIONS

8 new tests (Process pickling, fresh-event isolation, each start method, the new default, the fail-fast TypeError, and the fork opt-in proving closures still work there). 6 existing tests had their fn moved from a nested closure to module-level helpers (_get_cwd, _get_env, _print_something, _return_ok, plus reuse of _add) — they cover cwd/env/capture, not closure support. Two config-default assertions updated to "forkserver": test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py::TestConfigEdgeCases::test_subprocess_config_defaults and test_pugqeep_config.py::test_defaults.

title: feat: system-wide general search — Searchable protocol, adapters, GET /search, Cmd+K palette (phase 2)
body:
Phase 2, approved after house-cleanup (card 7796fc2c) and server-side-q fix (card c185374a). Build order: cleanup lands first, then this.

APPROVED PLAN (expert review in session)
1. domain/search/: SearchHit(id, store, title, detail, score, locator), Searchable Protocol (capability: live|indexed), SearchRegistry, SearchService — concurrent fan-out, per-store timeout + per-store limit, visibility filtering AT the aggregator before results leave, returns {hits, partial}.
2. File-backed adapters: mtime-keyed substring index over docs/, ~/.config/dev-notes/, .kanban/board.jsonl — file:line locators.
3. API adapters: members, training jobs, datasets, knowledge, files, kb, chat sessions, memory. Each adapter validated by ONE shared contract test suite (q respected, limit honored, well-formed hits, failure => partial) — that suite is what makes stores provably uniform.
4. GET /search?q=&scope=&limit= — q required (convention), workspace-scoped permissions server-side.
5. Frontend: Cmd+K command palette (keyboard-first, grouped, jump-to via locator) + existing search page switches to the same endpoint. Reuses workspace-search components.
6. TDD: contract suite first, then adapters, endpoint, palette.

SCOPE GUARD
- Do NOT migrate the 8 legacy /search endpoints (keep contracts; opportunistic later).
- Do NOT build a mega-index / fold stores into one DB.
- v1 excludes git history, terminal history, source-symbol indexing (LSP-scale).
- List-page in-memory filters stay (documented as legitimate in cleanup card 7796fc2c).
- Open sub-item: docstore data contract (schemaless docs -> validated title/content/tags shape) — decide during adapter design for docstore.

SHARED WORKSPACE
- index updated: domain/search is a new module inside existing package (no new app/package; register in docs/INDEX.md if a doc is added)
- shared copy reused: root .venv + node_modules
- coordination named: blocked by 7796fc2c (cleanup) and c185374a (server-side q)

title: Router/controller/engine conformance — grouped root-cause fixes
body:
PARENT CARD — groups 2026-10-01 findings by ROOT CAUSE so each class is fixed
once, not as scattered one-offs. Evidence pack lives in the dated re-run section
of docs/DOC_VS_CODE_GAP_AUDIT.md (branch docs/truth-up-2026-10-01).

DECISION (user, refined): the engine IS the controller. Shape
    [router + proxy]  ->  engine (controller inside)  ->  domain
The controller does not survive as a layer: its responsibility (moving and
serving data) is integrated into an engine "until it doesn't show up as a
controller standing alone in the logic". Proxy owns protocol shape (envelopes,
errors) and lives JOINED to the router. Controller logic moves into domain/<f>
behind the __init__ facade. apps/api/server/controllers/ is deleted when empty.

--- GROUP A: handler layer reaching past the engine ---
CORRECTED (supersedes earlier "13" and my "14"):
  routers/      11 files, 36 domain._internal import statements
  controllers/  4 files, 30 statements, 13 distinct modules
      models.py 12, datasets.py 8, feedback.py 5, health.py 5, config.py 0
  COMBINED: 66 statements across 15 files
  worst: domain.models._internal.provider x9, domain.training._internal.cache_tags x7
Playbook only forbids _internal in ROUTERS, so its rules never covered the 30
in controllers/. The executable check must span BOTH directories.
False positives if you grep the token: tokenizer.py:6 and cloud_training.py:4
mention _internal only in a docstring asserting they do NOT import it — parse
imports, do not grep.
Excluded (concurrent refactor zone owned by another session): shell, vm,
world_render. Also out of scope: api_keys (router deliberately unmounted) and
the 6 domain-free infra routers (images, docstore, security, ratelimit, config)
— they have no engine to join until one is created.

Facades that already exist (one-line import swap):
  agents     domain.agents._internal.system          -> get_agent_system
  memory     domain.memory._internal.service         -> get_memory_service
  lora_eval  domain.feedback._internal.per_user_lora -> get_per_user_lora
  tools      domain.models._internal.provider        -> get_provider
  files      domain.cognition._internal.rag_service  -> get_rag_service
Facades to create first:
  agents      domain.api._internal.sse_envelope   (domain/api exports NONE)
  registry    domain.infrastructure._internal (artifact_registry)
  self_train  domain.infrastructure._internal.errors
  model_stack domain.training._internal.cache_tags

--- GROUP B: undocumented controllers layer (2,892 lines / 94 defs) ---
No architecture doc mentions controllers/ at all (grep across
PRODUCT_ENGINEERING, PYTHON_FIRST, STRUCTURE, routers.md = no matches).
None is a pass-through, so the fix is ABSORPTION, not deletion:
  config 43 lines / 4 defs / 0 domain imports -> candidate for plain deletion
  feedback 341 -> conversation CRUD + record_feedback(67) + _wire_model
  datasets 661 -> list_datasets(129 lines/84 branches), stats, preview, versions
  health 763 -> read-only aggregation of 12 domain sources (engine-shaped already)
  models 1067 -> model lifecycle: _load_hf_model(146), load_model_path(112),
                 unload_model(91), device + process-guard management
REFactor scope: test_{health,models,config,datasets}_controller.py patch
controller symbols — per Playbook rule 8 they must be re-pointed to the facade
when the logic moves, or the refactor breaks them.

--- GROUP C: conformance rule written but never enforced ---
Playbook checklist `grep -c _internal <router>` = 0 is prose, not CI; that is
how the claim drifted from "only shell/vm" to 11 routers + 4 controllers.
Must parse imports (no docstring false positives) and cover controllers/.

--- GROUP D: doc claim-rot (8 claims disproven by code) — DONE on
docs/truth-up-2026-10-01: ROADMAP g7/g8/g10, PRODUCT_ENGINEERING rows 15/16 +
Build Order 4, USER_JOURNEYS results path, this audit's own stale table.

--- GROUP E: performance reporter broken ---
  benchmark_results.py history --kind latency CRASHES: do_history's generic
    else-branch assumes metrics is a dict (m.get('mean_ms')), but
    latency/served_2026-09-24...json carries a LIST of compression results.
  Root cause 1: collect_records() globs the directory and never validates the
    file's own `kind` field — a mislabeled write poisons the store forever.
  Root cause 2: only the `training` branch normalises list-vs-dict; startup
    and execution fall into the same else and render mean=? because their keys
    are time_to_health_s / dispatch_us, not mean_ms.
  training: 0 recorded runs although ROADMAP g16 names it the release gate.
  NOTE: 3 test files import this script — do not edit while a suite is running.

ACCEPTANCE
  1. conformance pytest green, spanning routers/ AND controllers/, parsing
     imports, allowlisting only shell/vm/world_render
  2. controllers/ deleted; proxy joined to router; 4 controller tests
     re-pointed at the facade
  3. parity script still exit 0 at 703 routes (no HTTP contract change)
  4. benchmark_results history renders every kind; training baseline recorded
  5. benchmark_latency.py within 20% (revert otherwise)

--- GROUP F: duplicate code, no single home (2026-10-01) ---
Same root-cause class as Group B: code lives in more than one place because no
rule says where it belongs.
  domain/cognition  23 py / 77 refs  <- the live one
  domain/core       15 py / 20 refs  <- CCGT home, holds duplicates
  domain/cognitive  10 py /  1 refs  <- stray clone, NOT the port target
10 files byte-identical between cognition/_internal and core/_internal
  (10 identical, 0 differing, 12 only-in-cognition). cognitive holds a 9-file
  copy of the same set. One copy = 167,376 B; three copies = 502,128 B;
  redundant = 334,752 B (327 KiB). Only __init__.py differs per package.
  These are literal copies, not re-exports - a fix must be applied 3x with
  nothing enforcing it.
CCGT state: training(380 refs) + cognition live; domain/gateway/ DOES NOT
  EXIST (only apps/gateway edge relay); legacy packages/core-py/domains still
  has 268 py / 36 subpkgs, reached by 45 star-shims in domain/.
Remedy already on file in ROADMAP: one home, others import it, old files
  deleted - no deprecated shims.

COORDINATION FLAG: another session has STAGED a facade refactor over 12
routers - 7 of which are my Group A targets (agents, files, lora_eval,
model_stack, registry, self_train, tools). Their staged routers import 14
names that do NOT resolve at runtime because the matching domain/<f>/__init__
exports were never staged. Work overlaps mine; do not start Group A until
theirs lands or is called off.

title: L3: test teardown stops infra threads (idle-manager / faf-pool / feedback workflow schedulers)
body:
Sources: domain/infrastructure/_internal/idle_manager.py:199 (loop), fire_and_forget.py:54 (pool), domain/feedback/_internal/workflow.py:855 scheduler_loop + :874 background_training_loop (flag+time.sleep exit => up to 30-300s lag; switch to threading.Event wait, stop() sets event, stop_all_workflows() registry + join(2)). fire_and_forget: add reset_pool() (shutdown + _pool=None). conftest: autouse teardown (sys.modules-guarded like _stop_pretrain_threads). RED first: thread-death within 2s after teardown, fresh pool after reset, no idle-manager thread after reset. Follow-up candidates: pugqeep process-monitor, model_health/online_train one-shot threads.

## Gate run7 verdict (2026-10-02)

- Suite completes 2:07:45; 594F/41575P/141E — per-file failure parity with run5
  (99/82/62/7/6 all equal); 141E = playwright env cluster (own card).
- TDD red->green delivered: Event-based prompt stop (workflow, idle_manager),
  stop_all_workflows registry, reset_pool(), autouse conftest teardown.
- Run7 exposed two gaps, both fixed:
  1. Orphan IdleManager instances (test_idle_manager: 58 register vs 13
     shutdown) leaked 5+ threads past the fixture -> weak instance registry +
     stop_all_idle_managers() (0177c25ef).
  2. Leaked pugqeep engine respawned 60 fork-deadlocked children in a 180s
     storm (20:11-21:08); pytest then hung 9h at exit in waitpid on the
     unreaped children (needed manual abort; coredump nearly filled disk)
     -> Engine/ProcessMonitor weak registries + stop_all_pugqeep() (b9f66eab0).
- pytest-timeout failures roughly unchanged (12->14): the remaining timeouts
  are slow e2e benchmarks (quantization/perplexity >180s), not thread leaks.
- Gate #8 (l3-full-suite8.log) validates the two follow-up fixes.

DONE 2026-10-15 (foreman, review→done — note-first): landed on origin/main as aabe3dd09 (10-01, in trunk tip ff1cc48a8; not on integration-sync). Implements the card's plan exactly: workflow Event-based stop + started-workflow registry + stop_all_workflows(); idle_manager event _check_loop (shutdown wakes the sleeper); fire_and_forget reset_pool(); conftest autouse _stop_infra_threads at line 55 (sys.modules-guarded, L1-style). GATES re-run at ff1cc48a8: packages/core-py/tests/test_infra_thread_teardown.py 8/8 passed in 3.12s (grew from the original 6 red→green); ruff check + format clean on all 5 touched files. Cross-check: main-tree lane + integration-sync do NOT contain aabe3dd09 — their conftest lacks the autouse hook (main-tree grep: threading.Event absent in workflow.py) → the teardown benefit lands with trunk merges, folded into the integration-sync-home decision.

title: Session compaction prompt override: tighter, workflow-aware summary (no Relevant Files)
body:
Stock OpenCode compaction template is wordy: 6 sections, mandatory '(none)' scaffolding, plus a 'Relevant Files' inventory.

Added .opencode/plugins/compaction-tight.ts using the experimental.session.compacting hook (full prompt replacement, fail-open) with our SOP fields: Card / Branch / Journey / Gates, max 4 one-line bullets per section, no file-inventory section.

Mechanism notes: setting output.prompt replaces the built-in prompt wholesale (context only appends, so it cannot drop a section). A prompt override also suppresses OpenCode's built-in <prior-summary> embedding, so the plugin fetches the last completed compaction itself via client.message.list({order:desc}) so a second compaction still rolls forward. Hook callbacks are awaited by Plugin.trigger, so async is safe; any error leaves prompt unset and the stock prompt runs.

Typecheck: tsc --strict clean on the new file (existing plugins still show the pre-existing TS1360 satisfies-Plugin mismatch).

title: Native forward perf pass: built-in GEMV kernel replaces netlib BLAS (3.6x) — levers measured, 2 of 3 killed
body:
Follows card 1228d061 (Linux build port, commit 25cd0a369). Its own NEXT-FEATURE CANDIDATES listed two perf levers. MEASURED BOTH BEFORE BUILDING — the disciplined version of "continue building".

BASELINE (scripts/benchmark_native_transformer.py, -O3, warmup2/rep9 median, same box):
  tiny  (L2 D16 V512):   prefill 14789.5 tok/s, decode 8000.0 tok/s
  small (L6 D128 V4096): prefill   273.1 tok/s, decode  259.1 tok/s
  Earlier runs on a busier box read ~2x lower — cross-session numbers are NOT comparable, only same-session A/B is.

LEVER 2 — hoist the per-step malloc/free: KILLED BY MEASUREMENT.
  Actual count is 7 + 2*n_layers per token, NOT 7. forward_layer mallocs "normed" every
  layer (transformer_forward.c:133) and gqa_attention mallocs "scores" every layer (:89).
  small = 19 malloc + 19 free per token. At ~30ns each that is ~1.1us against a
  3860us/token budget = 0.03%. Not worth touching. Do NOT build it.

LEVER 1 — better GEMM/GEMV: partially live.
  All 8 call sites pass sgemm_t(M=1, ...) so these are GEMVs, never GEMMs. Microbench at our
  exact shapes (8 shapes x 6 layers + lm_head, 8.00 MB read/token):
      sgemm(M=1) [current]  1.00x
      cblas_sgemv           1.02x   <- switching primitive is WORTHLESS here
      plain dot loop        1.20x
      restrict + ivdep      1.17x
      restrict + unroll4    3.64x   <- THE WIN (4 independent accumulators)
  Reference netlib BLAS does not special-case M=1, which is why the hand-rolled 4-way
  accumulator beats it 3.64x. Current rate = 2.80 GB/s against 8 MB/token, so the ceiling
  from GEMM work alone is roughly 550-700 tok/s on "small".

LEVER 1b — OpenBLAS: BLOCKED, needs owner approval to unblock.
  No OpenBLAS/ATLAS/MKL on the system (ldconfig: only libblas.so.3).
  numpy/scipy DO bundle one but it is scipy_-prefixed (scipy_cblas_sgemm,
  scipy_cblas_sgemm64_) and a hashed private copy -> BOTH link probes FAILED.
  Getting a real OpenBLAS means an install, which the shared-workspace rule forbids
  without asking. ESTIMATED UPSIDE: 2-3x on decode. Owner call.

WHAT THIS CARD BUILDS: built-in GEMV kernel as the default on non-Apple, making the .so
dependency-free (no cblas.h, no -lblas dev symlink, no probing) — which also removes the
whole class of problem card 1228d061 had to probe around. External BLAS stays available as
an opt-in (SLO_BLAS=... plus -DSLO_HAVE_CBLAS) for anyone who has OpenBLAS. The change is
confined to sgemm_t; semantics preserved (C = A*B^T, alpha=1, beta=0, lda=ldb=K, ldc=N —

title: --mock-drift: scan monkeypatch.setattr + boom-vs-baseline probe (dead-seam class)
body:
CAPABILITY CANDIDATE for scripts/test-doctor.py --mock-drift. Found 2026-10-07 while walking the slow-marked test set. Not built — needs a go-ahead (it extends a shipped tool, so it is a change to production tooling rather than a test fix).

WHY: the detector answers ONE question — "does patching this target move the attribute the code reads?" That caught a real case today (test_infer_router patched domain.models._internal.provider.get_provider while infer.py does `from domain.models import get_provider`; the tool printed `fix: patch("domain.models.get_provider")` and exited 1, independently matching what I derived by hand).

But packages/core-py/tests/test_process_isolation.py died 8x with a defect that question cannot reach: the fixture's `monkeypatch.setattr(mw_mod, "_slo_worker_main", _fake_slo_worker_main)` patches the EXACT module production reads, so the binding moves and condition (1) is satisfied — but ProcessGuard's default flipped from SUBPROCESS to THREAD (b002cc789, an unrelated commit), so nothing ever routes through that symbol. A perfect patch aimed at a symbol that exists, on a seam production no longer uses.

THREE GAPS, in order of value:

1. SCAN monkeypatch.setattr too. --mock-drift only enumerates patch("string") targets, so this fixture's target was never a candidate at all. Both spellings are patching; the detector should see both.

2. BOOM-VS-BASELINE for suspects. Today a suspect that passes with the seam booby-trapped is "harmless". A suspect that FAILS THE SAME WAY with and without the boom is neither harmless nor confirmed — it is an unrelated failure sitting next to a dead seam. That case currently falls through both labels. Compare boom run against baseline run instead of classifying on pass/fail alone.

3. FAIL-FIRST TRIAGE for the slow set. Static drift analysis found 0 of the 11 failures in this file; the run itself named every seam worth checking. Cheapest useful step is to run the deselected set and let failures point.

DETECTOR IS NOT AT FAULT FOR MISSING #3 — it diagnoses bindings, and every binding involved was correct. This is a different question (call path, not binding) and deserves a separate answer rather than being folded into --mock-drift's exit code.

RELATED: card 33773fce-b (refactor-drift backlog, ~300 of 619 failures) — the failures above are the same species: tests reading a pre-refactor API. Evidence + analysis in ~/.config/dev-notes/2026-10-05-mock-target-shim-drift.md, Round 6.

LANDED (combined, card complete): external lane c1308c9c9 (string-form setattr scan 202 targets + blocking --dead-seam command + scripts/dead_seam_plugin.py + 46 tests, merged 32005e630) + mine a58e694ce (port of the two deltas that implementation punted): (1) alias/importlib object-form setattr resolution — _md_setattr_targets resolves import-as / from-import-as / importlib assignment / inline importlib; live 202 -> 305 targets, including the card's own motivating fixture model_worker._slo_worker_main via mw_mod alias (root's scan punts it 'by construction'); unresolvable aliases COUNTED. title: /training/export-text returns 200 with pairs_count always 0 — export never migrated to MogDB
body:
REPORT ONLY — found 2026-10-07. The AttributeError on this endpoint was fixed and committed (64820c3aa, user-approved): FeedbackController now defines feedback_dir = repo_root/"data", so /training/export-text returns 200 instead of 500. THIS card is about what the 200 now contains.

WHAT: the endpoint returns 200 with pairs_count: 0, always.

WHY: it reads repo_root/"data/feedback.jsonl". That file does not exist anywhere in the main tree — training/feeds.py:34 and domain/training/_internal/experience_adapter.py:71 point at the same path, but nothing writes it. So the endpoint is hollow-but-correct: no crash, no data.

THE MISMATCH: FeedbackController was migrated to MogDB — its own docstring says "instead of raw JSON/JSONL" — and record_feedback() stores exactly the three fields this endpoint filters on (user_message, assistant_response, quality) into a MogDB collection. The export endpoint was never migrated with it. It still reads a JSONL file that the new storage path stopped writing.

So the data exists; the reader points at the old medium.

FIX: read the collection instead of the file. Small, but it changes what the endpoint returns (0 -> real pairs), so it needs a call rather than a drive-by.

CONSEQUENCE IF IGNORED: the UI silently shows "no pairs to export" forever while pairs accumulate in MogDB. A zero that looks like a legitimate empty state is worse than an error — nothing fails, so nothing gets reported.

EVIDENCE: tests/test_feedback_system.py::test_export_training now asserts the real contract (file key, target_count) and passes with pairs_count 0. If the endpoint is migrated, that assertion may need to widen to accept a non-zero count.

RELATED: card e205b15c and db9c4e70 are the other two findings from the same slow-test march. Notes in ~/.config/dev-notes/2026-10-05-mock-target-shim-drift.md, Round 4.

1. Canonical folder = REPO-ROOT tests/ (literal single folder).
2. Diverged duplicate pairs = REPORT ONLY, do not merge yet.

=== KNOWN RISKS (from the repo's own docs) ===

  ancestor of the args. A root-level arg moves rootdir to the repo root and
  stops the inner ini applying -> mogdb/chargectl fall off sys.path and
  collection ABORTS. Both pytest.ini files exist to prevent this.

  from the repo root."

  duplicate-basename problem and can be revisited once deduped.

title: test isolation: test_files_router.py fixture wipes real uploads DB and data/uploads
body:
"DEFECT (destructive test fixture) — found 2026-10-08 while consolidating test roots.

FILE: tests/api-server/test_files_router.py  (was apps/api/server/tests/test_files_router.py)

The autouse fixture `_cleanup_uploads` targets the REAL stores on every teardown:

    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
    def _cleanup_uploads():
        yield
        db = _get_db()
        db.collection("files").delete_many({})          # wipes the ENTIRE uploads DB
        for f in _upload_dir.iterdir():
            if f.is_file(): f.unlink(missing_ok=True)   # deletes EVERY file in data/uploads/

WHY IT MATTERS
- `_upload_dir = FilesRouter().UPLOADS_DIR` -> repo data/uploads (real user files)
- `_get_db()` -> get_db("uploads_mogdb") -> the real uploads database
- It has run against live data repeatedly. Journal replay shows 537 metadata
  records destroyed in a single wipe: 536 were test debris rebuilt by prior runs,
  but 1791188358_nbaallelo_csv.csv (18,173,265 bytes) was a REAL user upload.
- data/uploads_json/files.json was reduced to 2 bytes.

EVIDENCE
- journal (append-only) preserves the insert at line 3498:
  {"op":"insert","data":{"file_id":"1791188358_nbaallelo_csv",
   "filename":"1791188358_nbaallelo_csv.csv","original_name":"nbaallelo.csv",
   "size_bytes":18173265,...}}
- wipe op at line 3611: {"op":"delete_many","data":{"query":{},"count":2}}
- original bytes survive intact at runs/downloads/nbaallelo.csv (exact size match)

ROOT CAUSE
Test isolation: the fixture clears shared mutable state instead of creating
private state. Compare with the repo convention of tmp_path/monkeypatch.

REQUIRED FIX (not applied — awaiting owner)
- monkeypatch FilesRouter.UPLOADS_DIR to tmp_path
- point the metadata store at a throwaway DB (e.g. tmp_path/uploads_mogdb)
- never call delete_many({}) or unlink() on a path outside tmp_path
- add a guard test asserting the fixture cannot reach data/

NOTE: user decision 2026-10-08 = report only, do not edit this file.
ALSO NOTE: user does NOT want nbaallelo restored under the app's mangled
`<ts>_nbaallelo_csv.csv` name — that naming/saving logic misses the format.
The original nbaallelo.csv is the only form wanted, and it is already intact.

--- RESOLVED (landed bd592b642, review):
Root cause verified live: module-level `_upload_dir = _router.UPLOADS_DIR` captured the REAL <repo>/data/uploads at import (SLO_DATA_DIR unset then), so teardown unlinked real files; the app-side instance (routers/files.py:444) wrote test bytes into the real dir too. The DB half was ALREADY isolated (root conftest SLO_DATA_DIR per-test + _POOL clear; _get_db resolves at call time) — teardown delete_many hit the tmp store.
Fix = house-pattern instance-patch (matches tests/server + tests/core-py): autouse fixture points the app-side FilesRouter (discovered via routers.files.router route endpoints) at per-test tmp_path/uploads; teardown now touches NOTHING (fresh tmp per test replaces the wipe). No product change.
Gates: ruff check+format clean; suite 14 passed x2 (9.6s/6.0s); real-state snapshots before/after x2 identical (data/uploads 0 files, uploads_mogdb 6 docs) — snapshot diff in ~/.cache/opencode/c130b2aa_{before,after1,after2}.txt."

title: db_pool _get_repo_root uses parents[5] — DBs written outside the repo
body:
PRODUCTION BUG (repo-root off-by-one) — found 2026-10-08, DBs land outside the repo.

FILE: apps/api/server/infrastructure/db_pool.py:24

    def _get_repo_root() -> Path:
        global _REPO_ROOT
        if _REPO_ROOT is None:
            _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]   # <-- off by one

DEPTH PROOF (file = apps/api/server/infrastructure/db_pool.py)
    parents[4] = .../sloughGPT        <- actual repo root
    parents[5] = .../Default Project  <- PARENT of the repo

CONSEQUENCE: split-brain between metadata and bytes
- db_pool writes every MogDB to   <repo-parent>/data/<db_name>
  (+ its _json sync dir, default <name>_mogdb -> <name>_json)
- FilesRouter.UPLOADS_DIR uses parents[4] correctly -> <repo>/data/uploads
=> file bytes in-repo, file metadata out-of-repo. Verified: the live uploads
   journal sits at Default Project/data/uploads_mogdb/files.journal.jsonl
   (1,046,912 bytes) while <repo>/data/uploads_mogdb/ holds a stale Oct-5 copy.
- 4 _mogdb dirs exist in the parent, 14 in the repo: two divergent data homes.

WHY NOT A ONE-LINE FIX
Flipping to parents[4] redirects every database to <repo>/data/, which makes the
app stop seeing the data currently in <repo-parent>/data/. That is a migration,
not a patch: needs a move plan + a backup + a decision about which tree is canonical.

DECISION (user, 2026-10-08): file as a card, do NOT change it in this branch.

SUGGESTED PATH
1. decide canonical data home (in-repo data/ is gitignored, so it is safe)
2. back up <repo-parent>/data/
3. change parents[5] -> parents[4]
4. move <repo-parent>/data/* to <repo>/data/ (no overwrites without backup)
5. verify GET /files lists pre-existing uploads afterward

title: Scoped checkpoint retention + shared file-handler utility (checkpoint_files, atomic_write)
body:
ROOT CAUSE: Resume on recovery_job_1fbc3f55 422s — models/auto-training/api_conversations_1790317725.soul no longer exists. _prune_stale_checkpoints (train_pipeline.py:2094) and _enforce_disk_limit (:2070) glob the SHARED models/auto-training dir directory-wide and keep only the N newest .soul files (or exactly 1 on a final save), so a later unrelated job's save deleted another job's checkpoints. Read side is job-scoped (_candidates_newest_first stem_prefix), delete side is not — resume ownership enforced on read, violated on write.

INVARIANT: one predicate must define a job's checkpoint files identically for write, read and delete.

SCOPE (approved): retention scoping ONLY — the recovery gate stays as-is (recovery_incompatibility unchanged).

BUILD:
1. domain/training/_internal/checkpoint_files.py — sanitize_stem(raw, cap=120), stem_for(data_path, soul_name), is_owned(path, stem), list_owned(dir, stem), is_in_progress(path). Composes soul_path()/soul_meta_path() for the suffix — never re-derives .soul (that grammar has one owner, slo_format.py:697, kanban card in review).
2. domain/infrastructure/_internal/atomic_write.py — single tmp->os.replace primitive. Ship the primitive, migrate ONLY save_checkpoint here; the other ~14 tmp->replace sites across 12 files become a separate follow-up card (packages/* cannot import domain/* — wrong dependency direction).
3. train_pipeline.py — save_checkpoint derives its stem via stem_for() instead of raw Path(data_path).parent.name (write/read divergence today: writer unsanitized, reader sanitized — dataset parent dir with a space yields a file the reader can never own); _prune_stale_checkpoints + _enforce_disk_limit use list_owned(); _candidates_newest_first delegates to list_owned() so read and delete cannot drift apart.
4. Replace all 7 copies of the stem sanitizer: router.py:245, distill.py:316, legacy.py:65, from_feedback.py:187, from_feedback.py:239, execution.py:58 (cap 80), execution.py:427.
5. Tests: new tests/core-py/test_checkpoint_files.py (sanitize idempotence/cap, is_owned boundaries stem_2 vs stemother, .tmp exclusion, writer/reader stem agreement for a dataset parent containing a space); cross-job shared-dir retention + keep_final scoped to own stem + disk-limit must not touch other stems in test_train_pipeline.py:1474-1501 (existing tests stay green).

MUST NOT CHANGE: single-job 5-newest / keep_final semantics for a dir holding only that job's files; resolve_resume_checkpoint 'never silently substitute a recorded path'; stored output_checkpoint_stem values (canonical cap 120 applies to NEW writes only).

NOT IN SCOPE: the recovery-eligibility gate; the 14-site atomic-save sweep.

No benchmark applicable — retention/IO-path logic, not a training or inference hot path.

Landing: current tree, no branch switch (main and feat/cave-game-vm have diverged over a dirty tree).

---

## STATUS 2026-10-08 — built, tested, linted (awaiting review)

**Shipped.** 4 new files: `domain/training/_internal/checkpoint_files.py` (158L —
`sanitize_stem`/`stem_for`/`is_owned`/`is_temp_artifact`/`list_owned`,
`STEM_MAX_LEN=120`), `domain/infrastructure/_internal/atomic_write.py` (145L —
`atomic_writer`/`atomic_write`/`is_temp_name`), `tests/core-py/test_checkpoint_files.py`
(236L), `tests/core-py/test_atomic_write.py` (112L). 10 files edited:
`train_pipeline.py`, `slo_format.py`, the 5 sanitizer call sites
(router/execution/legacy/distill/from_feedback), 2 existing test files, `docs/FEATURES.md`.

**Root cause fixed.** `_prune_stale_checkpoints` and `_enforce_disk_limit` globbed the
shared `checkpoint_dir` directory-wide; both now call `list_owned(dir, stem, suffixes=(".soul",))`.
Read side was already job-scoped — only the delete side was not. Single-job semantics
(5-newest / keep_final) untouched.

**Tests — 823 green, and the 4 new ones are proven to catch the bug.**
- 195 slo_format/checkpoints/soul_path/checkpoint_utils/training_checkpoint_export
- 53 new (checkpoint_files + atomic_write)
- 165 test_train_pipeline (161 pre-existing + 4 new cross-job retention)
- 149 recovery/job_store/training_queue
- 261 call-site modules + `test_shared_indexes` + contract tests
- **Discrimination check:** swapped `git show HEAD:` train_pipeline.py in, ran the 4 new
  tests → all 4 FAILED (job A's checkpoint eaten by job B's disk budget; final save sweeping
  the dir; raw `my dataset_….soul` filename), then restored and re-verified byte-identical.
- 6 `TestCheckpointPruning` fixtures updated: they build the trainer via `__new__` (no
  `data_path`), so under ownership scoping they owned nothing. Each now carries the `ckpt`
  identity its files are named with; `final.soul` → `ckpt_final.soul` so the keep-final
  survivor is owned too. Assertion intent (keep N newest / keep exactly 1 / meta cleanup)
  unchanged; class docstring records why.

**Lint/typecheck.** ruff clean on all 13 touched files (2 nits in new tests fixed). mypy:
**0 errors** in `atomic_write.py` and `checkpoint_files.py`; 41 across
`slo_format.py`/`train_pipeline.py` all pre-existing and outside my hunks (verified against
hunk ranges); repo-wide baseline is 668 errors / 81 files. The 5 API-server files: 32
pre-existing errors, none at the changed lines.

**Benchmark.** `scripts/benchmark_soul_paths.py` (the save_soul path bench): guards PASS,
exit 0 — sidecar 0.103ms (limit 10ms), detail 0.064ms (limit 50ms).
A/B at the `save_soul` level was **inconclusive for environmental reasons**: identical HEAD
code measured 0.70ms then 30.5ms within 3 minutes (PSI io `full avg10=23.7%`, load 6.07,
two other sessions running full gates + a live coredump), and an untouched read-path control
moved 0.128→0.241ms across the same window. Isolated interleaved primitive A/B
(3 runs × 60 pairs, both orders): **+0.005 / +0.038 (one 44ms stall hit its slot) / −0.002 ms**
→ no measurable overhead. Sequence is structurally equivalent to HEAD (same `mkstemp →
fdopen → write → rename/replace` in the target dir, still no fsync); no leftover temps in
any run.

**Docs.** `docs/FEATURES.md` §Checkpoint retention rewritten: per-run budget not per-directory,
names the single owner, and corrects the stale filename (`<dataset-stem>_<timestamp>.soul`,
not `<soul-name>.soul` — no code writes the latter). `docs/policies/CONTRIBUTING.md:30`
already documents the atomic-write contract correctly and remains true.

**Pre-existing failures attributed (not mine):** `tests/core-py/test_data_import.py` 26 failed —
two root causes, neither in my diff: (1) `git clone` exit 128 / no network → IndexError on empty
output; (2) `ISBNImporter._fetch_gutenberg_text() missing positional 'isbn'` test/impl drift.

**Follow-up filed:** card `f910f36d` — 20 `os.replace`/`os.rename` sites across 15 files still
hand-roll the dance (11 in `domain/*`, 9 in `packages/*`); `packages/*` cannot import `domain/*`,
so the layering answer must be decided before sweeping.

**Not done (scope decision):** `recovery_incompatibility` gate deliberately unchanged. The 3 job
rows pointing at deleted checkpoints stay unrecoverable — the UI Abandon button
(`DELETE /recovery/abandon/{job_id}`) clears them. Nothing committed; working tree only, on
`feat/cave-game-vm`.

---

## SWEEP RESULT (2026-10-08, 144-file broad run)

`pytest --timeout=120` over every training/checkpoint/soul/recovery/feedback/queue
test file: **4515 passed, 135 failed, 2 errors in 9m51s**.

**Attribution: set comparison against HEAD code, not a count.** Swapped
`train_pipeline.py` + `slo_format.py` to `git show HEAD:` in place, re-ran the same
13 failing files, restored and verified byte-identical. HEAD = **139 failed**,
mine = **135**. Diff of failing test-ID sets:
- only-with-mine: **1** — `test_computer_use_training_integration::test_follower_screenshot`
  (Playwright screenshot flake)
- only-with-HEAD: **5** — the browser group flakes in both directions
- **0 attributable regressions**

Root causes of the 135, all pre-existing, none in a file I touched:
- **61 browser/e2e** — `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED localhost:3000` (no dev server),
  `fixture 'route' not found`, one screenshot failure
- **52 `test_hf_lora_trainer`** — `ValueError: model_path is required` from
  `hf_lora_finetune.py:103` (validation added, tests not updated)
- **7 `test_update_from_feedback`** — `assert 'Reflective' == 'Analytical'` mode-mapping drift
- **5 `test_training_stream`** — `AttributeError: module 'domain.training' has no attribute
  'runtime_protocol'` (module attribute missing — likely an in-flight refactor elsewhere)
- **3 `test_slonet_legacy`** — `assert 0.1 == 0.0 ± 1.0e-12` LR-scheduler edge
- **2 `test_ewc_trainer_config`** — `assert 0.0003 == 0.001` / `assert 5 == 0` config defaults
- **5 misc** — priority_queue, feedback_dataclasses, souls_router, mobile_training, feedback_router
- (separately) **26 `test_data_import`** — `git clone` exit 128 (no network) → IndexError on
  empty output, and `ISBNImporter._fetch_gutenberg_text() missing positional 'isbn'`

Each of those is a concrete next-unit-of-work candidate: the `runtime_protocol` missing
attribute and the `hf_lora` `model_path` validation drift are the two that look like real
bugs rather than environment.

title: Atomic-save sweep: migrate remaining tmp→replace writes to atomic_write
body:

SHIPPED there: `domain/infrastructure/_internal/atomic_write.py`
(`atomic_writer` contextmanager / `atomic_write`) and exactly ONE migration —
`slo_format.save_soul` (the checkpoint write path), both the meta-sidecar write
and the main payload write.

NOT in scope there, deliberately: the rest of the repo still does the hand-rolled
`tmp = ...; f = open(tmp); ...; os.replace(tmp, dst); except: os.unlink(tmp)`
dance. Ship-the-primitive-then-sweep.

CENSUS (git grep os.replace|os.rename, worktrees excluded) — 20 sites / 15 files:

domain/* (CAN import domain.infrastructure._internal.atomic_write — the easy half):
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/hf_hub.py (3)
  domain/training/_internal/slonet.py (2)
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/training_pipeline.py (2)
  domain/shell/_internal/storage_device.py (1)
  domain/memory/_internal/memory_card.py (1)
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/repository.py (1)
  domain/inference/_internal/slo_embedder.py (1)

packages/* (CANNOT import domain/* — layering goes the other way, this is the
  actual design question the card has to answer first):
  packages/downcraft/downcraft/download/http.py (2)
  packages/downcraft/downcraft/download/state.py (1)
  packages/core-py/domains/shell/cmds/linux.py (1)
  packages/chargectl/src/chargectl/policy.py (1)
  packages/chargectl/src/chargectl/daemon.py (1)
  packages/avion/src/avion/ai/skills.py (1)
  packages/app-planner/src/app_planner/store.py (1)
  packages/app-planner/src/app_planner/slot_chain.py (1)

OPTIONS for packages/*, decide before touching anything:
  a) move `atomic_write` down into a package both layers can import (breaks the
     "domain owns its infrastructure" read — needs an ADR),
  b) leave packages/* on their local copies (they are stable, and 8 files x 1 copy
     is cheap) — sweep domain/* only, and record b as the decision,
  c) duplicate the primitive per-package (rejected: this card exists to stop
     copying save logic).

DO FIRST: pick (a)/(b)/(c). Then sweep domain/* mechanically, one commit per file,
each guarded by the existing tests (tests/core-py/test_atomic_write.py is the
behaviour contract: temp beside target, original preserved on body raise, no
partial file, temp unlinked on failure).

ACCEPTANCE:
- `grep -rn "os.replace(" domain/` either shows atomic_write.py or a reviewed
  exception with a comment naming why not.
- No behaviour change: every migrated site must still leave the original file
  intact when the body raises.
- ruff + mypy clean on each touched file (mypy baseline: 668 pre-existing errors
  repo-wide, 0 in atomic_write.py).

---

## domain/* HALF — DONE (2026-10-08)

7 of the 11 domain sites migrated; the other 4 are now REVIEWED EXCEPTIONS with
a comment naming why not (the acceptance grep below passes).

MIGRATED (5 files / 7 sites):
  domain/memory/_internal/memory_card.py (1)            -> atomic_write (payload is a str)
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/repository.py (1)     -> atomic_writer (streamed json.dump; `import os` became unused and was dropped)
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/training_pipeline.py (2) -> atomic_writer; the hand-rolled `try/finally: tmp.unlink()` went away because the primitive owns cleanup
  domain/inference/_internal/slo_embedder.py (1)        -> atomic_writer, binary (struct writes; local `import tempfile` dropped)
  domain/training/_internal/slonet.py (2)               -> export_to_sou payload + save_checkpoint_npz

  Side effect worth knowing: save_checkpoint_npz now writes through a HANDLE, so
  numpy stops appending its own ".npz". The `x.tmp.npz` spelling disappears from
  production; the predicate still recognises it for files already on disk
  (tests/core-py/test_epochs.py and test_checkpoint_files.py still pin it).

REVIEWED EXCEPTIONS (comment added at each site — none of these is a temp-write):
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/hf_hub.py (3): marker rename
    (.incomplete -> .sgpart), reconciliation between two EXISTING partials
    (larger wins, smaller dropped), and promotion of a finished download to its
    final name. No bytes are written at any of them; atomic_writer writes bytes.
  domain/shell/_internal/storage_device.py (1): the rename(2) operation itself,
    exposed as the shell's filesystem API — the caller asked for a rename.

STILL OPEN (census above, unchanged): packages/* — 8 sites, blocked on picking
(a)/(b)/(c). Two more sites sit outside the original `os.replace|os.rename`
grep and are also not temp-writes: apps/api/server/routers/datasets.py:453
(shutil.move of an imported item into output_dir) and
scripts/migrate_planner.py:170 (one-off backup move).

NEW FINDING → FIXED (2026-10-08): slonet.export_to_sou wrote its `.meta.json`
sidecar with a plain `open()` — NOT atomic — while slo_format.save_soul (the
checkpoint path) writes that same sidecar through atomic_writer, so a crash
mid-sidecar left a truncated sidecar beside a valid .soul. Both writes in
export_to_sou now go through atomic_writer, pinned by
tests/core-py/test_slonet_wave_a.py::test_export_to_sou_sidecar_is_atomic
(fault injection: green on the new code, red when that one line is reverted).

EVIDENCE (2026-10-08, this session):
  - 1053 passed / 5 failed over every touched area plus the retention tests. The
    5 are pre-existing: 3 in test_slonet_legacy.py (reproduced by swapping HEAD's
    slonet.py back in) and 2 known EWC defaults (`assert 0.0003 == 0.001`) in
    packages/core-py/tests/test_epochs.py.
  - 2 tests pinned the old `os.rename` failure path and now pin `os.replace`
    (test_slonet_legacy.py::TestExportExceptionBranch, test_slonet_wave_a.py);
    both additionally assert the destination never appears when the replace
    fails — i.e. readers see no file rather than a truncated one.
  - ruff clean on every touched file. mypy on train_pipeline + slonet:
    124 errors at HEAD vs 124 with the change, identical message-for-message
    (0 new).


DECISION INPUT — packages/* (a)/(b)/(c): evidence gathered 2026-10-08, recommend (b)
  Layering measured, not assumed:
    - downcraft, chargectl, app-planner, avion, sdk-py, cli: 0 `import domain.*`
      each — the 6 leaf packages are clean today.
    - No import-linter config and no boundary contract test anywhere → layering is
      convention only, so (a) would not be "restoring" an existing edge, it would
      create the first one.
    - The 227 packages→domain hits are all packages/core-py/domains/** re-export
      shims; domain→core-py is 68 (`from domains import ...`). The trees are not
      strictly one-directional already, but the 6 leaves are.
    - The local copies are ADAPTED, not redundant:
        chargectl/policy.py::_atomic_write — fsync + chmod 0644 and SWALLOWS
          OSError so a read-only root can never kill the daemon;
        app_planner/store.py::_atomic_write — fires apply_board() after the
          replace (re-derive the slot chain on every board write).
        Our primitive raises instead of swallowing and has neither hook.
  → (b): leave the 6 leaf packages on their local copies. (a) would need the first
    packages→domain (or leaf→core-py) edge to share ~60 deliberately-different
    lines, and would turn atomic_write into a config kitchen-sink (fsync, mode,
    swallow_errors, on_after) serving a different failure model. The defect domain

title: Stale __pycache__ under tests/ — 849 pyc carry pre-move co_filename, 10 orphaned
body:
Found while root-causing the post-consolidation core-py run.

WHAT
tests/ contains 849 .pyc whose code.co_filename still points at the OLD
locations, and 10 orphaned .pyc with no source:
  - 849 stale: packages/core-py/tests/... , apps/cli/tests/...,
    apps/api/server/tests/...
  - 10 orphaned: e.g. tests/cli/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-312.pyc
    (from deleting tests/cli/__init__.py), plus test_probe_distill,
    test_dummy_polluter, test_zz_diag2/3

WHY IT PERSISTS
The consolidation moved files with `mv`, which preserves mtime AND size.
Python validates a .pyc by (source mtime, source size) recorded in its
header — both still match, so every moved pyc stays "valid" while embedding
the pre-move path.

HOW IT SHOWS UP
Tracebacks point at files that no longer exist and print ??? for source
lines, e.g.:
  packages/core-py/tests/test_cpu_topology.py:280: in test_numa_from_sysfs
    ???
  OSError: no lscpu
even though the test actually ran from tests/core-py/test_cpu_topology.py.

IMPACT
- Correctness: NONE. Bytecode was compiled from identical content, so the
  executed logic is right; only co_filename is stale. Files edited after the
  move got a new mtime and recompiled correctly (494 pyc already carry the
  current path).
- Debugging: real cost — stack frames resolve to nonexistent files.

FIX (not done)
Clear generated caches after all in-flight pytest runs finish:
  find tests -name __pycache__ -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} +
Regenerated automatically on next run. Deliberately deferred: 3 pytest
processes are active in this worktree right now, and deleting caches under
running interpreters is not safe.

Cleanup of the 10 orphaned pyc is cosmetic only — Python will not import a
package from __pycache__ without its source file, which is exactly why
removing tests/cli/__init__.py took effect immediately.DONE 2026-10-12 (no commit needed — fix is untracked-cache deletion only). Blocker cleared: the main tree's pytest runs had finished; the two live pytest processes were in .wt-chatfix (its own tests/ dir, outside the sweep path). Evidence: pre-sweep 7 __pycache__ dirs / 429 pyc under tests/ -> post-sweep 0 / 0; git ls-files showed 0 tracked files in the sweep path (nothing irreplaceable touched); regenerated one cache and read its header — fresh test_cpu_topology pyc co_filename = tests/core-py/test_cpu_topology.py, i.e. the current path, not the pre-move one. Tracebacks will now resolve to real files.

    result["timestamp"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")

correctly caught. Not covered by it.

title: fork-futex leak forensics (evidence for card 32914d93): 24 idle children, futex_do_wait, 2Gi swap
body:
Answers the /proc forensics step card 32914d93 left as its next action.
Observed 2026-10-08 ~08:12 on the shared worktree while another session ran a
full core-py gate (pid 93590, pytest tests/core-py/ -q --tb=line --timeout=600).

WHAT LEAKS
24 child processes, all with ppid=93590, all:
    stat=S   Threads=1   cputime=00:00:00   cpu=0.0%   mem=5.4% each
    wchan=futex_do_wait
    cmdline = identical to the parent pytest (inherited at fork)
They have NEVER executed (0 CPU time) and never will: they forked and then
blocked on an inherited futex. This is the card 075 mechanism, made visible.

SPAWN CADENCE (wave starts, seconds of etimes at observation)
    3044 x7 | 2443 x7 | 1843 x5 | 1243 | 643 | 43
=> a new child appears roughly every 600s, which is exactly --timeout=600.
Their log shows 11 "Timeout" banners, so each timeout leaves one more
futex-blocked orphan behind.

RESOURCE IMPACT (why concurrent runs in this worktree slow down)
    free: 23Gi total, 9.0Gi used, Swap 2.0Gi used of 3.8Gi
    load average 3.40 on 8 cores -> NOT CPU-bound; it is process + swap
    pressure. Each child holds a COW copy of the parent heap (5.4% each).

WHERE IT COMES FROM
    grep -rln "os.fork()" tests/core-py/ --include="test_*.py"
      -> tests/core-py/test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py   (ONLY such file)

REPRO / NON-REPRO
- isolated: pytest tests/core-py/test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py
  -> 175 passed in 48s, exit 0. Matches the card "file-alone + pair runs pass".
- full group: the leak appears. So the fork deadlocks only when the parent is
  concurrently busy or killed, not when it runs alone.

CAUTION
Do NOT kill these children to clean up: they belong to another sessions live
run, and killing them would corrupt that gate. Left untouched here.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION (for the card owner, not done here)
- make the forked child close or reinit inherited sync primitives after fork
  (atfork handler, or a bare exec), and/or
- reap children in the test teardown, and/or
- have pytest-timeout kill the process group, not just the test thread.

body:

full-suite run (card vq-huffm), and it is a DIFFERENT hanger from card
32914d93 (which blames test_pugqeep_process_mgmt / fork futex).

SYMPTOM
  Chunk C3 (tests/core-py/test_[o-w]*) hit the shell timeout: exit=124 at
  timeout 3000, only 41% rendered, no pytest summary line. -q mode means the
  failure summary is only written at exit, so that whole 50-minute run was
