  on exactly one test, no status emitted:

    tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py::TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow

  Had to SIGTERM it manually (exit=143).

ROOT CAUSE — an unguarded duplicate of a guarded test
  There are THREE test_logs_follow definitions in
  tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py:

    line  8330  class TestCmdLogsLevels      has_alarm=2   <- GUARDED, never hangs
    line 20305  class TestCmdLogsExplainV2   has_alarm=0   <- HANGS
    line 23086  class TestCmdLogsDeeperV2    has_alarm=0   <- calls "follow 1", bounded

  The guarded copy (8330) reads:

      # Follow mode has a while True loop - just test it doesn't crash on init
      def alarm_handler(signum, frame):
          raise KeyboardInterrupt()
      old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, alarm_handler)
      signal.alarm(1)
      try:
          repl._cmd_logs("-f")
      except KeyboardInterrupt:
          pass
      finally:
          signal.alarm(0)
          signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)

  The hanging copy (20305) has NO alarm, NO KeyboardInterrupt handler:

      def test_logs_follow(self, repl):
          repl._log_buffer.clear()
          _run_with_io(repl, [], lambda: repl._cmd_logs("-f"))
          assert repl._last_exit_code == 0

  Production side: domain/shell/_internal/repl.py
      2536: def _cmd_logs(self, args: str = "") -> None:
      2720:     while True:        <- the follow-mode loop

  So the test enters repl.py:2720's while True with a cleared log buffer and
  nothing ever breaks the loop. The 8330 copy breaks it with SIGALRM; 20305
  never can -> blocks forever.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH
  - file-alone and pair runs pass, because alphabetical/pytest ordering does
    not always reach this class before other work (same shape as 32914d93's
    "file-alone + pair runs pass").
  - -m "not slow" deselects slow tests but this is an infinite loop, not a
    slow test, so the marker never applies.

SUGGESTED FIX (NOT APPLIED — needs approval, file may be owned elsewhere)
  Mirror the 8330 guard into 20305: install a SIGALRM handler that raises
  KeyboardInterrupt, signal.alarm(1) around the _cmd_logs("-f") call, then
  always signal.alarm(0) + restore the previous handler in finally.
  Also review 23086 (TestCmdLogsDeeperV2) — unguarded too, though it passes
  "follow 1" which appears bounded; unverified whether it can hang.

WORKAROUND ALREADY IN USE (mine, no code change)
  Re-run that one file with a deselect so coverage completes:

    pytest tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py \
      --deselect tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py::TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow

PROCESS NOTE FOR FUTURE RUNS
  Switched all remaining chunks to verbose + PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 streaming.
  Verbose writes one line per test AS IT COMPLETES, so a killed run still
  yields every completed result (this is how 4149 results were salvaged from
  the killed C3b). With -q, a timeout discards everything — do not use -q for
  long chunks.

CLOSED (stale todo — fix AND closure already in root tip): the guard landed as 64c8c73f6 'fix(tests): guard TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow — the unguarded while-True duplicate' and the closure 462d7ee87 also reached root tip; only the board row was lost to a stale-base board merge, so it still read todo. LIVE PROOF at tip: the exact hanging test passes in 2.05s (EXIT 0, was 'blocks forever' + SIGTERM-only), and the whole TestCmdLogsExplainV2 class passes 2 in 2.05s under a 180s cap. File is clean (no foreign edits).

title: ORDER-DEPENDENT: importlib.reload in test_quantization_coverage.py breaks test_quantized_matmul (3 failures, reproduced in 2s)
body:
ORDER-DEPENDENT TEST ISOLATION DEFECT — reproduced on demand, not a product bug.

SYMPTOM (seen in chunk C3a of the full-suite run, card vq-huffm)
  tests/core-py/test_quantized_matmul.py:
      TestQuantine::test_init_symmetric
      TestQuantine::test_init_asymmetric
      TestQuantizeStateDict::test_returns_tensor_info

  The assertion is self-contradictory on its face:

    AssertionError: assert <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC: 'symmetric'> == <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC: 'symmetric'>
      +  where <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC> = <domain...quantization.Quantine object>._mode
      +  and   <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC> = QuantMode.SYMMETRIC

  Two visually identical enum members failing == means they are TWO DIFFERENT
  class objects — Python Enum does not define __eq__, so it is identity-based.

REPRODUCTION (2 seconds, deterministic)
  pytest tests/core-py/test_quantized_matmul.py -q
      -> 3 passed                       (passes alone)

  pytest tests/core-py/test_quantization_coverage.py \
         <the 3 tests above> -q
      -> 3 failed, 31 passed            (fails)

  So the failure depends entirely on test_quantization_coverage.py running first.

ROOT CAUSE
  tests/core-py/test_quantization_coverage.py calls importlib.reload():
      line 106:  importlib.reload(q)
      line 114:  importlib.reload(q)

  reload() re-executes the module in the EXISTING module object, which
  re-creates the QuantMode Enum class — a brand-new class object.

  Collection order (glob/locale order in tests/core-py/):
      5  test_quantization_coverage.py   <- reload() runs here
      9  test_quantized_matmul.py        <- holds the OLD QuantMode binding

  test_quantized_matmul.py binds QuantMode AT COLLECTION TIME (module-level
  import). The reload then swaps in a new QuantMode. When the matmul tests
  later construct a Quantine, engine._mode is a member of the NEW class while
  the test compares against the OLD class -> identity mismatch -> assert fails,
  even though both render as QuantMode.SYMMETRIC.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS
  - passes when the file runs alone (the usual local workflow)
  - only fails in a full-scope run, where files execute in collection order
  - the repr is identical on both sides, so the failure looks impossible

SUGGESTED FIXES (NOT APPLIED — needs approval)
  Preferred (fix the polluter): in test_quantization_coverage.py, make the
  reload harmless — either
    (a) capture module state and restore it in a fixture finalizer, or
    (b) reload inside a fixture that re-imports the names the other tests
        depend on, or
    (c) stop reloading entirely if the reload only exists to pick up a
        monkeypatched value — monkeypatch the attribute instead of the module.
  Alternative (defend the victim): have test_quantized_matmul.py resolve
  QuantMode lazily inside each test (module attr lookup at call time) instead
  of holding a module-level binding.

  Note: this is one instance of a wider pattern — the repo has 13 test files
  using importlib.reload / sys.modules[...] mutation. Any of them can cause
  the same class of order-dependent failure. A targeted sweep would be a
  separate, larger piece of work.

RELATED
  - The traceback for these failures shows a path that no longer exists
    (packages/core-py/tests/...) — that is a SEPARATE issue, stale .pyc with
    pre-move co_filename, card 9dba061c. Clearing bytecode does NOT fix this
    failure: verified by re-running with PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX set to a fresh
    directory (forces full recompilation) — the 3 tests still fail, while
    test_list_cached_models_includes_local_cache still fails for the unrelated
    reason that the Qwen model.slnc is absent from ~/.cache/huggingface.

title: HANG: test_vector_backend fork-futex deadlocks in-suite (passes alone, 20 passed/3.3s) - fork from multi-threaded pytest, killed C3f chunk
body:
SECOND FORK-FUTEX HANG (family of card 32914d93), this time in
tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py. It killed chunk C3f of the full-suite
run (card vq-huffm); 48 of its 61 files had to be re-run separately.

SYMPTOM
  Chunk C3f (tests/core-py/test_[u-w]*) froze. Output stopped after:

    tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py::TestVectorBESimpleOps::test_silu PASSED [  9%]

  Zero byte growth across repeated 12-25s samples. Only 13 of 61 files had
  completed (385 passed, 83 failed salvaged before the kill).

PROCESS TREE AT THE STALL (the decisive evidence)
    549915  timeout 3000 python -m pytest ...
      549916  MAIN pytest          state=S  5.8% CPU  wchan=do_wait
        559953 FORKED child        state=S  0.0% CPU  wchan=futex_do_wait  age 1895s
        559889 multiprocessing resource_tracker  wchan=anon_pipe_read  age 1744s
        559954,559955,559956,559958  [python] <defunct>   <- 4 ZOMBIES

  The child at 559953 has an IDENTICAL argv to the parent — that is the
  signature of os.fork() (fork copies argv; an exec would not). It has been
  blocked on futex_do_wait with ZERO CPU time since it was created, and the
  parent is stuck in do_wait waiting for it. So the parent forked a worker,
  the worker deadlocked on an inherited futex, and the parent blocks forever.

ROOT CAUSE (fork from a multi-threaded process)
  Only one of the 13 completed files touches fork/multiprocessing at all:

    grep -cE 'os\.fork|multiprocessing|SharedMemory|Pool\(|Process\(' over the
    13 files -> test_vector_backend.py: 2, every other file: 0
    (test_user_journeys.py, which supplied 75 of the 83 failures, has 0)

  test_vector_backend.py's own docstring:
    """Tests for VectorBE compute backend with shared memory multiprocessing."""

  WHY IT PASSES ALONE BUT DEADLOCKS IN A RUN
    pytest tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py -q
      -> 20 passed, 1 warning in 3.30s, exit 0      (verified just now)

  The preceding u-range files (browser/dashboard journey tests) leave the
  pytest process MULTI-THREADED. POSIX fork() copies only the calling thread
  into the child, but it also copies every mutex — including mutexes currently
  held by the threads that were NOT copied. The child then waits on a lock
  whose owner does not exist there -> futex_do_wait forever. In isolation the
  process has no other threads, so the fork is safe and the file passes in 3s.

  This is the classic async-signal-safety hazard that pthread_atfork() exists
  to solve. It is the same mechanism as card 32914d93 (pugqeep fork futex),
  which also "passes file-alone and in pairs" — consistent with the
  thread-count-dependent nature of the bug.

IMPACT
  - killed a 61-file chunk; required SIGKILL of the tree (549915/549916/559953)
    and manual re-run of the remaining 48 files
  - leaves a multiprocessing resource_tracker wedged on anon_pipe_read and
    orphaned <defunct> children until the tree is killed
  - same class of leak observed in ANOTHER session's run: 24-31 idle children,
    all futex_do_wait / 0 CPU / ~5.4% mem each, spawning ~every 600s
    (see card 057cab05), which drove swap to 2.0-2.2Gi of 3.8Gi

SUGGESTED FIXES (NOT APPLIED — needs approval)
  1. Prefer a safe start method: use multiprocessing.get_context("spawn") or
     "forkserver" for the shared-memory pool instead of the default "fork".
     spawn never inherits locks — this removes the hazard outright.
  2. If fork is required, register a pthread_atfork handler that locks/unlocks
     a dedicated child-side lock, or ensure all worker threads are quiesced
     (joined) before forking.
  3. Belt-and-braces: in the test's teardown, reap children and shut down the
     pool so a wedged worker cannot outlive the test.

ALSO NOTE
  The remaining 48 u/v/w files were re-run WITHOUT test_vector_backend.py
  (it is already covered by its own passing isolated run). If the suite is
  ever run as one monolithic process, this file will hang again once the
  u-range has run before it.

CLOSED (stale todo — fix already landed): 9bb7ca159 'fix(infra): kill the two gate-wedge sources — chat_stream producer leak + fork-into-multithreaded pool' (card f1816d61) is in root tip; a74fcf364 already cross-referenced this card as fixed by that forkserver port. LIVE PROOF at tip: tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py 24 passed in 4.13s alone (EXIT 0), AND an in-suite probe of the exact original freeze window (chunk C3f = tests/core-py/test_[u-z]*, incl. vector_backend + vector_stores + vfs + video + video_trainer forking siblings) completed EXIT=0 under a 180s cap — no fork-futex hang.

title: PHANTOM collection errors: explicit file-list args flip sys.path[0] so 'from conftest import build_test_app' resolves to root conftest (8 router files; bare/dir run collects them, 115 pass)
body:
## Symptom

8 router test files collect-fail with `ImportError: cannot import name 'build_test_app' from 'conftest' (/home/mana/Documents/Default Project/sloughGPT/conftest.py)` — but ONLY when pytest is invoked with an explicit file list. A bare run or a directory argument collects all 8 and they pass.

Affected (all `tests/core-py/`): test_health_router, test_inference_router, test_kb_router, test_mobile_router, test_models_router, test_self_train_router, test_souls_router, test_system_router.

## Root cause (systematic)

`from conftest import build_test_app` is resolved through `sys.path`, and which `conftest.py` wins depends on what lands at `sys.path[0]`:

- `sys.path[0] = packages/core-py` (relative, from `pythonpath` in pytest.ini) -> `packages/core-py/conftest.py`, the SHIM that does `from tests.conftest import build_test_app` -> OK
- `sys.path[0] = <repo root>` (absolute, after root `conftest.py` runs its `sys.path.insert(0, repo_root)` / remove+insert block) -> root `conftest.py`, which has 0 hits for `build_test_app` -> ImportError

Reproduced with a debug plugin printing `sys.modules["conftest"].__file__` and `sys.path[:5]` at `pytest_collection_finish`:

- `pytest tests/` (directory arg) -> `conftest` = `packages/core-py/conftest.py` (shim) -> 0 errors
- `pytest tests/core-py/test_health_router.py` (file arg) -> `conftest` = root `conftest.py` -> ImportError
- `pytest tests/core-py/test_a*.py ... test_n*.py` (expanded glob = file list) -> same ImportError

So the deciding factor is the invocation shape, not the code. It is a latent landmine: any chunked/scoped run that passes files explicitly will report phantom collection errors that a canonical run does not.

Confirmed NOT a consolidation regression: at `dcb2a5eaf^` (pre-move) `build_test_app` was likewise absent from root `conftest.py`, `--import-mode=importlib` already existed, and the shim already existed. A bare full-tree collect at 04:18 (`final_collect.txt`) showed 0 such errors.

## Evidence

- 8 phantom events across the chunked run: C2_en=5, C3b2_left=1, C3d_rest_s=2
- Re-run through a directory arg + `-k` (`H_eight_files.txt`): **115 passed, 0 failed** -> the files themselves are green
- shim: `packages/core-py/conftest.py` = `from tests.conftest import build_test_app`
- root: `conftest.py` has no `build_test_app`

## Proposed fix (needs approval)

Make the import deterministic instead of `sys.path`-order dependent. Options, cheapest first:

1. Root `conftest.py` re-exports `build_test_app` (one line: `from tests.conftest import build_test_app  # noqa: F401`) so both winning resolutions succeed.
2. Or change the 8 test files to import from `tests.conftest` directly (package-qualified, immune to `sys.path[0]`).

Option 1 is the smallest blast radius and also un-breaks any other explicit-file invocation.

## Impact on accounting

These 8 events were subtracted from the full-suite totals as invocation artifacts (777 raw -> 769 real).

DONE 2026-10-13 (foreman verify): landing 549b3e58a ancestor of integration-sync + local lane; gate re-run on integration-sync @fa9ee4e8b — 11-file explicit list 152 passed / 0 collection errors, canonical 8-file list = 115 collected (matches card evidence); side-observation resolved (term_screen present via 23776c16a, test_shell_tui_live collects 42).

title: chat tests fail on production API-connectivity gate added 2026-09-13
body:
PROBLEM — 12 chat-test failures share one root cause: a production connectivity gate the tests never stub.

Scope: tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py, chunk C3g (81 failures total).
Signature split of C3g's 81: 28 `_interpret_natural` missing · 21 other assertion ·
15 init-None shutdown · **12 API-connectivity gated** · 2 event_bus · 2 ImportError · 1 other.
The 12 are one coherent bucket and had not been separated out before.

The 12:
  TestCmdChat::test_chat_no_args, ::test_chat_reset
  TestCmdChatExtra::test_chat_no_args, ::test_chat_reset, ::test_chat_success
  TestCmdChatExecution::test_chat_no_args, ::test_chat_reset, ::test_chat_new_session, ::test_chat_continues_session
  TestCmdChatDeeper::test_chat_no_args
  TestCmdChatDeeperV5::test_no_args, ::test_reset_session

ROOT CAUSE
`ShellREPL._require_api` (domain/shell/_internal/repl.py:4245) reads `self.os.api_status`;
when unavailable it prints "✗ API server is not connected. Use 'api start' to launch it.",
sets `self._last_exit_code = 1`, returns False. `_cmd_chat` consults it.

Three distinct failure modes:
  (a) test_chat_no_args — NO stub at all. Real gate runs -> exit code 1.
      Assert: `assert repl._last_exit_code == 0` -> `assert 1 == 0`.
  (b) test_chat_reset — gate fires before the local `/reset` mutation, so
      `_chat_session_id` stays "old". Assert: `assert 'old' is None`.
      FAILS ON STATE, not exit code. Relaxing the exit assert does NOT fix this.
  (c) test_chat_success — patches `_require_api` AND `_spinner_call`, but the send path
      has a SECOND connectivity check emitting "Error: Cannot connect to API server",
      so the patched `_spinner_call` is never reached. `_chat_history` stays length 1.

Contrast — two variants in the SAME run pass and prove both points:
  * TestCmdChatDeeperV2::test_chat_no_args PASSES because it uses the tolerant form:
        out = _run_with_io(repl, [], lambda: repl._cmd_chat(""))
        assert "Usage" in out or repl._last_exit_code == 1
  * test_chat_no_api PASSES because it patches `_require_api` directly.

CAUSAL TIMELINE (git archaeology)
  2026-07-30  e19f96190  chat tests first land (at the pre-move path)
  2026-09-13  68c427af5  "feat: add startup optimization suggestions" — 197 files,
                         +105,486 lines. Creates domain/shell/_internal/repl.py
                         (4,652 lines, all inserted) INCLUDING `_require_api`.
    git show 68c427af5^:.../repl.py | grep -c 'def _require_api'  ->  0
    git show 68c427af5:.../repl.py   | grep -c 'def _require_api'  ->  1
    That commit's --stat does NOT list test_shell_repl_more.py.
  => The gate arrived ~6 weeks AFTER the tests, and that commit did not adapt them.
     Not original test debt; introduced 2026-09-13.

NOT ANOTHER SESSION'S WIP
  git diff domain/shell/_internal/repl.py  ->  1 line, a comment typo
  (line ~330: "domains.logging" -> "domain.logging"). Nothing near
  `_require_api` (4245) or `_cmd_chat` (3317). Failures are against committed HEAD.

NO BASELINE AVAILABLE
  ~/.cache/sloughgpt-gate1/failures.txt (pre-move baseline, 2026-10-06 05:42)
  contains 0 entries for test_shell_repl_more. run6's testpaths never included it
  (gap math in ~/.cache/sloughgpt-gate1/FULL_SUITE_REPORT.md). So NEW-vs-pre-existing
  cannot be settled from run6 data — the git timeline above is the evidence instead.
  NOTE: a direct run at 68c427af5^ was NOT executed (shared worktree, branch must not
  be switched), so before/after execution is unproven; the timeline is inferential.

FIX OPTIONS
  1. PRODUCTION (recommended for a + b) — exempt local operations from the gate.
     Empty-args usage/help and `/reset` mutate only local state and should not require
     a live API. Printing "API server is not connected" instead of Usage for an empty
     argument is arguably a UX defect on its own.
  2. TEST (required for c) — stub the second connectivity check on the send path so
     the already-patched `_spinner_call` is actually reached.
  3. REJECTED — relax assertions to the TestCmdChatDeeperV2 style. Cannot fix (b),
     which fails on state (`_chat_session_id` still "old"), and it would mask whether
     `/reset` worked at all.

DECISION NEEDED
  Is (b) a product question? Should `/reset` clear local chat session state while
  disconnected? Recommended: yes, it is local state. Option 1 then fixes a + b
  behaviorally and option 2 covers c.

EVIDENCE
  ~/.cache/sloughgpt-gate1/suite/C3g_shell_repl_more.txt
    lines 1540-1543  FAILED markers
    lines 4217-4250  the three tracebacks with captured stdout
---
CLOSED 2026-10-12 by the health/agent-surface session — STALE CARD, already
fixed on origin/main. Fresh evidence, no code written:

  pytest packages/core-py/tests/test_shell_repl_more.py -k "chat_no_args or
  chat_reset or chat_success or chat_new_session or chat_continues_session or
  no_args or reset_session"
    -> 476 passed, 0 failed, 3638 deselected, at origin/main a01bc99b8

Root cause of the card's 12: ShellREPL._require_api read os.api_status and the
tests never stubbed it. That is gone — origin/main now stubs cmds.chat_stream
(not cmds.chat, which this path never calls) and asserts exit_code == 1, i.e.
it grew an independent answer to the same defect. 9d9512a91 (shell-repl green
series) IS in origin/main; the deeper d3c20f708 ("chat bypassed the IO
abstraction — 12 failures from 3 causes") is NOT, living only on
fix/journal-append-race, and is no longer needed for these 12.

TWO NOTES, and the distinction matters: this note title-matches the card and is
its backing note; 4c22d948 merely carries aab5df8b in its body and already read
done. Sync keys on the title match, so it kept reverting the card to todo while
the id-matched note sat green — the card is only now consistent because THIS
note moved first.

Process lesson: this session first measured "13 failed" and nearly port-picked
d3c20f708 on the strength of it. That count came from 99a16eae7, whose base
carries a different tree layout (tests/core-py/ vs packages/core-py/tests/) —
not current main. Red number manufactured by the measuring branch. Check the

title: quant_core: guard _LIB deref in _load_lib — missing .c/gcc became an import-time crash
body:
FOUND WHILE: cleanup-agent sweep (ruff + code-quality patterns) on 2026-10-09.

BUG: both quant_core wrapper copies deref _LIB unguarded at L222: _LIB.matmul_int8_select_kernel = getattr(_LIB, ...).

When the .c source is missing or gcc is unavailable, _build_one() returns False, ctypes.CDLL raises, has_int8=False and _LIB stays None (L207-209). L215 already guards with 'has_int8 and hasattr(_LIB, ...)'; L222 does not -> AttributeError at *import* time -> every importer gets a collection error instead of the intended numpy fallback.

REPRO (verified): monkeypatch _SRCS/_DYLIBS to /nonexistent, set _LIB=None, call _load_lib() -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'matmul_int8_select_kernel'.

FIX: wrapped L222-229 in 'if has_int8 and _LIB is not None:' + comment. L249 (_LIB.matmul_int4) already safe (inside try/except).

title: chat API gate moved to the sink: /reset, /status and bare chat work offline (aab5df8b)
body:
Card: aab5df8b-6e04-47b3-966b-43563f7c5f44
Commit: b2ba18527 (feat/caret-core)

## Problem

12 chat-test failures shared one root cause: `_require_api("chat")` sat
*before dispatch* in `_cmd_chat` (repl.py:3337), so a network precondition
gated subcommands that never touch the network. `/reset` and `/status` mutate
or read local session state only; bare `chat` enters a prompt loop.

## Fix (2 parts, both production)

1. Move the gate from the command entry into `_chat_send` — the only site
   doing HTTP, reached by both the direct path and `_cmd_chat_interactive`.
   Placed *before* the history append so the send path's output, history and
   exit code stay bit-for-bit unchanged.
2. Guard the empty-arg branch on `self.io.owns_stdin` (the declaration-not-
   probe seam `/logs -f` already uses at repl.py:2717): False -> print Usage,
   exit 0; True -> interactive mode as documented.

Part 2 was forced by measurement, not preference. `_cmd_chat_interactive`
reads with builtin `input()`, which raises `OSError: pytest: reading from
stdin while output is captured!` under capture, and the loop only catches
EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt. A gate-only change converted 5 assertion failures
into 5 errors and added 1 NEW failure (TestCmdChatDeeperV2 passed at baseline
on its `or exit == 1` disjunct).

## Behaviour deltas

- `chat /reset`  API down -> `[session cleared]`, exit 0 (was warning, exit 1)
- `chat /status` API down -> session info, exit 0 (was warning, exit 1)
- bare `chat`, no terminal -> Usage, exit 0 (was warning, exit 1)
- bare `chat`, real terminal -> unchanged (interactive)
- bare `chat`, TUI -> Usage (was raw input() across the curses screen)
- `chat <msg>` API down -> UNCHANGED: same warning, exit 1, history intact
- interactive mode: 278us per 20 messages of gating (was 14us/session)
- other 10 `_require_api` sites and `_cmd_ai` untouched

## Tests

3 approved one-line `repl.cmds = MagicMock()` stubs (test_chat_success,
test_chat_new_session, test_chat_continues_session) — those tests stubbed the
stale `_spinner_call`/`cmds.chat` collaborator while production streams via
`cmds.chat_stream`, so history came up short (`assert 1 == 2`). Pattern matches
the already-passing sibling `test_chat_with_response`; 33 existing uses in the
file. No assertion weakened.

## Verification

- red first: `12 failed in 3.37s`, all assertions for the right reason
- test_shell_repl_more.py: 81 -> 69 failed, 4025 -> 4037 passed
  set-diff vs recorded 81-id baseline: FIXED 12, **NEW 0**
- the 12 + DeeperV2: 13/13 passed
- test_repl_execute.py + test_api_provider.py: 51 passed (other _cmd_chat callers)
- scripts/benchmark_chat_dispatch.py (new) 3/3 rc=0 — exact probe counts:
  reset 0, status 0, usage 0, gate_down 1; gate 13.9us vs 2ms ceiling;
  probe is in-memory at 8.8us
- ruff + py_compile clean on all three files
---
CLOSED 2026-10-12 by the health/agent-surface session — STALE CARD, already fixed
on origin/main. Fresh evidence, no code written:

  pytest packages/core-py/tests/test_shell_repl_more.py -k "chat_no_args or
  chat_reset or chat_success or chat_new_session or chat_continues_session or
  no_args or reset_session"
    -> 476 passed, 0 failed, 3638 deselected, at origin/main a01bc99b8

That is byte-for-byte the sha the earlier closure commit 0374f327c claims to
have verified ("12/12 + file 4058 green at a01bc99b8") — so the closure was
real, the card simply never moved: this note already read status=done while the

Why it was still failing elsewhere: 9d9512a91 (the shell-repl green series) IS
in origin/main, but the deeper fix d3c20f708 ("chat bypassed the IO abstraction
-- 12 failures from 3 causes, not the 1 the card named") is NOT, living only on
fix/journal-append-race. It is no longer needed for these 12: origin/main

title: RAG: per-insert full BM25 rebuild over an unbounded singleton chunk list — latency grows without bound
body:
FOUND WHILE: cleanup-agent sweep 2026-10-09, root-causing a suite timeout.

SYMPTOM: tests/api-server/test_knowledge_router.py::test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates times out (120s). It POSTs 250 facts; each POST /knowledge costs ~1.3-1.8s -> ~325s total.

ROOT CAUSE (two compounding defects, both verified by cProfile):
(1) O(N) full index rebuild per single-document insert. ProductionRAG.add_document (domain/cognition/_internal/rag.py:616) chunks the doc, add_chunk()s each, then calls retriever.build_index() -> BM25Indexer.index(self.chunks) (rag.py:69), which re-tokenizes and rebuilds inverted_index/doc_freq/doc_lengths from scratch over ALL chunks. Measured: 42,759 _tokenize calls from rag.py:69 for ONE insert.
(2) The chunk list is unbounded for the life of the process. HybridRetriever.add_chunk (rag.py:193) only appends; there is no self.chunks = [] / .clear() anywhere in rag.py, and get_rag_service() is a process-lifetime singleton (rag_service.py:660) with no reset API. So chunks accumulate monotonically; the KB store cleanup clears entries.json but NOT the retriever chunk list, so the index keeps growing across tests and across a long-lived server.

The API already documents this trap: add_document(rebuild_index=False) + build_index() once at the end. rag_service uses that for bulk paths (rag_service.py:105,136,411) but the single-insert endpoint path uses the default rebuild_index=True.

IMPACT: unbounded memory growth + insert latency that grows linearly with corpus size, in a production server process.

PROPOSED FIX (needs approval, not applied — core algorithmic change in another lane's active worktree):
(a) Make indexing incremental: on add_chunk, append postings and update doc_freq/doc_lengths/num_docs incrementally instead of rebuilding. BM25Indexer.index() keeps its reset-and-rebuild path for the explicit bulk build_index() call.
(b) Add a bounded-growth guard / reset API on the retriever (e.g. retriever.clear()) and call it from the knowledge-store cleanup path so tests and purges actually reset the index.
(c) Have the single-document endpoint path batch: add with rebuild_index=False, then build once.

VERIFICATION AVAILABLE: rerun tests/api-server/test_knowledge_router.py::test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates with --timeout; expect 250 inserts well under timeout. Also benchmark scripts/benchmark_slonet.py is unrelated; a dedicated micro-bench of inserts/sec vs corpus size is the right measurement.

COORDINATION: repo worktree was concurrently mutated during this session (branch switched 06:10:32/06:10:43; commits 3d49ff923 and 465eecc8b landed mid-session). Carded rather than patched for that reason.

title: [DONE 2026-10-09] Guard DaitRuntime.shutdown() against an unbooted runtime (740ea0b26)
body:
Commit: 740ea0b26 (feat/caret-core)
Scope: second bucket of the test_shell_repl_more.py tail — 15 failures, one
root cause. (Previous: 65ca94433, the 28 `_interpret_natural` skips.)

## Root cause

`domain/shell/_internal/runtime.py:383` — `DaitRuntime.shutdown()`
dereferenced `self._init`, which is `None` from `__init__` (322) until
`boot()` populates it (343):

    AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shutdown'
    15 of 15 failures, zero other reasons

    TestCmdShutdown* 6, TestCmdExit*+ExportStateExitHistory 6,
    TestCmdBootShutdown* 3

The codebase already treats "not booted yet" as real in two places —
`status_summary` (423: `if self._boot_complete and self._init is not None`)
and `_cmd_svc` (4321: "Init system not booted yet. Run 'boot' first."). This
was the one path that forgot.

Latent rather than active: production calls `os.boot()` at repl.py:5207 before
the prompt. Still a crash on a user command, and all 15 assert the correct
contract (exit 0, `_running -> False`).

## Shipped in two iterations — first guard was wrong

Attempt 1 (ternary on the dereference) cleared the 15 but added a NEW
failure: it left `kernel.shutdown()` + `reset_device_system()` running on the
never-booted path, and both are module-level singletons, so they tore down
state this runtime never created and leaked that to every later test.
Full-file runs went 41 -> 27/29 with whoami NEW, 3 runs running.

Attempt 2 (shipped) returns before touching anything:

    if self._init is None:
        return ""

`boot()` is what creates the devices (344) and boots the kernel (354), so an
unbooted runtime has nothing to tear down. This also matches what the
crashing code did — it stopped dead, so nothing after it ran. The comment
records the leak, because the obvious defensive fix is the one that breaks.

## Verification

    pre-change 41 -> 26 failed;  4052 passed;  36 skipped; total 4114
    NEW vs pre-change: 0      cleared: 15

No benchmark covers this path (none of scripts/benchmark_*.py exercise

title: knowledge_store: every single add drops+rewrites ALL entries and visited hashes (second O(N^2), persistence layer)
body:
FOUND WHILE: measuring the RAG per-insert fix (card 4563be94). That fix landed and took POST /knowledge from ~1300-1800ms to 45-81ms, but test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates STILL times out — so a second O(N^2) remains, here in persistence.

DEFECT (domain/memory/_internal/knowledge_store.py): _save_entries() (L684) and _save_visited() (L664) do a full-table rewrite on EVERY single add:
  1. self._entries_col.drop()          <- drops the whole collection
  2. self._entries_col.insert_many(data) <- re-inserts EVERY entry
  3. ENTRIES_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(data))  <- rewrites the whole JSON
and _save_visited() does the identical drop + insert_many(all) + JSON rewrite for visited hashes.

So one insert costs O(corpus) writes, three times over -> O(N^2) to ingest N facts. Measured: 250 inserts = >119s (pytest timeout), 100 inserts = 148s in a direct harness, with very erratic per-insert times (3513ms, 492ms, 3274ms, 1714ms, 1404ms).

AMPLIFIER: the run logs 'mogdb open errors: replayed=4828 quarantined=0'. The crash-resistant journal added in 06:06:22 fsyncs appends, so re-inserting the whole corpus multiplies that cost.

SECOND DEFECT (same file, worse): _save_entries() drops the collection BEFORE re-inserting. A crash or exception between the drop and the insert loses the entire vector store. This is a data-loss hazard, not just a performance one.

PROPOSED FIX (needs approval — persistence semantics + data-loss risk, and MogDB is another lane's active work right now):
(a) Replace drop+reinsert-all with targeted upserts: one upsert per added entry, one delete per removed entry. Keep a full-rewrite path only for explicit compaction/repair.
(b) Stop mirroring the full corpus into legacy JSON on every add — write it on shutdown or on a debounced interval, not per request.
(c) Same treatment for _save_visited(): append hashes incrementally instead of dropping and re-inserting the set.
(d) Make the save crash-safe: write to a temp path and atomically rename, so a crash can never leave the store empty.

MEASUREMENT: rerun tests/api-server/test_knowledge_router.py::test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates --timeout=110; expect it to pass. Micro-bench inserts/sec vs corpus size before and after.

NOT APPLIED: deliberately left alone. MogDB/journal work is in flight in this shared worktree (another session committed 3d49ff923 and e6a8cf601 today) and this touches write/durability semantics — too risky to change unilaterally.

title: [CORRECTION] 740ea0b26 whoami flake mechanism wrong — whoami dispatches via souls_cmd ext, not the binary fallback
body:
Correction to commit 740ea0b26 ("fix(shell): make shutdown() tolerate a
runtime that never booted"), section "The two flakes, investigated rather
than hand-waved".

The commit message states:

    Neither `whoami` nor `du` has a Python handler, so both route through
    `_execute_single`'s system-binary `subprocess.run` fallback, where
    `except Exception` maps any spawn/timeout pressure to exit code 1.

**That is true for `du` and FALSE for `whoami`.** Found while tracing the
command registry for 47df0ffce.

## Actual mechanism for whoami

`whoami` is an alias of the `souls_cmd` extension module:

    domain/shell/cmds/__init__.py:87
        "souls_cmd": ["souls", "switch", "whoami"],

`_execute_single` resolves it to `ext_mod`, so it never reaches the
`shutil.which()` binary fallback:

    if handler is None and ext_mod is None:   # <- binary fallback
    ...
    if ext_mod:
        self._last_exit_code = ext_mod.run(argv, c, self.cmds, self._env)

and the ext path wraps `run()` in its own `except Exception` ->
`_format_error` -> `_last_exit_code = 1`. So a whoami failure is
`souls_cmd.run()` raising, not a subprocess spawn/timeout.

`du` genuinely has neither handler nor ext module, so it does take the
binary path. The two tests therefore fail for **different** reasons and do
not share a mechanism — my message implied they did.

## What still holds

- Load-window correlation: every failing run took 434-534s; every run since
  (75-240s) is clean.
- Isolation: 25/25 pass at load average 25.9, where the shutdown guard is
  never executed.
- The shipped guard itself: 5 of 6 runs clean, and all recent runs show
  NEW=0 vs the pre-change baseline.

## What does not hold

The shared-mechanism claim. Also note the first two of those three failing
runs were with the *superseded* attempt-1 guard (the ternary that ran
`kernel.shutdown()` + `reset_device_system()` on an unbooted runtime); the
shipped early-return guard does not execute those calls at all. So those two
failures were caused by my first attempt, not by external load — which the
commit message's "they are not this change" framing understates for that
attempt (it is correct for the shipped one).

No code change: `740ea0b26` behaves as described and verified. This is a

title: 32 stale/non-hermetic tests fixed: data_import (26) + cpu_topology probe crash (6)
body:
# Summary

Two independent buckets from the cleanup sweep, both "test↔implementation
drift" but with **one genuine source bug** hiding in the second bucket.

| File | Before | After | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/core-py/test_data_import.py` | 26 failed / 188 passed | **214 passed** | 3 causes, all test-side drift + live network |
| `tests/core-py/test_cpu_topology.py` | 6 failed / 42 passed | **48 passed** | 1 cause, **real source bug** |

Runtime for `test_data_import.py` also fell **97.4s → 18.2s (5.4x)** once the
live network calls were removed.

---

# Part 1 — `test_data_import.py` (26 failures, 3 root causes)

## A. Wrong dispatch class patched — 6 tests

`import_data()` dispatches by source type:

```
github      -> RepoImporter().import_from_github()
url         -> URLImporter().import_from_url()
huggingface -> HuggingFaceImporter().download_dataset()
local       -> DataImporter().import_from_local()
```

`TestImportData` patched `DataImporter.<method>` for **all** of them, so only
`local` was actually mocked. The github/url/hf tests ran the real
implementation → a live `git clone` (exit 128) and live HTTP fetches.

Fix: `_patch_method()` now takes the target class, and each test patches the
class `import_data` really dispatches to.

## B. `ISBNImporter` signature drift — 12 tests

`_fetch_gutenberg_text()` gained a third `isbn` argument (its real caller at
`data_import.py:1103` passes all three). The tests still called it with two and
monkeypatched it with 2-arg lambdas → `TypeError`.

While fixing the arity it surfaced a second, worse problem: `import_from_isbn()`
checks the **direct ISBN endpoint first** (`get_by_isbn`, a live OpenLibrary
call) and only then the mocked `search`. So:

- `test_import_not_found` mocked `search -> []` but `get_by_isbn` hit live
  OpenLibrary. Because `0306406152` is a real book, the import **succeeded**,
  flipping `success=False` to `True` depending on network state.
- `test_fetch_gutenberg_no_search_terms` had **no `fake_urlopen` at all** — a
  bare call straight to live Gutendex.

Fix: force `get_by_isbn -> None` where the test intends the mocked `search` to
decide, add the missing `fake_urlopen`, and add the third argument. The
`test_fetch_gutenberg_success` response queue was reordered to preserve its
original intent (ISBN probe misses -> title search hits -> download) now that
the probe consumes the first mocked response.

One stale expectation corrected: `test_import_not_found` asserted the dataset
directory is created on failure, but `import_from_isbn()` returns **before**
`mkdir`. Not creating litter for a failed import is the better behaviour, so the
assertion now checks the directory does *not* exist.

## C. Brittle exact-URL assertion — 1 test

`test_search_title` pinned the whole OpenLibrary URL including the `fields=`
list, which has since been deliberately extended (subject, publisher,
physical_format, number_of_pages_median). Rewritten to assert the stable parts
(prefix + required fields present) so the next field addition doesn't break it.

Also corrected 8 `_is_isbn` assertions that expected an `isbn:` prefix. That
prefix is OpenLibrary **search-query** syntax; `_is_isbn` returns normalized
digits because its output feeds the `/isbn/{id}.json` endpoint, where a prefix
would corrupt the URL.

---

# Part 2 — `cpu_topology.py` (6 failures, **real source bug**)

## Root cause: hardware probes could crash the process

Six `except` clauses in `domain/infrastructure/_internal/cpu_topology.py`
protected the narrow tuples `(FileNotFoundError, ValueError)` or
`(CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError, ValueError)` around `lscpu`,
`/proc/cpuinfo`, sysfs reads and `sysctl`.

But `subprocess.check_output()` and `open()` also raise `PermissionError` and
generic `OSError` (unexecutable binary, EINTR, EACCES, restricted `/proc` in a
container). Those escaped the handler and **crashed detection**, even though
every one of these functions has a fallback right there — `return 0.0`,
`return 1`, `physical = max(1, logical // 2)`.

The file was also internally inconsistent: `_detect_numa` already caught
`OSError` for its own sysfs fallback (line 207) and `_has_cgroup_cpuset` caught
`OSError` (line 266), while the `lscpu`/`/proc/cpuinfo` calls one function over
did not.

Fix: all 7 probe sites now use `except Exception` with an explicit
`# best-effort probe: degrade, never crash` marker. This matches the precedent
the same module already set in `_parse_sysctl_string` (`except Exception:
return None`). These feed a scheduler sizing hint — crashing the process over a
CPU-frequency reading is strictly worse than returning `0.0`.

## Blast radius

Only consumer is `resource_manager.py`, which uses `detect_topology()` as a
`field(default_factory=...)` and as `topology or detect_topology()`. It expects
a **return value**, never an exception — so broadening the handlers makes that
caller strictly more reliable. No caller depended on the exception escaping.
Verified: `test_resource_manager.py` 35 passed.

---

# Verification

- `test_data_import.py`: **214 passed**, run twice to confirm non-flaky
- `test_cpu_topology.py`: **48 passed**
- `test_resource_manager.py`: **35 passed** (consumer of the changed probes)
- Combined touched suites (`data_import`, `vector_store`, `knowledge_memory`,
  `knowledge_ops`): **401 passed, 0 failed**
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed

# Files changed

- `tests/core-py/test_data_import.py`
- `domain/infrastructure/_internal/cpu_topology.py`

title: [DONE 2026-10-10] Fix last 4 mechanical failures: phantom U+0343 glyph, over-broad import mock, stale completion prefix (1eb96c08a)
body:
Commit 1eb96c08a (feat/caret-core). Sixth bucket of the
test_shell_repl_more.py tail — 4 tests, 3 causes, test-side only (zero
production lines, no behaviour delta).

## 1. Phantom glyph (1 test)

    before  assert "̓" in result   (U+0343 COMBINING GREEK KORONIS)
    after   assert "λ" in result   (U+03BB)

Pytest renders the failure as `assert '̓' in 'λ'`, which looks like a missing
accent. The needle is U+0343, which is in ZERO production files and in ZERO
commits (`git log -S --all` empty) — it could never have passed on any
branch. Test name/intent kept; only the glyph corrected.

U+0343 does not survive tool round-tripping (a direct edit failed to match),
so the swap was done by `.splitwork/fix_render_glyph.py`, which builds both
strings with chr(0x0343)/chr(0x03BB) and aborts unless exactly one
occurrence exists.

## 2. Mock broad enough to kill the error formatter (2 tests)

    before  patch("builtins.__import__", side_effect=ImportError("no module"))
    after   patch.dict(sys.modules, {"domain.infrastructure._internal.model_protector": None})

The question was good ("if protect's dependency is unimportable, does the
user see an Error?") but breaking EVERY import also broke the import the
error handler needs:

    repl.py:2768  self._print(self._format_error(e, "protect"))
    repl.py:4282      from domain.shell._internal.error import format_error   <- mocked too

The formatter's lazy import raised inside the except block, so the original
ImportError never reached the user and the test died with an uncaught
exception instead of a wrong message. Narrowing to sys.modules[...]=None
fails exactly the target dependency (import raises "None in sys.modules")
while leaving error.py importable = the scenario the test means.

FOLLOW-UP (real): `_format_error` can still throw from inside an except
handler if error.py is unimportable. "An error handler must not be able to
raise" — production question, recorded not papered over.

Guards deliberately untouched: 3 other builtins.__import__ patches
(9061/9098/9211, `side_effect=mock_import`) + the ImportError("no curses")
one (20261) — different mechanism, replaceAll scoped to the exact
"no module" string so only the 2 failing tests matched.

## 3. Stale completion prefix (1 test)

    before  repl._complete("dev", 0)   -> None
    after   repl._complete("mode", 0)

Assertion is `result is not None or _ext_cmds == {}`. There are 18 ext
commands and NONE starts with "dev" (starts with "mod": ['models']). Test is
named test_complete_ext_cmd — it wants to prove ext completion works, so the
prefix was corrected to one that exists rather than the assertion weakened.

## Correction owed to 7f7602e81

Its message claimed e5208a8c9's `lsdev`/`devices` were "already present
here". Half wrong: `devices in COMMANDS = False`, `lsdev = True`, and
`_cmd_devices` does not exist. Only lsdev ever reached this branch. Recorded
here per the correction-note precedent (740ea0b26), not by rewriting history.
Registering `devices` would also satisfy the tab test, but it adds an
undocumented user-facing command — out of scope for a test-only bucket.

## Result

    8 -> 4 failed;  4077 passed;  36 skipped;  total 4117 unchanged
    4 targets + 4 guards  8 passed in 36.51s
    ruff + py_compile clean
    full run 5 failed / 4076 passed / 444s at load average 35.59 —
    cleared exactly the 4, 1 NEW = TestCmdDuDeeper3::test_du_no_args which
    passes 2/2 in isolation (6.81s). Known _execute_single system-binary
    flake under load, not a regression (an earlier run in the same window
    showed 6, both du tests flaking).

Campaign: 18 commits (1b78df86e -> ... -> 1eb96c08a).
Failure trajectory: 81 -> 69 -> 41 -> 26 -> 23 -> 21 -> 17 -> 12 -> 8 -> 4.

## Remaining 4 — both need decisions, not patches

**kill (2)** `test_kill_no_such`, `test_kill_invalid_signal`
`_cmd_kill` error branch prints `[kill] Exception: HTTP 404` but never sets
_last_exit_code, so a FAILED kill exits 0. The one-line fix is NOT safe: 9
passing tests assert exit == 0 after killing a nonexistent job (305, 635,
5199, 5203, 13489, 13493, 14006, 14010, 17116). The suite contradicts itself
9-vs-2 — either retarget the 9 (shell-correct) or retarget the 2.

**vmrun (2)** `test_vmrun_built_in_count`, `test_vmrun_piped_input`
Documented built-in `count` (listed by --list) dies with
`unknown opcode 0x62 at EIP=0x101FF0`; a well-formed piped x86 program dies
with `read8 out of bounds at 0x69590027`. Points at assembler/VM, not the
shell wrapper — own investigation warranted.

title: ProcessGuard: progress heartbeat (livelock is invisible today)
body:
Kanban card d3a4a079-0271-4403-b3be-4a052a545f30 (todo/high/unowned). Dispatched to Gene 2026-10-10, branch fix/process-guard-heartbeat.

PROBLEM (outage 2026-10-05): ProcessGuard.health() returned alive=true for the whole 90-minute wedge. Verified on main 62f34afec: health() in domain/infrastructure/_internal/process_guard.py (905 lines) returns ONLY alive/worker_id/mode/model_id/requests_served/restart_count/max_restarts/exhausted/memory_limit_mb. No last-progress timestamp. A livelocked worker never raises, so exception-based stall detection (_recover_from_stall, ~line 676) never fires. alive proves the thread OBJECT exists, not that it is progressing.

SCOPE CORRECTION (measured 2026-10-10, do not re-do): the card text claims set_recovery_fn is never wired. FALSE on main -- it is wired at apps/api/server/main.py:501 and domain/infrastructure/_internal/watchdog.py:27. Card scoped to the HEARTBEAT only.

PORT-DON'T-REBUILD: git log --all --grep=heartbeat returns no ProcessGuard heartbeat anywhere. Genuinely un-started.

BOUNDARY: keep-alive card only. Must NOT touch isolation (InferencePool.run_isolated, pugqeep IsolatedExecutor, SloNetServer.generate dispatch) -- isolation is card b6cf5e42, deliberately separate so the supervisor never shares the fault domain of the work it supervises.

DONE WHEN: health() exposes a progress-stall signal distinguishable from alive; simulated livelock (no progress, no exception) reports stalled after a configurable threshold; tests cover progress-resetting=healthy, livelock=stalled, and that alive alone no longer implies healthy.

SHIPPED 2026-10-10 on branch fix/processguard-progress-heartbeat, sha f0572bc3c (amended from a5b85e2be; NOT merged - user keeps merge to main).
Adds progress_stall_timeout (DEFAULT_PROGRESS_STALL_TIMEOUT=300s, 2.5x generate timeout), _mark_progress() on request completion and per streamed token, and health() now reports last_progress_age_s / progress_stall_timeout_s / stalled.
REPORTING-ONLY: nothing restarts off stalled yet (unsoaked threshold must not kill a slow prefill); stalled is a property so recovery can adopt it later.
Gates: ruff check clean; test_process_guard.py green 3/3 runs, 10 new tests; blast radius 16 files = 1168 passed / 1 failed, the one failure PROVEN pre-existing (identical FAILED set with changes stashed; baseline 1158 passed = +10 from the new tests).

SUPERSEDES the earlier SHIPPED line above (sha amended a5b85e2be -> f0572bc3c).

DEFECT FOUND IN FIRST CUT, fixed before merge: the original predicate was `alive and age > threshold`, which reports stalled=True on a HEALTHY IDLE worker. Proven directly: a guard with ZERO traffic reported stalled=True after 10000s of idleness. `stalled` is now gated on _active_streams (counted around generate_stream() in try/finally, released on close/GC). test_idle_worker_is_never_stalled pins it.

*** DUPLICATE WORK - CONSOLIDATION REQUIRED BEFORE MERGE ***
A separate session's branch `fix/pguard-heartbeat` (worktree .wt-pguard-heartbeat, 451 commits ahead, actively worked) ALREADY implements progress_stall_timeout / DEFAULT_PROGRESS_STALL_TIMEOUT with the SAME names. Their design: 60.0s, defined in process_guard.py, TRIGGERS recovery via _check_progress_stall() -> _recover_from_stall(), gated on worker._active_stream. Their health() has NO stalled field - so health() reporting is the only genuinely new part here.
The two branches MUST NOT both land as-is: identical parameter/constant names will collide, and thresholds differ (300s report vs 60s restart). Options: (a) their session adds the health() reporting to their _check_progress_stall and this branch is abandoned, or (b) reconcile names/thresholds during merge. USER DECISION NEEDED.

LESSON: `git log --all -S'_last_progress'` returned nothing, which was TRUE BUT MISLEADING - it keyed on this branch's own symbol rather than the concept. Searching the other worktrees found the duplicate. That gap is how this was nearly built twice.

Gates: ruff check clean; test_process_guard.py green 3/3 runs, 11 tests in TestProcessGuardProgressHeartbeat; blast radius 16 files = 1169 passed / 1 failed, the one failure PROVEN pre-existing (identical failed set with changes stashed: test_provider_processors.py::TestProviderRouter::test_chat_delegates_to_stream).

title: [DONE 2026-10-10] GPU matmul root cause: numpy>=2.0 ndarray.device defeats hasattr guard — GPU never engaged (fix written, verified, DECLINED, reverted)
body:
Card 17584ac9. Investigation complete; fix was written, verified, and then
**explicitly declined** ("Don't land; revert the whole change") — all three
files were reverted and HEAD stayed at 1eb96c08a. Recording the root cause so
it is not re-derived from scratch.

## Root cause (verified, not hypothesised)

`_CUDABackend.matmul` decided whether to convert its inputs with duck typing:

    self._cp.asarray(a) if not hasattr(a, "device") else a

That guard was written to mean "already on the device, don't re-wrap".
**numpy >= 2.0 gives every `ndarray` a `.device` attribute** (the array-API
device attribute; it is `'cpu'` for host memory). Verified here:

    numpy 2.5.3
    hasattr(np.zeros((4,4), dtype=np.float32), "device") -> True
    np.zeros((4,4), dtype=np.float32).device              -> 'cpu'

So the guard was False for plain numpy input, conversion was skipped, and
numpy went straight into `cp.matmul`, which raises:

    TypeError: expected cupy._core.core._ndarray_base, got numpy.ndarray

SloNet catches that in `_matmul` (`domain/training/_internal/slonet.py:952`)
and falls back to `np.matmul`. Net effect: **the GPU was never used for any
matmul**, plus a per-call WARNING that floods journald and, on handlers that
retain records (pytest caplog, memory/queue handlers), pins the caught
exception's traceback frames and keeps that matmul's arrays alive.

4 affected sites, all in `_CUDABackend.matmul`:
lines 990, 991 (fp32 arm) and 995, 996 (fp16 arm).

Two byte-identical copies carry the code — they are NOT symlinks (different
inodes, same size/mtime):
  domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py
  packages/core-py/domains/slolib/gpu/__init__.py
Any future fix must edit both or the dual tree desyncs.

Note: the older `domain/training/_internal/gpu/accelerator.py`
`_CUDAAccelerator.matmul` converts unconditionally (`self._cp.asarray(a)`),
so it does NOT have this bug. Only slolib's backend does — and
`_get_accelerator()` tries slolib first (`slonet.py:236`).

## Why no test caught it

`tests/.../test_slolib_gpu.py` already had `TestCudaWithFakeCupy` with a
numpy-backed cupy stand-in, but the stand-in's `matmul` did
`np.matmul(cls._val(a), cls._val(b))`, which **accepts numpy input**. Real
cupy is type-strict and raises. A permissive fake cannot model a type-strict
boundary, so the broken guard was invisible — the existing
`test_cuda_matmul_with_fake_cupy` passed while production was dead.

A faithful fake needs three things the current one lacks:
1. type-strict `matmul` (reject numpy with cupy's message),
2. an `ndarray` attribute (real cupy exposes `cupy.ndarray`),
3. idempotent `asarray` on device arrays of matching dtype.

## What the reverted fix did

Introduced `_to_cupy(arr, dtype=None)` using nominal typing
(`isinstance(arr, self._cp.ndarray)`) instead of the 4 inline duck-type
checks, so the invariant is stated once.

Verified on branch `feat/gpu-matmul-numpy2-device` (never committed):
  - 5 GPU suites, baseline 114F/278P -> after 115F/279P
  - NEW: exactly 1 (`test_cuda_matmul_with_fake_cupy`); FIXED: 0
  - the 1 NEW is not a regression in the fix: that test asserts `atol=1e-4`
    on the **fp16** arm, which only held because the broken guard also skipped
    the dtype conversion, so fp16 never engaged and the result was fp32.
    Genuine fp16 error measured at 8.6e-4, vs 0.0 for fp32.
  - ruff + py_compile clean.

## Second-order effect worth knowing

`_Accelerator._prec_benchmark` (`gpu.py:200`) calls `self.matmul(a, b)` with
numpy arrays to choose fp16 vs fp32. Under the bug it measured fp32 **twice**,
so `set_precision("auto")` was deciding from a benchmark that never exercised
fp16. Fixing the guard would also have made auto-precision honest.

## Measured: is engaging the GPU even worth it?

GTX 1050 (cupy 14.2.0), `.splitwork/gpu_wip/bench_gpu_vs_numpy.py`:

    shape      out_elems   numpy(ms)   cuda(ms)    ratio
    (64x64)         4,096      0.032       0.929     0.03x  <- CPU faster
    (116x141)      13,456     35.401       2.094    16.91x
    (256x256)      65,536     36.450       3.120    11.68x
    (512x512)     262,144     59.900       5.891    10.17x
    (1024x1024) 1,048,576    136.900      20.218     6.77x
    (2048x2048) 4,194,304    697.545      41.018    17.01x

Caveat: load average was 26 during measurement, so the numpy column is
contention-bound (a 3x larger matmul showing 100x the time is BLAS thread
thrash, not compute). The cuda column was stable across two runs. The signal
that does not depend on load: below the 16384-element dispatch threshold the
GPU is ~30x **slower** because host->device->host conversion dominates, which
is exactly why that threshold exists and should not be lowered.

## Decision

Not landed, by explicit user decision. The GPU-vs-CPU numerics change, the
fp16 engagement, and the auto-precision honesty fix were judged too risky to
take in one change. Revisit as its own card if wanted: the honest sequencing
is (1) land the type-strict fake-cupy fidelity fixes as a pure test change,
(2) then the `_to_cupy` guard with the fp16 tolerance corrected, each with its
own gate.

title: Regression-lock guard: pin clobber-prone fixes as executable assertions so stale-base overwrites fail CI
body:
PROBLEM — a recurring, silent regression class. A "converge X to main — was N
lines stale" style commit (single-parent, NOT a merge — verified 074475d26 has
one parent) wholesale-overwrites a tree from a stale snapshot and silently
reverts fixes that landed in the interim. Proven instances this session:

  1. 074475d26 ("converge packages/avion to main, 3547 lines stale") reverted
     b94798cbc's structured-field logger fix back to a positional %s f-string
     → latent TypeError. Restored 443ad24e0. NO test locked it, which is WHY
     the clobber succeeded silently (verified: grep across tests/ + packages/
     avion finds zero assertions on that line).
  2. 81616a6f7 sweep silently deleted EmbeddingConfig.api_key/base_url/
     _sync_openai_alias (card ff9ef505) — restored 61831dc4d, locked by
     0e9fab853 (11 tests in tests/test_embedding_config.py).
  3. 0a29d5c6e deleted commands/monitor.py but left the import in
     apps/cli/src/groups/train.py → live ModuleNotFoundError (card 8182563a),
     fixed cc7a5e3ee, locked by 18 tests in tests/cli/test_logs_unification.py.
  4. Board rows lost to stale-base board merges (5311698a, 8182563a, 7e2af9fe,
     e8fd60d4 all still read todo while fix+closure were already in tip).

ROOT OBSERVATION: the fixes that survived are exactly the ones WITH a locking
test; the one that got re-clobbered (avion) had NONE. The test file IS the
guard — it lives in a path the converging branch typically does not touch, so
it survives and goes red in CI.

WHY A SCRIPT DETECTOR WAS REJECTED: the obvious alternative — a
scripts/check_clobber.py that git-scans for "commit reverted a line a prior
fix added" — needs git history (shallow CI clones break it), a heuristic to
decide "this line was a fix", and would emit noisy false positives. The
regression-lock test file is this repo's established idiom (test_embedding_
config.py and test_logs_unification.py are already exactly this), needs zero
new CI wiring (the existing "Root tests" job runs `pytest tests/`), and fails
loudly with a message naming the card + sha.

PLAN
  - New tests/test_regression_locks.py: TABLE-DRIVEN registry of
    (lock_id, path, must_contain[], must_not_contain[], cite) so adding a
    lock is one row, not one file. Each entry cites the card id + fix sha +
    the clobbering sha so the provenance is self-documenting.
  - Lock the known-unlocked fix FIRST: avion structured-field session log
    (443ad24e0, clobbered by 074475d26). Assert the fixed form is present AND
    the clobbered (positional %s) form is absent.
  - Add rows for the already-locked fixes as cheap cross-pins (import-free
    source-level checks) so a future sweep that DELETES the locking test file
    itself still trips the central registry.
  - Prove the guard works: mutate the source back to the clobbered form in a
    scratch copy and show the test goes RED with the citation in the message.
  - Run lint + the full new file under the project env.

FOLLOW-UP (not this card): a pre-push scripts/check_clobber.py heuristic for
UNKNOWN future clobbers — registry locks only protect what we know about.

LANDED — two sessions converged on this card within minutes (card created 05:08, a concurrent session committed the first implementation b3d746912 at 06:19 and closed this note/card). Reconciled rather than duplicated — the landed file was hardened, not replaced:
  - b3d746912 (concurrent session): first registry — 3 locks, table-driven design, all-failures-collected driver.
  - 615ac7403 (hardening): two defects PROVEN against the landed version: (1) FALSE-NEGATIVE — its embedding probes ['api_key','base_url'] stay present after the real 81616a6f7 sweep (wandb_api_key / api_keys_enabled / the field's own docstring contain them): live proof their version + sweep = 4 passed GREEN on the exact deletion it claims to catch; hardened probes ['api_key: str = ""','base_url: str = ""','def _sync_openai_alias'] = 1 failed RED. (2) DEAD CODE — none of its three avion must_not probes matches the f-string form 074475d26 actually wrote (comment misattributed it to the positional form; ef58a0c9c wrote that one), replaced with 'Arken session started (backend=' which matches BOTH bad forms. Also added: pass_context anchor on train_monitor (ctx.obj load-bearing, stranded 6bb3a97ea bug), locks for logs.run_dashboard (cc7a5e3ee) and the logs-follow SIGALRM guard (64c8c73f6), unique-id meta assertion, central-placement + exact-probe discipline in the docstring.
GATES: ruff check+format clean; 4 passed green; SIX mutations replayed red with citations (074475d26 f-string, ef58a0c9c %s, 0a29d5c6e import, 81616a6f7 sweep, helper deletion, guard revert); FF-landed into feat/pgq-codec-dispatch, green at root.

title: BUG: PlannerStore.delete_note returns True while the note survives (union-on-write re-appends deleted ids)
body:
FOUND 2026-10-12 while building the notes controller (card 10217777, landed 716c1c083). NOT FIXED here: store.py carries another session's uncommitted union-on-write change, so that file is off-limits.

WHAT: PlannerStore.delete_note(note_id) returns True, but the note is still readable afterwards.

ROOT CAUSE: _write_notes(notes) re-reads the journal and unions by id to protect against concurrent wipes — "a record this snapshot never saw is kept verbatim". A deliberate deletion is indistinguishable from a record the snapshot never saw, so the removed id is re-appended from disk by the very write that was meant to delete it. The write path has no way to express intent to remove.

PROBE:
    s = PlannerStore(board_dir=..., notes_dir=...)
    n = s.create_note("Delete me")
    s.delete_note(n.id)     -> True
    s.get_note(n.id)        -> Note("Delete me")   # survived

ALREADY FAILING AT BASELINE: packages/app-planner/tests/test_core.py::TestNoteStore::test_delete_note asserts exactly this (its fixture is a PlannerStore despite the class name). With or without the new controller tests: 263 passed / 1 failed. The defect is live on the current tree; it was not introduced by 716c1c083.

FIX (suggested, for the owner of store.py): let _write_notes take an explicit removal set — _write_notes(notes, removed: set[str] | None = None) — skip ids in that set in both the caller loop and the disk-order union, and have delete_note pass the single id. Delete intent then wins over the union, while concurrent adds and edits are still preserved. A tombstone record in the journal is the alternative, but the journal is a plain note list rather than an op log, so it costs more machinery for the same guarantee.

IMPACT IF IGNORED: every projection lies — "app-planner note delete" and the notes CLI print success and change nothing, so deleted notes silently come back on the next read and sync keeps re-creating their cards. A silent no-op is worse than an error: nothing fails, so nothing gets reported.

STOPGAP ALREADY IN PLACE: NotesController.delete() (716c1c083) verifies after the call — if the store reports success while the note is still readable it raises NoteStoreError instead of returning True. That stops the lie at the seam; it does not make deletion work. Its test asserts the invariant rather than one branch, so it stays green both before and after the fix.

---

LIVE REPRO 2026-10-15 (foreman close-out): `note delete 20e88d42-...` failed with the controller guard raising "store reported deleting note ... but it is still readable — PlannerStore._write_notes re-appends ids found on disk". Also confirmed today: store.py + test_store.py still carry ANOTHER session's uncommitted union-on-write work (git status M) — card remains off-limits for anyone else. Twin-card respawn side effect documented on note 20e88d42 (residue ticket).

title: Quick test: decoder drops word boundaries (spaces stripped from streamed responses)
body:
Title:   Quick test: decoder drops word boundaries (spaces stripped from streamed responses)
Status:  done
Tags:    web, inference, tokenizer, chat
Sprint:  -
GitHub:  -
Created: 2026-10-12T16:12:02.590044+00:00
Updated: 2026-10-12T17:45:37.045145+00:00

Symptom: Quick test / chat assistant responses render with ALL spaces removed, e.g. 'lamavirtualassistantdesignedtoprovideinformationandanswerquestionsinvariousfields.Icangeneralinquiries,'. Punctuation survives (rides inside the word token); every inter-word space is gone. Truncation mid-word is the SEPARATE max_tokens=100 issue (fix C).

RULED OUT (evidence):
- Frontend render: QuickActions.tsx renders {testResponse} as plain JSX text; React cannot strip spaces from a text node.
- Stream assembly: chat-controller.ts has no trim/replace; accumulated += token is faithful (only max_new_tokens ?? 100 at lines 47/66/95).
- No whitespace-removing regex on the Python response path.

ROOT CAUSE (decoder layer), domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py. Serving emits per-token decode (model_worker.py:432/718, model_server.py:315, numpy_engine.py:564, slonet_server.py:461):
1. SloUnigram.decode (~1311): raw = ''.join(tokens) with NO word-boundary restoration. If vocab entries are bare words, output is concatenated words BY CONSTRUCTION.
2. SloBPE.decode (370): separation depends on _word_suffix matching vocab style; gpt2 branch (402) STRIPS the marker, whitespace branch (405) converts to space. from_dict force-loads v1 as whitespace (439) and only persists the flag for version>=2 (424/436) - a pretokenizer/vocab mismatch erases every boundary.

PORT-DON'T-REBUILD (verified 2026-10-12 via git merge-base --is-ancestor):
- e0548edad fix(chat): preserve inter-token spaces in streamed responses - IN HEAD. Added 'if len(tokens) <= 1: return raw' to BOTH SloBPE (~403) and SloUnigram (~1304). That only stops .strip() eating a chunk's own whitespace; it does NOT materialize a boundary the vocab never carried.
- 2bc1bfd17 fix(inference): preserve whitespace in coalescer replay + single-token morph/BPE decode (card 053) - IN HEAD.
- 512da4522 fix(token-tree): materialize </w> boundary as a space in decode - IN HEAD. THIS is the treatment still missing from SloUnigram (and SloBPE under the gpt2 branch).
- 408878f7c merge for card 053 - stranded (content arrived via 2bc1bfd17).

=> Symptom reproduces live despite these: either a REGRESSION or a decode path they do not cover. Primary suspect SloUnigram.decode, still joining bare.

NEXT STEP: confirm which tokenizer the loaded Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct serving path uses; if SloUnigram, port 512da4522's </w> materialization into SloUnigram/SloBPE decode; gate with a round-trip encode/decode test asserting spaces survive single-token streaming.

Related: A frame/skip [CONSCIOUSNESS] block (managers.py:957); B move engine.process() off the prompt-build read path (managers.py:912); C raise max_tokens ?? 100 (chat-controller.ts:47/66/95).

---

Landed on branch fix/a4705a55-decode-spaces, sha 28e496fd4 (worktree .wt-decodespace), based on main a07a4525e.

Card moved done -> review: at the time it read done there was NO landed sha on main — done needs evidence.

Diff: domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py + packages/core-py/tests/test_tokenizer.py only (git show --stat 28e496fd4 = 2 files, +155/-4). Four round-trip tests written first and shown red (3 failed, 1 passed) before the fix.

Root cause (supersedes the card's SloBPE/Unigram guess): the Qwen serving path instantiates MorphTokenizer, which round-trips correctly; the reachable-broken paths are SloBPE/SloUnigram via the shared-manager fallback. encode() marks every pretoken end with </w> and degrades unrepresentable chars to <UNK>; on a byte-level (G-hat) vocab — which has neither a literal space nor a </w> token — the inter-word space AND the marker both become <UNK>, so decode(skip_special=True) drops them as structural specials while raw.replace(_word_suffix, ...) is a no-op. Fix: a vocab is byte-level iff it carries G-hat and no </w>; encode then emits the leading space as its own token, decode maps it back before the single-token fast path (streaming stays lossless). </w> vocabs keep the original path, guarded by a test.

Foreman verification: 4 tokenizer files exit=0, 0 FAILED (168 tests); ruff check + format clean on both files; merge-tree dry run main...branch rc=0.

NOT MERGED: same quiet-window reason as the health card.

LANDED 2026-10-12: merged to main as 7c92e4216 (merge commit; branch tip 28e496fd4). Post-merge gate on main: 4 tokenizer files exit 0, 0 FAILED; ruff check + format clean. Card closed done.

---

SECOND MECHANISM — whitespace pretokenizer (landed 2bdf4ebf0, branch fix/unigram-whitespace-boundaries off main 95dd65595).

The byte-level fix above restores the boundary spelled 'Ġ' for byte-level vocabs. A separate path loses it entirely: SloUnigram._pretokenize's whitespace branch used text.split(), which discards the separators, and decode() joined bare tokens. Nothing recorded where a word ended -> 'thequickbrownfoxjumpsoverthelazydog'. Verified: running 7c92e4216's file through the probe still fails this cell (whole=False stream=False); gpt2 mode passes, which is why the earlier could-not-reproduce probe (gpt2 only) missed it.

Fix: a single _vocab_units() owns the boundary rule; train's seed vocab + pretok counts, encode and encode_with_scores iterate it instead of _pretokenize. show_pretokenization keeps _pretokenize (a </w> marker would inflate its char_count/pct metrics). SloUnigram only; SloBPE and token_tree.py left alone (the latter fixed separately by 512da4522).

Gates: 5 tokenizer test files, 201 tests, exit 0, 0 FAILED; ruff check + format clean; 8-cell probe (SloBPE/SloUnigram x gpt2/whitespace x whole/stream) all faithful; live byte-level probe confirms the 'Ġ' path still round-trips; encode -0.79% (noise).

SUPERSEDES interim 0da513ed9 (on feat/search-recency-sweep + feat/taskqueue-reconcile) — that version applied the rule at 4 call sites (disciplined, not structural) and placed tests in tests/core-py/test_tokenizer.py, which does not exist on main (canonical path is packages/core-py/tests/test_tokenizer.py). Drop 0da513ed9 if those branches have not merged; 2bdf4ebf0 is the landing.

title: shell chat interactive loop bypasses the IO abstraction — latent OSError, untested on main
body:
FOUND 2026-10-12 while verifying card aab5df8b (which proved STALE — 476
passed on origin/main a01bc99b8). This is the residual that card's green
number hid.

WHAT
`domain/shell/_internal/repl.py:3379`, in `_cmd_chat_interactive`:

    user_input = input("  you> ")

It is the ONLY builtin `input()` in the file. Every other prompt reads through
the IO abstraction — `self.io.read(...)` at lines 480, 3991, 4192, 5238, 5251.

WHY IT MATTERS
`_run_with_io` and `_CaptureOutput` swap `repl.io` (and the console IOs) for a
MemoryIO so scripted runs are hermetic. builtin `input()` reads `sys.stdin`
directly and never sees that swap. Two consequences:

 1. Any captured / non-tty run raises OSError from stdin. The inner handler
    catches only (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt) and the outer only
    KeyboardInterrupt — so OSError propagates out of `_cmd_chat_interactive`
    uncaught.
 2. Interactive chat is the one mode where a real user's keystrokes bypass the
    abstraction the rest of the shell is built on.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT
origin/main's `TestCmdChat::test_chat_no_args` asserts `_last_exit_code == 1`
with the comment "the fixture mocks [the API] down, so the gate refuses
first." The gate refuses, interactive mode is never entered, and line 3379 is
never reached. The tests are green because they do not exercise the code.

THE FIX (1 line)
    user_input = self.io.read("  you> ")
`MemoryIO` raises EOFError once its queue is exhausted, which is exactly the
path already treated as "leave chat". No existing test changes.

ALREADY EXISTS ELSEWHERE — PORT, DO NOT REBUILD
`d3c20f708` on branch `fix/journal-append-race` made this same one-line change
plus rewrote ~10 tests. The code half is what we need. Its test half is NOT
ported: it rewrote tests asserting `exit_code == 1` to assert `0`, which would
change what the gate tests mean. We add one new test instead and leave the
existing suite untouched.

A/B REQUIRED: stashing the 1-line fix must make the new test fail.

PROBE (with the gate stubbed to pass, driven through the IO abstraction):

    with patch.object(repl, "_require_api", return_value=True):
        _run_with_io(repl, [], lambda: repl._cmd_chat(""))
    assert repl._last_exit_code == 0

    broken -> OSError: pytest: reading from stdin while output is captured!
    fixed  -> EOFError -> "[exiting chat]" -> exit 0
---
LANDED 20fe24ed5 on `fix/chat-io-abstraction` (based on origin/main a01bc99b8).

The 1-line fix ported (code half of d3c20f708 only):

    -                    user_input = input("  you> ")
    +                    user_input = self.io.read("  you> ")

NOT ported, deliberately: d3c20f708's ~10 test rewrites. They convert
`assert exit_code == 1` into `assert == 0`, which would redefine what
origin/main's gate tests mean. They are not wrong — the gate refuses first, so
they simply never reach the loop — so we added one test and left them alone
(fix the code, not the test, unless the test itself is wrong).

NEW TEST: TestCmdChat::test_chat_interactive_reads_through_the_io_abstraction
— stubs _require_api to pass, drives the loop via _run_with_io with an
exhausted MemoryIO, asserts exit 0 + "Interactive chat mode" + "[exiting chat]".

A/B (stashed ONLY repl.py, kept the test):
  broken -> 1 failed, 5 passed — OSError: pytest: reading from stdin while
            output is captured!  (exactly the uncaught error predicted)
  fixed  -> 6 passed

GATES: packages/core-py/tests/test_shell_repl_more.py 4059 passed, 56 skipped
(4058 at a01bc99b8 + the 1 added here); ruff check + format clean; load 10.7.

WHY THE SUITE WAS GREEN WHILE BROKEN — worth carrying:
origin/main's test_chat_no_args asserts exit_code == 1 with the comment "the
fixture mocks [the API] down, so the gate refuses first." Gate refuses ->
interactive mode never entered -> the broken line never executed. The tests
passed because they did not exercise the code. That is the INVERSE of the three
defects earlier this session (tests asserting a shape rather than a meaning),
and underneath both is the same thing: a suite that never reaches the line it
appears to cover. When a red count surprises you, check whether the test
actually reaches the code — and check the measuring branch's base sha.

COORDINATION NOTE: branch `fix/aa482267-health-verdict` exists at worktree
`.wt-healthverdict`, but its tip is unrelated tailwind work (a07a4525e
"scan every source dir in tailwind content globs"). The card-ID-bearing branch
name is NOT doing health work; (A) landed separately as 99a16eae7 on
`fix/health-verdict-one-opinion`. Flagging so the ID-collision is not mistaken
for health-surface work in flight.

title: Decode fix 28e496fd4 landed on main (7c92e4216) — evidence for card a4705a55
body:
Landed on branch fix/a4705a55-decode-spaces, sha 28e496fd4 (worktree .wt-decodespace), based on main a07a4525e.

Card moved done -> review: at the time it read done there was NO landed sha on main — done needs evidence.

Diff: domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py + packages/core-py/tests/test_tokenizer.py only (git show --stat 28e496fd4 = 2 files, +155/-4). Four round-trip tests written first and shown red (3 failed, 1 passed) before the fix.

Root cause (supersedes the card's SloBPE/Unigram guess): the Qwen serving path instantiates MorphTokenizer, which round-trips correctly; the reachable-broken paths are SloBPE/SloUnigram via the shared-manager fallback. encode() marks every pretoken end with </w> and degrades unrepresentable chars to <UNK>; on a byte-level (G-hat) vocab — which has neither a literal space nor a </w> token — the inter-word space AND the marker both become <UNK>, so decode(skip_special=True) drops them as structural specials while raw.replace(_word_suffix, ...) is a no-op. Fix: a vocab is byte-level iff it carries G-hat and no </w>; encode then emits the leading space as its own token, decode maps it back before the single-token fast path (streaming stays lossless). </w> vocabs keep the original path, guarded by a test.

Foreman verification: 4 tokenizer files exit=0, 0 FAILED (168 tests); ruff check + format clean on both files; merge-tree dry run main...branch rc=0.

NOT MERGED: same quiet-window reason as the health card.

title: Native core tokenizer format: chars on the tree, one scheme/origin surface (backward compatible)
body:
User directive: "chars should be on the tree and called core tokenizer format native — to know what we have"; build it BACKWARD COMPATIBLE (user overrode the risk-based deferral: "build it so its backward compatible").

PROBLEM: native models tokenize through two ad-hoc wrappers in domain/inference/_internal/slonet_provider.py (_CharTokenizer stoi/itos, _TreeTokenizer TokenTree) with no format identity — nothing on the object or the .soul says which format it is, so "which tokenizer served this?" needs a code crawl (the a4705a55 lesson). Vocab for char models lives OUTSIDE the tree machinery.

DESIGN (data unification, semantics stay per-format):
1. NativeTokenizer — one wrapper; ALWAYS carries a TokenTree (char: tree.vocab/stoi/itos built from the checkpoint stoi/itos — chars literally ON the tree; empty trie, _trained=False). encode/decode dispatch on scheme:
   - native/token-tree: exact current _TreeTokenizer behavior (tree.encode/decode incl. lowercase normalize + pretokenize).
   - native/char: exact current _CharTokenizer behavior (raw per-char, NO normalize, OOV->0, decode raw join, eos=stoi.get(chr(10),0), pad=0, vocab_size=max_key+1).
   Backward-compat contract: bit-identical encode/decode/eos/pad/vocab_size on legacy fixtures for BOTH formats; _CharTokenizer/_TreeTokenizer names stay importable (tests/core-py/test_slonet_provider.py + test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py import them); apply_chat_template hoisted (identical duplicate today).
2. Format tag on save: top-level soul.metadata["tokenizer_format"] = "native/char" | "native/token-tree" (parallel key — existing readers of metadata["stoi"]/metadata["tokenizer"] untouched). Load: ONE from_metadata helper at both load sites (from_soul + embedded-emb loader); tag read if present, else DERIVED FROM CONTENT (tree present -> token-tree, stoi/itos -> char); CONTENT WINS on disagreement (it is what encode/decode will actually use) + warning log.
3. origin: checkpoint path threaded where naturally in hand (from_slnc(path)), optional=None elsewhere; field only, NO log lines / NO API surfacing (user answered surface: off).

FILE SAFETY: domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py is DIRTY with another session WIP — NOT touched (SloBPE/SloUnigram provenance deferred). Targets: slonet_provider.py, train_pipeline.py (save stamp — verified clean), tests.

GATES: new tests/core-py/test_native_tokenizer_format.py (legacy bit-identity x2, tag round-trip, content-wins-on-mismatch, old names importable, apply_chat_template parity); existing test_slonet_provider.py, test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py, token_tree suites; ruff check+format.
