title: Site doctor: triage layer over domain/journeys — coordination + design (builds on journey owners, no new harness)
body:
PHASE 1 LANDED as `1c5abc300` (read-only probe). PHASE 2 LANDED as `29b6f126b`
on `feat/site-doctor-sse-triage` (branched off origin/main a01bc99b8, phase 1
cherry-picked in as 1e7b910c4 so phase 2 sits on main's tree, not the branch's).

=== PHASE 2: streaming routes judged on their first read ===

Phase 1 skipped every SSE route, and that was right for its reason: an SSE body
never finishes, so reading it to completion turns the client's own
IncompleteRead into a false failure. But skipping wholesale made a defect only a
consumer ever sees invisible — a route that accepts the connection and then
never emits is indistinguishable from a healthy one until someone waits.

Now judged on the FIRST read, bounded in bytes and seconds, and separated into
the outcomes that need different owners:
  ok              bytes arrived and they are events
  heartbeat-only  bytes arrived but every line is an SSE comment (`:`)
  silent          connected, nothing even within the window
  dropped         connection died mid-stream
  closed-empty    200, then closed having emitted nothing

=== TWO CORRECTIONS OF MY OWN MEASUREMENT (keep both) ===

1. FALSE SILENCE FROM A WINDOW SHORTER THAN THE THING OBSERVED. The first cut
   used a 4s window and reported /consciousness/stream and /errors/stream as
   silent when both were heartbeating exactly as written — consciousness.py
   heartbeats every 10s, errors.py:451 every 30.0s. That is phase 1's original
   sin in phase 2's clothes: the observation was shorter than the cadence, so
   correct behaviour read as a defect. STREAM_GRACE is now 35.0s, and
   test_the_observation_window_outlasts_the_slowest_heartbeat PARSES the
   cadences out of apps/api/server/routers instead of copying them, so
   tightening a heartbeat anywhere in the tree trips the test first.
   Cost tracks defects, not route count: a stream that emits returns the
   instant its first bytes arrive, so a healthy site pays ~nothing.

2. read() VS read1(). response.read(512) blocks until it has 512 bytes or EOF,
   so a route sending 13 bytes every 30s looked starved and then "dropped" at
   120s having never actually failed. read1() returns whatever one buffer
   already holds — the true first read. This also cut the run 141s -> ~50s.

=== LIVE RESULT (load ~1, :8080) ===
  7 streaming routes probed; 6 healthy (/consciousness/stream,
  /dashboard/events, /dashboard/stream, /health/stream, /system/stream,
  /training/stream) and 1 heartbeat-only: /errors/stream returned 200
  text/event-stream and emitted exactly 13 bytes in 30.6s — its own heartbeat
  cadence, no events. Correct for an idle error stream, so medium, not high.

Also re-confirmed live and NOT fixed here: lifecycle stuck in `init` (4816s
uptime), request_count=0 while inference_count>0, and 6 of 246 routes not
serving 2xx/3xx — /phoneme/languages 500, /providers 500, /registry/artifacts
None, /registry/verify None (both slow/hang, see card 2460373b),
/settings/training/analytics 500, /training/trends 400. The last two are NEW
since phase 1's 4 and are untriaged.

GATES: ruff clean; tests/contract/test_site_doctor_probe.py 11 passed (was 6,
the 5 new ones pin heartbeat classification, the window invariant, query-required
stream skipping, per-cause finding separation, and probe survival);
read-only held — 0 write verbs in the probe.

=== REMAINING (phase 3) ===
browser journeys via domain/journeys (avion+playwright — playwright IS
installed in the conda env), and inference-engine triage. Once the baseline is
clean, --strict exits 1 on any non-ok finding and can gate CI.


===== CLOSURE (Gene 2026-10-14) =====
SITE DOCTOR TRIAGE LAYER — DESIGN + COORDINATION DELIVERED (stale-card closure, 2026-10-14, Gene)

This card's deliverable was THE DESIGN + coordination (implementation lands via
follow-up cards, per its own SHARED WORKSPACE note). Delivered 2026-10-08 and

title: SSE keepalive: one shared primitive in domain.api
body:
## What

One shared SSE keepalive primitive, lifted from the one place it worked.

Measured surface (**re-measured; an earlier survey's output was truncated and
misstated this**): **52 StreamingResponse sites across 14 routers**.

- **5 routers hand-roll heartbeats**, under **3 different variable names**
  (`_last_heartbeat` x9, `_last_yield` x6, `last_heartbeat` x3).
- **9 routers / 27 sites have no keepalive at all** — `agents`(2),
  `dashboard`(3), `health`(6), `mobile`(3), `models`(2), `shell`(2),
  `souls`(3), `system`(2), `tools`(4).

`health.py` and `dashboard.py` are the diagnostic surfaces — the ones a probe
most needs to be able to tell apart from a hung process are exactly the ones
that never speak unless spoken to.

The one working implementation lived in `apps/api/server/training/sse_stream.py`
coupled to `build_training_sse_response`, so only 2 consumers could reach it.

## Landed

`04dc9973d` on `feat/sse-keepalive-primitive` (off origin/main `a01bc99b8`).

- `domain/api/_internal/sse_envelope.py` — `StreamPacing`,
  `SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` (10.0), `SSE_HEARTBEAT_FRAME`. Placed here, not in a
  new module: `domain.api` already owns the SSE envelope, so every consumer
  already importing it gets liveness for free. (Check-if-exists: a new
  `infrastructure/sse.py` would have been a third SSE module beside
  `sse_envelope.py` and `sse_fallback.py`.)
- `apps/api/server/infrastructure/sse_fallback.py` — re-exports all three with
  a pure-Python fallback, so routers keep one import path.
- `apps/api/server/training/sse_stream.py` — drops its hand-rolled copy.
  10 insertions / 10 deletions, **no signature change**.

## The design constraint worth keeping

A `with_keepalive(async_generator)` adapter cannot work, and the failure is
invisible on the wire. `asyncio.wait_for` CANCELS its awaitable on timeout, and
cancelling `anext()` throws into the generator at its await point. Measured on
CPython 3.12.14:

    silence 1 -> TimeoutError        (frame already cancelled)
    silence 2 -> StopAsyncIteration  (frame gone)

So the adapter emits exactly one heartbeat and then **closes the stream** — and
a clean close reads as normal end-of-stream, so the client sees success while
the route still looks healthy for having sent bytes. That is the worst available
failure mode. The timing must therefore live on the consumer's side of the
yield, where the coroutine being abandoned is a plain `queue.get()`.

Hence: extract the *invariant* (cadence, exact bytes, deadline arithmetic) and
leave the loop with the consumer.

## Gates

- `tests/contract/test_sse_keepalive.py` — **7 passed** (new). Includes the
  adapter-failure pin above so the code comment cannot drift from what the
  interpreter actually does, and a functional test proving the queue pattern
  survives repeated silence and still delivers a real event.
- `tests/contract` 21 passed; `tests/server/test_startup_routers.py` 49 passed;
  `tests/test_layer_conformance.py` 3 passed.
- Training suites (runtime / router_kwds / status_transitions /
  audit_instrumentation / webhook_consolidation / schemas) — **100 passed**.
- `ruff check` clean on all 5 files.

## Cost

No benchmark applies — the change is not on a training/inference hot path, and
`scripts/benchmark_latency.py` measures the live server, which runs old code.
Measured the touched path directly instead: the per-event timestamp write goes
from 202 ns inline to 291 ns via `StreamPacing` (+89 ns, +44%). That is
**0.0035%** of a 120 tok/s chat stream's loop, and the loop JSON-encodes each
event, which dwarfs it. Deliberately NOT adding a benchmark script for this —
a permanent gate on a 0.005% delta is a noise generator. Side benefit:
`time.monotonic()` is immune to NTP/wall-clock steps, which under a wall clock
could make a 10s keepalive fire early or never.

## Assumptions

- **API routers only.** The Rust gateway's SSE/compression path and the web
  client's reconnect behaviour are out of scope — separate toolchain, separate
  card.
- **10s cadence.** Training already streamed at 10s; unification adopts the
  plurality. The 30s `/errors/stream` cadence is not migrated here.

## Follow-ups (NOT in this change)

1. Migrate the 5 hand-rolled routers (`chat.py`, `consciousness.py`,
   `errors.py`, `infer.py`, `inference.py`) to `StreamPacing`.
2. ~~Add keepalives to the 27 bare sites~~ **CORRECTED 2026-10-12 by
   card 09360d76 (landed 0bbad4df2)**: this priority was wrong.
   health.py / dashboard.py / startup_stream are bare because they are
   FIXED-CADENCE producers where the loop is the clock, so an interleaved
   keepalive can never fire — it would be dead code. The real defect there
   is an *unbounded* `get_detailed_health()` call with no timeout: a blocked
   subsystem check wedges the stream with no signal. That is now fixed on
   health.py. Of the 27 bare sites only system.py is genuinely idle-capable
   and actually needs the keepalive — and that is blocked on this branch
   merging. See 09360d76 for the per-site shape table. — **`health.py` and `dashboard.py`
   first**: they are the observability surfaces, and an unobservable health
   stream is the exact failure the probe already caught once.
3. Derive the site-doctor probe's `STREAM_GRACE` from `SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL`
   instead of parsing cadences out of router source. **Blocked**: the probe
   (`scripts/site_doctor_probe.py`) is not in origin/main yet — it is on
   `feat/site-doctor-sse-triage` in the pending cherry-pick queue.

## Repo hygiene noted (not touched)

1. `.git/objects/6e/1d1f41f596be538904acb0444130ba1bc3d690` is a **0-byte object
   file** (dated Oct 10) and it blocks `git gc` for every session sharing this
   repo — every `git commit` prints a prune failure. Fixing it touches shared
   `.git` state, so left alone pending approval.
2. **The board card's `description` is a stale snapshot of an earlier draft** —
   it still quotes sha `01344c443` and the wrong "59 sites / 16 routers" figure.
   `sync.py:53` sets `description=note.body` only when *creating* a card and
   never refreshes an existing one, and `app-planner board` has no
   description-update subcommand. **This note is the source of truth** (per
   AGENTS.md: notes carry the body, the board is the derived view). Left
   unpatched rather than hand-editing shared `board.jsonl` while another
   session refactors `store.py`. Whoever fixes sync's description refresh
   should re-run it here and confirm the card picks up `04dc9973d`.

## Status

Implemented and green. **Merge is not approved by this card** — it joins the
pending cherry-pick series awaiting an explicit call.

title: Diagnostic streams: surface a stalled health check, keepalive on system
body:
LANDED 0bbad4df2 on fix/health-stream-stall-visibility (off origin/main
a01bc99b8). Merge is not approved by this card — it joins the pending
cherry-pick series awaiting an explicit call.

## Why this card exists (it corrects card d14cee64)

d14cee64 shipped the shared keepalive primitive (`StreamPacing`) and listed
"add keepalives to the 27 bare sites — health.py and dashboard.py first" as
follow-up 2. **That priority was wrong.** Inspecting the bare sites:

| site | shape | can it sit silent? | does a keepalive help? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `health.startup_stream` | fixed 1.0s cadence, terminates at ready | no | **no** — always emits |
| `health.health_stream` | fixed 3.0s cadence, body in `to_thread` | only when the build hangs | **no in-loop** |
| `dashboard.generate` | fixed cadence, body in `to_thread` | only when the build hangs | **no in-loop** |
| `system.generate` | `sub.async_read(timeout=0.2)` | **yes** | **yes** |
| `tools.unknown_stream` | one-shot error frame | no | no |
| `tools.generate` | token stream awaiting inference | maybe | not this card |

These routers are bare **because the loop is the clock**. An interleaved
keepalive cannot fire while the loop is blocked — so on `health_stream` it
would be dead code that never executes. The training loop is different: it
reads from a queue fed by an external producer, so silence is genuinely
possible and the keepalive means something.

## The actual defect

`health.py` built each snapshot with

    await asyncio.to_thread(self._build_health_snapshot, ctrl)

`_build_health_snapshot` -> `ctrl.get_detailed_health()` is synchronous and
**unbounded**, called with no timeout. If any subsystem check blocked — a lock,
a subprocess, a network call — the stream wedged *forever* emitting nothing.
A stalled health stream is indistinguishable from a healthy one, and it is the
one surface goal (A) requires an underlying agent layer to read. Silence must
mean "nothing to report", never "I am wedged".

## What changed

The build now runs as **one long-lived task** polled through
`wait_for(shield(task))`, so the generator keeps speaking while the check is
stuck and reports how long it has waited. `HEALTH_SNAPSHOT_STALL_S` = 3x the
cadence (9.0s): slower than the cadence is *late*, past that is *stuck*.

Two non-obvious properties, both measured on CPython 3.12.14:

1. **`shield`, not a bare `wait_for`.** `wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(...))`
   abandons the *future* on timeout, not the thread underneath it. Retrying it
   every cycle spawns a fresh pool thread each time — measured live threads
   **2->3->4->5** over four cycles. Shielded: **flat at 2** across ten cycles.
   Pinned by builder *call count* (what actually matters) not thread counting.
2. **The `task.done()` step is load-bearing, not an optimisation.** A build can
   finish *during* a cycle whose wait timed out. Without consuming that result
   the next cycle discards the finished snapshot and starts another build — the
   stream then stalls forever and re-spawns a thread on every completed build.
   My first draft had exactly this bug; the empirical probe caught it.

The stall frame is `phase=STALL` / `status=working` (not `error`): the stream is
alive and the check may yet return, so clients keying on `status` are
unaffected. Verified `health-blocks.ts` lifts `data` only and never reads
`phase` (0 matches) before adding a new phase value.

## Gates

- **`test_wedged_check_reports_stall_and_spawns_exactly_one_build` was A/B'd**
  against a naive no-shield variant that keeps the stall frame: it **fails**
  there (`5 == 1`) and passes here (`1`), so the pin discriminates rather than
  passing either way.
- New: `tests/server/test_health_router.py::TestHealthStreamStallVisibility` —
  3 tests (late-is-not-stalled; stall + exactly one build; recovers after a
  wedge without surfacing as an error). Real timing, not the
  `patch("asyncio.sleep")` trick, because the timing *is* the behaviour.
- Existing health suites: **86 passed** (83 pre-existing unchanged + 3 new).
- `tests/contract` + `tests/server/test_startup_routers.py` +
  `tests/test_layer_conformance.py`: **66 passed**.
- `ruff check` clean on both touched files.

## Assumptions taken

- **This branch carries no dependency on the unmerged keepalive branch.**
  `health.py` needs nothing from it, so it is cherry-pickable onto origin/main
  regardless of the merge call. Deliberate: work that cannot land independently
  is worth less while a merge decision is pending.
- Stall bound = 3x cadence. Chosen so a merely-slow snapshot never raises a
  false alarm, while a real hang is reported within one bounded window.

## Deferred (recorded, not forgotten)

1. **`dashboard.py`** — the identical defect, same fix mechanically once this
   pattern is proven in review.
2. **`system.py` keepalive** — the one genuinely idle-capable bare stream
   (`sub.async_read(timeout=0.2)` returns even when silent, so a `StreamPacing`
   check actually gets a chance to fire). **Blocked on d14cee64 merging.**
3. **`tools.generate`** — needs a separate judgement about bounding the
   inference await.

---

# Round 2 — commit 0d87bc474 (boot warmup), and three calls that resolved to NO change

Asked whether the module-import protocol is what slows us down, from a systems
view. Measured, and it invalidated two of my own claims.

## 1. DONE: warm the health snapshot at boot (0d87bc474)

The FIRST `get_detailed_health()` cost **804-1281ms** and landed in-request on
the first `/health/stream` subscriber. Chain, found by instrumenting
`builtins.__import__`:

    controllers/health.py:575  get_detailed_health()
      -> slolib/_internal/gpu.py:90  get_accelerator()
        -> gpu.py:133  _detect_best_backend()
          -> gpu.py:930 is_available()  ->  import cupy

`controllers.health` pulls **284 modules**; cupy alone is 279ms self / 758ms
cumulative. The preloader's `DEFAULT_PRELOAD_MODULES` (stdlib + httpx/fastapi/
pydantic/sqlalchemy) had **zero overlap** with this path — no `psutil`, no
`controllers` — so it never warmed it.

Fix: branch a `PgqProcess` beside the existing checkpoint warmup in
`_phase6_routers` — same class of problem (`first list_checkpoints()` ~1-5s),
ported not rebuilt. **Verified `PgqProcess` runs in-process** (marker file +
unrelated stdlib module both land in the parent's `sys.modules`); a forked
child would have warmed only the page cache and been a silent no-op.

## 2. CORRECTION: "~200x" was a cache artifact

`_CACHE_TTL = 2.0` vs stream cadence **3.0s** means production rebuilds every
cycle — real cost **1.479ms**, not 0.001ms. My "200x overhead" figure was
measured inside a single 2s cache window. Actual overhead ~10%, and
1.479ms / 3000ms = **0.05% of the interval**.

## 3. CORRECTION: `to_thread` does NOT protect against import

Measured with a 1ms heartbeat task:

| mode | max loop gap | work |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 3.1 ms | - |
| `to_thread(time.sleep)` | 6.9 ms | 504 ms |
| `to_thread(import slonet)` | **803.7 ms** | 802 ms |

The loop froze for the entire import. Module-body execution holds the
**process-wide GIL**, so moving an import to another thread only changes which
thread starves the loop. I said in chat that `to_thread` "helps with the
one-off import" — **it does not**. The code comment never claimed that (it
claims protection from "a lock, a subprocess, a network call", which *do*
release the GIL), so the code was right and my verbal claim was wrong.

## 4. Resolved to NO change, with reasons

- **Break the cupy closure** — the cost is once per process (global `_BACKEND`
  cache + `sys.modules`), and GPU backend/vram/tier are legitimate health
  fields already wrapped in `try/except`. Boot-warming makes it free. Ripping
  it out would trade real health information for a cost that no longer lands
  anywhere. Deferred unless a health check is ever expected to run pre-boot.
- **Drop `to_thread`** — rejected. It is load-bearing for the stall detection,
  which is what actually protects against a future blocking syscall. At 0.05%
  of the interval the cost does not justify removing the protection.
- **Re-examine 0bbad4df2** — survives. Re-read against the evidence: its stated
  premise (blocking lock/subprocess/network) is exactly what `to_thread` + the
  GIL *do* handle, and the shield/one-task invariants are pinned by an A/B'd
  test (5 builds vs 1). The failure was in my narration, not the commit.

## Gates (round 2)

ruff clean; `test_startup_routers` **50 passed** (49 existing + 1 new);
health + contract + conformance **103 passed**; startup finalizers/readiness
**12 passed**. The new test was A/B'd: removing the branch call fails it with
`branched instead: ['ckpt-warmup']`.


---

# Round 3 — commit 41a08f9dc: the deferred dashboard item, taken

The card's own note listed dashboard.py under "Explicitly deferred ... takes
the same fix mechanically once this pattern is proven". `0bbad4df2` proved
the pattern (A/B'd: 5 builds vs 1), so the deferral condition was met.

## 1. Stall visibility on /dashboard/stream

`generate()` awaited `asyncio.to_thread(_build_snapshot)` inline — the exact
defect this card was opened for, one file over. A wedged build silenced the
stream with no signal, and on a dashboard silence reads as *idle*, never as
*broken*. Now the same polled-task shape as health: one long-lived task
through `wait_for(shield(task))`, `DASHBOARD_SNAPSHOT_STALL_S = 3x cadence =
6.0s`, `phase=STALL`/`status=working`. The comment points at health for the
full derivation rather than restating it, so the two cannot drift apart.

## 2. Boot warmup — and it is a SEPARATE closure

Measured fresh: first `_build_snapshot()` = **1419ms** across 654 modules vs
**6.6ms** warm. Worse than health's cold path. Critically it is *disjoint*:
neither `controllers.health` nor `cupy` is in `sys.modules` afterwards, so
the health warmup (0d87bc474) does not reach it — dashboard has its own
closure (`domain.infrastructure`, `training.jobs`, event buffer). Branched as
its own `PgqProcess` so either warmup's failure stays isolated.

## Method note — a control that was invalid

I first "proved" the 6 broad-suite failures pre-existing by running them in a
probe worktree. That was **wrong**: `git worktree add ... HEAD` executed in
the *shared* repo, so the probe sat at `f0d174427` (another session's branch
tip) — a different codebase, not my base `0d87bc474`. Redone properly by
stashing my 4 files in my own worktree. Result:

- `test_companion_router::TestListPresets` (2 errors) — **pre-existing on my
  base**; they only pass at `f0d174427`, which means another session fixed
  them on a newer commit I do not have.
- `test_models_controller` (4 failures) — pass in isolation both ways, and
  report "System memory too low for safe model loading": environmental under
  a 1940-test run, not a regression.

## Gates

ruff check clean; ruff format clean on the 3 files I touched (the 4th has
pre-existing drift at lines 308-596 which I deliberately did NOT reformat —
sweeping it would put unrelated churn under this message). dashboard+startup
**67**; health+contract+conformance **103**; full `tests/server` **1940
passed** with the 6 above A/B-proven. The 3 new stall tests A/B against the
original inline generator: reverting only `generate()` fails them with
`expected stalls while wedged: [DASHBOARD x5]`.

## Still open on this card

`routers/system.py` keepalive — still blocked, it needs `StreamPacing`
(`04dc9973d`) which is not on this branch's tree.

---

# Round 4 — LANDED on main

Both halves of this card's shipped work are on the local integration trunk
**`main` @ `ca7ae8573`** (85 ahead of `origin/main`).

## sha mapping (branch commit -> landed commit)

| original (branch) | landed on main | subject |
|---|---|---|
| `0bbad4df2` | **`a6b59bf23`** | health: surface a stalled subsystem check instead of going quiet |
| `0d87bc474` | **`8709abff4`** | startup: warm the health snapshot at boot instead of in-request |
| `41a08f9dc` | **`ca7ae8573`** | dashboard: make a stalled snapshot visible, and warm it at boot |
| `2ed475805` | **`2ed475805`** (unchanged) | cli: render a stalled dashboard snapshot as a stall, not an idle server |

## Why CHERRY-PICK and not `git merge`

User approved "merge both branches now". A literal `git merge` of
`fix/health-stream-stall-visibility` into `main` was measured first and
produced **23 conflicts** — not from my 6 files, but because
`merge-base(main, origin/main) = 67c406ee2`, with **local main 81 ahead and
origin/main 288 ahead**. The lines have genuinely diverged; a merge would
have dragged that entire 288-commit divergence across the trunk, colliding in
`contract-baseline.json`, `routers/_manifest.py`, `AGENT_SYNC.md` and the
doctor -> mole tree rename.

My 3 commits touch only 6 files, and cherry-picking them applied **cleanly,
0 conflicts**, carrying exactly +564/-35 — the same content a merge would
have delivered, without the unrelated divergence. The CLI branch was based on
`main` itself, so that one fast-forwarded. Verified after landing:
`git diff fix/health-stream-stall-visibility main` over the 6 files is
**one** hunk, a docstring line my commit never touched — `origin/main` reads
``sloughgpt logs --dashboard``, local main reads ``sloughgpt monitor``.
Pre-existing divergence between the two lines, both still true (`train
monitor` exists as a subcommand), so deliberately left alone: not my change.

## Gates on the landed result (run on `main` itself)

dashboard + startup routers); **14 passed** (CLI suite incl. the 7 new stall
tests); earlier full `tests/server` 1940 passed with 6 A/B-proven
pre-existing/environmental.

## A coordination hazard I caused and repaired

I fast-forwarded `main` via `git update-ref` while another worktree
(`/home/mana/Documents/sloughgpt-api-std`) held `main` **checked out** — my
`git worktree list | grep refs/heads/main` check was wrong, because that

## Correction to an earlier claim

I told the user this merge would release `system.py`'s keepalive. **It does

title: BUG: slolib gpu.py duck-types numpy via hasattr(x, "device") — numpy>=2.0 breaks it
body:
Found during card 21135daa kernels-parallel work (Gene probe). domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py decides input device by hasattr(x, "device"). numpy>=2.0 ndarrays now HAVE .device, so the numpy->device conversion path is skipped and cupy ops crash. Same root cause as the closed card "GPU matmul always TypeErrors -> CPU fallback" (numpy>=2.0 ndarray.device defeats hasattr guard) — that fix was written, verified, then DECLINED+reverted; this card re-opens the decision with kernels-parallel evidence (benchmark works around it locally; real fix belongs in gpu.py). Fix: explicit isinstance(x, np.ndarray) check BEFORE the hasattr device probe. Tags: bug,gpu,inference. Status: todo.

PORTED 2026-10-13: branch fix/slolib-numpy2-discriminator, worktree /home/mana/.cache/wt-slolib-gpu, commit fb51433f3 (pathspec-limited to domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py + packages/core-py/tests/test_slolib_gpu.py).

Approach per brief: PORT of 20ef82c8c (fix/cpu-accelerator-elementwise, pushed), NOT the isinstance rewrite sketched in the original card text. The source commit replaces the hasattr(x, "device") cupy-vs-numpy discriminator with hasattr(x, "get") at 4 sites in gpu.py matmul (~L987-996). The .get idiom beats isinstance because gpu.py:981 ALREADY uses hasattr(arr, "get") as the cupy discriminator — the port makes the matmul path consistent with that existing idiom (cupy arrays and the test fake _CupArr expose .get; numpy>=2.0 ndarrays no longer fool it). Kept the source commit's fp16 tolerance recalibration (test_slolib_gpu.py:1337, atol 1e-4 -> 1e-2: the old passthrough silently computed fp32 in fp16 mode so 1e-4 was calibrated against the bug; genuine fp16 error ~5e-3). docs/AGENT_SYNC.md hunk (session bookkeeping +16) EXCLUDED via git restore — cherry-pick conflicted there on main, resolved by dropping.

title: Shell engine phase 1: WS /shell/term + VT100 emulator + <TermScreen>
body:
Goal: run the curses shell TUI in the web UI, like opencode web.

Context established by measurement (not assumption):
- Three terminal surfaces exist; none can render a curses TUI.
  * TerminalPanel  -> POST /shell/exec (req/resp), returns a PROCESSED string;
                      apps/web/lib/ansi.ts is an SGR style parser, explicitly
                      NOT an emulator ("a full VT100 emulator would be dead
                      weight here"), drops all cursor motion.
  * V86TerminalPanel -> SSE, sanitizeVmOutput handles only ESC[2J + \b and
                      strips every other sequence (broken for full-screen apps).
  * curses TUI      -> emits real cursor motion + alt screen (ESC[?1049h via
                      graphics.py, curses windows in tui_repl._render_all);
                      unreachable from the browser.
- No xterm.js dependency anywhere (apps/web/package.json has no terminal dep).
- Precedent for WS already in-repo: inference.py:1489 ws_generate
  (accept -> auth -> receive_text/send_json).
- Reference decoder already written and tested: tests/core-py/test_shell_tui_live.py
  decodes the pty byte stream into a persistent 80x24 frame.

Design (expert-reviewed, approved):
Alt-screen and scrollback are two BUFFERS OF ONE VT100 STATE MACHINE, not two
models. Build one engine, two projections:

  pty (server) --WS raw bytes--> SHELL ENGINE (client, primary+scrollback |
                                  alternate buffer)
                                      |-- projection A: alt frame -> <TermScreen> (TUI)
                                      |-- projection B: line log  -> <TerminalPanel>

PHASE 1 SCOPE (this card):
1. WS /shell/term carrying raw framed pty bytes + {resize rows,cols}, modelled
   on the existing ws_generate auth pattern.
2. From-scratch VT100 emulator, scoped to the sequence families the TUI
   actually emits (cursor addressing, alt screen, SGR, erase). Allowlist of
   sequence families -- deliberately NOT "interpret everything".
3. New <TermScreen> component rendering the ALTERNATE buffer.
4. Validate the emulator against the existing 80x24 decoder as reference.

MUST NOT AFFECT (explicit):
- TerminalPanel and V86TerminalPanel keep working unchanged until each is
  deliberately migrated in phases 2/3.
- TerminalPanel's measured perf contract: ~30us/line parse; full re-parse hit
  30ms/render (>16ms frame budget) at the 1000-line cap -- scrollback
  projection must stay incremental (capLines identity + WeakMap cache).
- The ansi.ts security property "raw escape garbage can never reach the DOM":
  the emulator reopens this surface, so sequence handling is allowlisted and
  reviewed as its own change.

PHASES 2/3 (separate cards, not this one):
- P2: primary buffer + scrollback path, migrate V86TerminalPanel (bug fix).
- P3: migrate TerminalPanel; needs /shell/exec to expose raw bytes -> contract
  change through the descriptor discipline.

Acceptance for this card:
- index updated (apps/README.md / docs/INDEX.md) if a new app/doc lands
- shared copy reused (no new node_modules/.venv; root toolchain)
- coordination named (this card is the shared-workspace handle for shell TUI work)

Known finding to fix in passing: the comment in test_shell_tui_live.py claims
"the browser shell feeds pty output through it to rebuild the cell grid for the
wire" -- no such component exists (ansi.ts says it is not that). Stale comment.

title: CLI dashboard: a stalled snapshot must not render as an idle server (completes the 5d5a92b8 stall signal end-to-end)
body:
LANDED 2ed475805 on fix/cli-dashboard-stall-render (branched off main 37e4c1053), 2 files / +133.

## The gap

Card 5d5a92b8 made /dashboard/stream emit phase=STALL when _build_snapshot fails to return within DASHBOARD_SNAPSHOT_STALL_S. But the CONSUMER never looked at phase: apps/cli/src/commands/logs.py::_render_dashboard reads only data.health/processes/events. A stall frame therefore rendered through the normal path as:

    SERVER no model  no model  up 0s
    SYS   cpu 0%  mem 0% (0MB)  reqs 0  err 0
    EVENTS
      (no events yet)

visually identical to a server that is idle and perfectly healthy. That relocates the exact defect the server-side frame exists to kill - silence reading as "nothing to report" - one hop downstream, to where a human is looking.

Fix: STALL renders as SNAPSHOT STALLED + the server message + the cadence; ERROR as SNAPSHOT FAILED. A stall is deliberately NOT dressed up as a failure (status=working means the stream is alive and the build may still return). Frames with no phase - ordinary snapshots and the /poll fallback - are untouched.

## Method note - I wrote this into another session's territory first

The edit was initially made in the SHARED worktree, which was on feat/notes-cli-gui-controller @ f0d174427 (another session). Caught it immediately, reverted both files there, and re-applied in a dedicated worktree off main. It could NOT be carried across because the bases differ and tests/cli/test_logs_unification.py does not exist on main - hence this card carries its own tests/test_cli_dashboard_stall_render.py in main flat tests/test_cli_*.py convention. title: Native tokenizer: unify char + token-tree into ONE algorithm (policy hoisted)
body:
WHAT: Unify the native tokenizer so char and token-tree are ONE algorithm, not two branches.
  User: "characters makes up tokens... we dont need separate char and token in native tokenizer implementation."

FINDING: TokenTree.query() does greedy longest-prefix match; over a depth-1 trie that
  reduces to exactly stoi.get(c,0) = the legacy _CharTokenizer body. One algorithm, two
  configs. NativeTokenizer.encode branched on self.variant -> two drifted code paths.

FIVE policy knobs had to be hoisted (not one): pretokenizer none|gpt2, lowercase F|T,
  word_suffix ""|</w>, oov_id 0|unk_id, decode raw-join|skip-specials+spaces.
  TRAP: a naive degenerate tree returns unk_id(1) on OOV; legacy char returns 0.
  test_oov_char_maps_to_zero pins encode("z")==[0]. Skip this and every existing
  char-vocab model silently changes ids (same silent-corruption class as SessionKVCache).

LANDED: sha 2bfabac5f on branch feat/tokenspace-char-tree-unify (NOT merged - see
  MERGE BLOCKED below).

WHAT SHIPPED:
  - TokenTree.__init__ now takes policy: pretokenizer ("gpt2"|"whitespace"|None),
    lowercase, word_suffix, oov_id, skip_special_decode. Defaults reproduce the
    old tree behavior byte-for-byte.
  - query(text, start=0) - the start offset replaces the per-step slice that made
    the walk quadratic (char has no pretokenization, so s was the whole document).
    Also falls through to the single-piece edge on an unmatched "<" instead of
    abandoning the match: a bare "<" that was a vocab character used to go OOV.
  - _CHAR_POLICY in slonet_provider states the legacy char behavior explicitly;
    _char_carrier_tree builds a real depth-1 trie instead of an empty carrier.
  - NativeTokenizer.encode/decode/pretokenizer now DELEGATE - the self.variant
    branch is gone from the algorithm. variant remains as provenance and drives
    only vocab_size/eos/pad attribute semantics (test-pinned).
  - to_dict/from_dict round-trip the policy; legacy sidecars without those keys
    load with historical defaults.

GATES (all green):
  - 346 passed / 41 skipped (native format + token_tree + tokenizer + slonet
    provider + morph + kv benchmark + shared indexes).
  - 37/37 byte-parity tests in test_native_tokenizer_format.py, asserted against
    the FROZEN inline oracles (_legacy_char_encode/_legacy_char_decode) - not
    against the legacy class names, which would be vacuous.
  - 45/45 independent checks: no self.variant in encode/decode/pretokenizer,
    depth-1 trie built, every legacy behavior matched, policy round-trips,
    "<" fallthrough works, legacy sidecars load identically.
  - ruff check clean, ruff format clean.
  - mypy: ZERO new findings (slonet_provider 86 on pristine HEAD -> 86 with
    changes; token_tree 6 -> 6; new script 5 -> 0).

BENCHMARK: scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py (new, registered in AGENTS.md).
  Three rows / five configurations, coverage reported FIRST so a low round-trip
  score is never misread as a decode bug:
    A Morph byte-level  cov total   F1 11/11  F2 11/11   0.93 Mchar/s
    B SloBPE            cov  89%    F1  7/11  F2  6/11   0.31 Mchar/s
    B SloUnigram        cov  89%    F1  7/11  F2  6/11   0.66 Mchar/s
    C TokenTree char    cov  89%    F1  8/11  F2  8/11   1.71 Mchar/s  <- fastest
    C TokenTree tree    cov  89%    F1  6/11  F2  2/11   1.33 Mchar/s
  Unification COST char 3.1x (6.03 -> 1.95 Mchar/s on an equal payload; 1.71 in
  the battery). 27% recovered via two behavior-preserving optimizations (skip the
  word-suffix copy when empty; hoist skip_special ahead of the dict/list lookups).
  The residual is the per-char query() call - closing it would mean a second
  inline implementation, which is the exact branch this card removes. Char is
  STILL the fastest row, 1.8x Morph, and absolute cost is 0.5ms per 1000 chars.
  Every non-total row scores on COVERAGE (89%), not decode - confirming the
  earlier 3-4/11 findings were test-corpus artifacts, as diagnosed.

MERGE BLOCKED (needs a human call):
  feat/tokenspace-char-tree-unify carries 576 commits not on main, of which only
  2bfabac5f is mine; the rest are board churn plus the state of
  feat/notes-cli-gui-controller at fork time. local main is also 91 ahead /
  290 behind origin/main. Merging would drag in ~575 commits that are not this
  card's, so the branch sits in REVIEW, not done.

FOLLOW-ON CARDS FILED (both pre-existing, verified against pristine HEAD):
  27d6e4ff - SloUnigram._all_segmentations enumerates every segmentation
             (exponential); one 48-char unbroken word hangs/OOMs train().
  823c6fba - TokenTree.train fails at vocab>=256: pugqeep compress_cluster
             emits accuracy outside [0,1]; k-means RNG also makes runs
             irreproducible (PYTHONHASHSEED=0 does NOT stabilize it).
  Both are why the battery runs under a 60s per-phase alarm and vocab_size=128.

SHARED WORKSPACE:
  index updated - yes, scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py registered in
    AGENTS.md benchmark list (tests/test_shared_indexes.py green).
  shared copy reused - yes, ONE TokenTree, no new module, no new dependency.
  coordination named - gate file tests/core-py/test_native_tokenizer_format.py;
    board churn from parallel sessions swept into this branch is NOT mine and is

title: SloUnigram.train hangs: _all_segmentations enumerates every segmentation (exponential in pretoken length)
body:
WHAT: SloUnigram.train hangs/OOMs on any long unbroken word. Discovered while
  re-running the tokenizer battery for card 8fefc101.

ROOT CAUSE: `_all_segmentations` in domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py
  materializes EVERY segmentation of a pretoken into a list. That is exponential
  in pretoken length. A single 48-char word
  ("lamavirtualassistantdesignedtoprovideinformation") is enough to hang or OOM
  train(). A 9-line corpus containing just one such word never finishes.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is not an exotic input. URLs, base64 blobs, identifiers,
  camelCase compounds and file paths are all unbroken runs. Any real corpus hits
  it, so SloUnigram is effectively untrainable outside toy data — which is why
  the battery needs a per-phase alarm to complete at all.

FIX DIRECTION: do not enumerate. Score segmentations lazily (generator /
  beam / DP over the lattice) and keep only the k best. The memory that matters
  is the frontier, not the full cartesian product.

GATE: a 48-char unbroken word must train within a bounded time. The battery
  (scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py) already carries that word as its last
  case — make it a hard assertion once fixed, and drop the 60s alarm for this.

EVIDENCE: found in battery runs for 8fefc101 (commit 2bfabac5f).

title: TokenTree.train fails at vocab>=256: pugqeep compress_cluster emits accuracy outside [0,1], and k-means RNG makes runs irreproducible
body:
WHAT: TokenTree.train raises ValueError for vocab_size >= 256 on small corpora:
  "Accuracy must be 0-1, got -0.1719..." (value varies run to run).

ROOT CAUSE: TokenTree.train builds embedding Points and hands them to pugqeep's
  PointLibrary.add, which validates `0.0 <= point.accuracy <= 1.0`
  (packages/core-py/domains/infrastructure/pugqeep/library.py:419). The point
  comes from PointCompressor.compress_cluster (k-means/Lloyd refit), which can
  emit an accuracy outside [0,1]. More vocab -> more points -> higher chance one
  is out of range.

EVIDENCE THAT IT IS PRE-EXISTING (verified, not introduced by 8fefc101):
  - pristine HEAD fails identically at vocab_size=256 (checked by restoring the
    original files and re-running);
  - in-process TokenTree.train is deterministic (two runs give identical vocab
    and merges), so the cross-process variance is the k-means RNG, not hashing —
    PYTHONHASHSEED=0 does NOT stabilize it;
  - only vocab_size >= 256 fails; 128 succeeds.

IMPACT: blocks training any tree larger than ~128 tokens on a small corpus, and
  makes results irreproducible across runs (a benchmark hazard).

FIX DIRECTION: (1) clamp/validate accuracy at the compressor boundary rather
  than letting PointLibrary reject it, and (2) seed the k-means RNG so embedding
  Points are reproducible.

GATE: TokenTree().train(corpus, vocab_size=512) succeeds; two runs produce
  byte-identical to_dict().

WORKAROUND IN PLACE: scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py uses vocab_size=128
  and documents why in a comment. Lift that once fixed.

RELATED CARD - CHECK BEFORE IMPLEMENTING (port, don't rebuild):
  vq-huffm (done) "Wire Huffman into compress_cluster + Point.generate" —
  compress_cluster was ALREADY touched by prior work. Read that card's evidence
  first: the accuracy defect may be a regression from it, or the fix may already
  exist behind a flag. Do not write a second compressor path.

REPRO (deterministic shape, random value):
  from domain.training._internal.token_tree import TokenTree
  TokenTree().train(<9-line corpus>, vocab_size=256, min_frequency=1)
  -> ValueError: Accuracy must be 0-1, got <varies>
  vocab_size=128 succeeds; vocab_size=512 also fails.

title: Core tokenizer: put SloBPE into the native format (lossless), keep Unigram on its own scheme
body:
WHAT: Put SloBPE into the core native tokenizer format as a lossless conversion
  — user: "put them in core tokenizer" / "then see how they compare as a whole
  [with] native tokenizer we just added as token tree and char".

PRECONDITION PROVEN (this is what makes the conversion safe):
  SloBPE.train and TokenTree.train are the same algorithm AND produce the SAME
  OUTPUT. Matched parameters (lowercase=X for both):
    lowercase=False -> 81 merges each, 81 shared, 0 bpe-only, 0 tree-only, vocab IDENTICAL
    lowercase=True  -> 82 merges each, 82 shared, 0 bpe-only, 0 tree-only, vocab IDENTICAL
  An earlier probe claimed "9/10 disagree, 71 shared, 81 vs 82 merges" — that was
  a PROBE BUG (SloBPE trained lowercase=False, TokenTree defaulted to True).
  Corrected: identical vocab + 100% shared merges.

  The residual 2/10 encode disagreement is NOT vocab — it is SloBPE.encode
  calling _normalize on input (.strip() + re.sub(r"\s+"," ",..)) which destroys
  data Tree preserves:
    '  leading and trailing  '  bpe -> 'leading and trailing'   tree -> preserved
    'line one\nline two\n'      bpe -> 'line one line two'      (newlines collapsed)
  Converting BPE into core therefore also RETIRES the lossy round-trip.

SCOPE:
  + NativeTokenizer.from_slo_bpe() — build the trie + lineage from SloBPE's
    vocab/merges (TokenTree.from_dict needs a trie; SloBPE.to_dict has none),
    wrap as NativeTokenizer(variant="tree").
  + battery row proving core-BPE == tree through the same interface.

OUT OF SCOPE (recorded, not silently dropped):
  - SloUnigram CANNOT convert: it is a Viterbi lattice walk, not a greedy trie
    walk. Forcing it in would re-fork encode/decode — the exact branch the
    char/tree unification removed. Stays its own scheme "training/unigram".
  - lowercase persistence: train(lowercase=False) never writes self._lowercase,
    and SloBPE/SloUnigram encode hardcode literal True (lines 279/1176/1213).
    Real incoherence BUT lowercasing-at-encode is PINNED CONTRACT
      test_lowercase_normalization_active: tree MUST lowercase
      test_case_is_preserved: char must NOT
    and it provably moves NO battery score (corpus has no uppercase). Follow-on.

CONTRACTS THAT MUST NOT BREAK:
  test_one_scheme_per_family_and_uniform_attrs (card 85dedb7e) — schemes stay
  {"native","hf","training/bpe","training/unigram"}; BPE does not become "native".
  test_delegates_encode_decode_to_tree / test_chars_live_on_the_tree — NativeTokenizer
  stays a TokenTree wrapper; no duck-typed dispatch.
  test_native_tokenizer_format.py 37 byte-parity tests.

SHARED WORKSPACE:
  index updated — yes if battery row added (registered already in AGENTS.md).
  shared copy reused — yes, no new module/dependency; converts into existing TokenTree.
  coordination named — token_tree.py / slonet_provider.py owned by card 8fefc101
    (branch feat/tokenspace-char-tree-unify, sha 2bfabac5f, status review).

LANDED: sha 436befcf4 on feat/core-tokenizer-bpe-into-native (NOT merged — same
  board-churn situation as 2bfabac5f; status is review, not done).

WHAT SHIPPED:
  - NativeTokenizer.from_slo_bpe(): replays SloBPE vocab into a trie and
    reattaches lineage from merges. Verified lossless on the structural
    contract: vocab identical, merges identical, lineage == len(merges).
    bpe.scheme stays "training/bpe" — card 85dedb7e untouched.

TWO DECODE DEFECTS FOUND WHILE VALIDATING (both real, both fixed):
  1. REGRESSION I introduced in 2bfabac5f. The skip_special "hoist" dropped the
     omit: it appended the literal marker on the True side and space-prefixed it
     on the False side. The 37 byte-parity tests never caught it because NONE of

title: tokenizer: train(lowercase=False) never reaches encode — 3 sites, 2 ways; contract-bound
body:
WHAT: The `lowercase` training argument does not reach encode, in three places
  two different ways. A model trained with lowercase=False still folds case on
  encode, leaving uppercase vocabulary entries that are unreachable.

  TokenTree.train(lowercase=...) uses it ONLY for corpus prep. self._lowercase
    is assigned in __init__ (default True) and never again — grep
    "_lowercase *=" finds no assignment outside __init__.
    encode/decode read self._lowercase, so the constructor default wins.
    -> uppercase tokens land in the vocab (verified: ' CASE</w>', ' CAS') and
       encode("Hello World") still returns "hello world". Dead vocabulary.
  SloBPE.encode    passes the literal lowercase=True (tokenizer.py:279)
  SloUnigram.encode / encode_with_scores pass the literal (1176, 1213)

WHY NOT FIXED ALREADY (deliberately deferred):
  Lowercasing-at-encode is a PINNED FORMAT CONTRACT, not an accident:
    test_lowercase_normalization_active — native/token-tree MUST lowercase
      (tok.encode("THE CAT") == tok.encode("the cat"))
    test_case_is_preserved — native/char MUST NOT
    TestNormalize.test_no_lowercasing — _normalize itself honours the flag
  So the incoherence is narrow: only `train(lowercase=False)` failing to
  persist. And it provably moves NO battery score (verified by running the
  battery with build_tree at lowercase=False — identical F1/F2), because
  CORPUS has just one uppercase char.

PROPOSED FIX (needs a call, because it changes a contract):
  Persist: TokenTree.train writes self._lowercase; SloBPE/SloUnigram gain a
  _lowercase field set by train, read by encode instead of the literal.
  Default stays True, so every default path and the format contract above
  are unaffected; only an explicit lowercase=False caller changes behaviour.
  DECISION NEEDED: should native/token-tree be allowed to opt OUT of
  lowercasing at all, given it is documented as part of the format? If the
  answer is no, the correct fix is the opposite — remove/deprecate the
  lowercase=False path from train instead of honouring it.

GATE: whatever is chosen, test_lowercase_normalization_active and
  test_case_is_preserved are the acceptance tests. Do not weaken either.
  Also re-run scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py (a case-faithful tree row
  would be a NEW row, not a replacement — char already covers that role).

FILES: domain/training/_internal/token_tree.py (train),
  domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py (SloBPE.encode 279, SloUnigram 1176/1213).

SHARED WORKSPACE: no new module, no index change. Coordination: token_tree.py
  is owned by card 8fefc101 (review) and touched by d0d36f55 (review).

DECISION 2026-10-16 (foreman, user call): HONOR lowercase=False — persist the flag
through train() into encode at all 3 sites (TokenTree.train -> self._lowercase;
SloBPE.encode :279; SloUnigram.encode :1176 + encode_with_scores :1213). Default stays
True, so native/token-tree's pinned lowercase contract and native/char's case
preservation are untouched; only an explicit lowercase=False caller changes behavior.
Batch: handed to Gene together with card 92af1aa0 (rehome uxjourneys); branches
fix/tokenizer-lcase-persist + feat/rehome-uxjourneys, one worktree per card.

title: Chat persist bug: stream-complete session-context save writes the stale pre-stream snapshot — assistant reply content only persists on the NEXT turn's save
body:
MEASURED 2026-10-16 while landing the first agentic journey (card 861c89e4, commit 43aad2473): chat-store.ts send() builds messagesWithNew = [...state.messages, userMessage, assistantMessage] before the stream (line ~421) and the stream-complete persist saves messagesWithNew.map(...) (~627) — token flushes replace message objects in state, so the captured array still holds the empty placeholder. Server transcript after one exchange = [.., prompt, ''] (measured via POST/GET /session/{sid}/*); the rendered reply reaches the session surface only when a LATER save reads live state (next turn's persist / useChatMessages storeSessionContext with messagesRef). Consequences: (1) /session/{sid}/context — the regeneration source — misses the latest reply after every exchange; (2) any crash/close after a turn loses the reply from context. The agentic journey works around it with a deterministic two-turn exchange. Fix candidate (frontend lane): persist live state (useChatStore.getState().messages at complete time) instead of the captured array. Re-resolving relative imports and facade re-exports cut that to 10 — a 69% false-positive rate. This is the fourth time string-matching has misled this analysis... Any tooling for this must build an import graph from AST the way Python resolves, not grep dotted paths."

No such tool exists — scripts/ has test-doctor.py, check_docs_api_parity.py, gen_ts_contracts.py, no import-graph tool. §8 step 3 already prescribes "verify with AST not grep".

BLOCKS:
§8 open question #5 — "Which of the 10 callerless modules get wired and which get deleted? Ownership sits with whoever holds the routers." That question is undecidable without this tool. It is also the gate on the knowledge/RAG duplicate consolidation:
  - domain/{core,cognitive,cognition}/_internal/knowledge_graph_v2.py — 3x 676L, byte-identical md5 2951268e (verified on main too)

A grep pass was already run this session and is DISCARDED per §7 — its "13 importers vs 9" count did not follow facade re-exports, so the two numbers were not comparable.

DELIVERABLE:
scripts/check_module_reachability.py — AST import graph resolving the way Python does:

  - sys.path package roots (domain, packages/*/src, apps/api/server, scripts)
  - roots = routers + entrypoints + __main__; fixed-point reachability walk
REPORT-ONLY by default (exit 0); --fail-on-unreachable gates later.
It must print a verdict for each of the 5 duplicate files above with its
AST-resolved importer list, so the dedup becomes mechanical rather than a guess.

§8 names as the collision risk.

title: RAG vector execution: indexing + retrieval requests run through the vector store (batched matrix rank) — the engine computes vectors, not just generation + search UX
body:
USER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-16 ('continue building'): we want vector-based computation — execution of the RAG engine AND vector store for indexing + retrieval of data — instead of just generation and user-facing search.

FOUND (verified): domain/inference/_internal/vector_store.py is a FULL vector store (VectorStore ABC, InMemoryVectorStore + MogDBVectorStore, VectorEntry/QueryResult, batched _build_matrix/_matrix_norms/_rank_matrix with versioned cache) whose upsert_sync/query_sync have ZERO callers in the RAG flow — RAGService imports only simple_embed. Today's dense leg (HybridRetriever._dense_search) is a per-chunk Python loop; ingest computes no vectors at all (lazy embed on first search). Built-but-unwired surface = the ModelStack pattern.

BUILD (TDD): (1) RAGService creates an InMemoryVectorStore, wires it as retriever._dense_store; upserts VectorEntry per chunk at ALL three ingest sites (add_document + both _load_documents paths — _load_documents bypasses the service method); resets+rewires on clear() (clear() rebuilds self.rag). (2) HybridRetriever._dense_search executes store.query_sync (batched matrix rank, version-guarded cache) when a store is wired; default _dense_store=None = behavior unchanged for every other caller; falls through to the loop if the store has no matches. Embed authority stays ONE fn (retriever _get_embedding, = simple_embed 384) for population and query — same vector space. (3) InMemory not MogDB store: documents persist via MogDB/JSONL and re-add through the same code path at boot, so a persisted store would be a second writer that can go stale (single-writer consistency).

BOUNDARIES: does NOT touch the BM25/sparse leg or ProductionRAG.add_document chunking (the in_progress BM25-rebuild card 4563be94 owns those — different methods, service-level wiring only; rag.py edit = one seam in _dense_search + one __init__ line). No external readers of chunk.embedding (grep: only rag.py's own loop).

TESTS: packages/core-py/tests/test_rag_service.py (isolated fixtures exist) — ingest→store round-trip, dense spy executes query_sync, query contract {question,results,context,num_results} + content hit, boot reload repopulates, clear resets.

body:

WIRE THAT'S MISSING (verified): KnowledgeGraph triples are extracted on every ingest (_extract_kg_claims) but consulted by nothing in the retrieval path — query() is flat only. This closes the gap between 'two flat structures' and the vector-graph mental model: hit one chunk -> follow its KG relations -> surface the connected neighborhood as context.

DESIGN: RAGService.query post-processes — collect entity keys from the top retrieved chunks + the question, match KG triples whose subject/object hit a key (one hop, no transitive walk), bound to a fixed max (no latency blowup), format matched triples into context ('- subject predicate object') + expose them as an additive 'kg_triples' field in the result dict (wire-additive, non-breaking). Empty/unpopulated KG = exact today behavior (no-op). KG classes and rag.py untouched — service-level post-processing only.

STACKED: based on feat/rag-vector-execution (c088a7b59) — retrieval now executes the vector store, and the expansion builds on those top hits; lands after it in the ports-lane batch.

title: DUPLICATE of a13140c8 (GraphRAG-lite, foreign claim) — handoff: hop semantics + design notes for the owning session; delete when 8c4b7927 lands
body:
USER APPROVAL 2026-10-17 ('build'): GraphRAG-lite as proposed — flat retrieval stays authoritative, one knowledge-graph hop expands the context the generator actually sees.

FOUND (verified): domain/cognition/_internal/knowledge_graph_v2.KnowledgeGraph has REAL traversal (get_outgoing/get_incoming/bfs/find_paths, facts dict of Fact{subject,predicate,object,confidence,source}), populated on every ingest via _extract_kg_claims -> _kg.add_fact, with kg_query already scanning facts as substring patterns. None of it is consulted at query time — the graph is write-only in the retrieval loop.

DESIGN: RAGService.query gains _graph_expand(question, result): probe = question + top-hit contents; HOP 0 = facts whose BOTH endpoints appear in the probe (asserted-by-passage, exact-substring, kg_query idiom); HOP 1 = facts sharing a subject/object entity with hop-0 facts (the genuine one-hop beyond flat). Matched triples -> result['graph'] = {entities, triples, expanded, hops:1} + a compact 'Knowledge graph (1-hop expansion)' block APPENDED to result['context'] (so generation sees it — a side key alone would be dead weight). Capped at 12 triples (confidence-desc) + 10 entities; results[] stays flat top-k (graph never injects ranked results in v1); expansion wrapped in its own try/except — KG failure degrades to empty graph shape, never breaks flat retrieval. Service-level only: ProductionRAG/kb endpoints untouched; additive response key = contract-envelope safe.

TESTS (TDD): packages/core-py/tests/test_rag_service.py class TestGraphRAGExpansion — one-hop proof (sibling triple surfaces via shared entity, unrelated triple absent, context carries it), empty-graph degradation, cap enforced, results stay flat. Benchmark: scripts/benchmark_rag_graph.py (new — query latency p50/p99 with vs without expansion + avg triples contributed; the benchmark obligation for a query-path change).

CLOSED AS DUPLICATE 2026-10-17 — real card = foreign claim 'GraphRAG-lite: retrieval consults the knowledge graph' / note a13140c8 (status doing, claimed first; user dispatched the same 'build' to two sessions). One card = one branch = one session — this claim stood down, no code written on feat/rag-graphrag-onehop.
DESIGN HANDOFF for the owning session (analysis from this side, use freely):
1. HOP SEMANTICS: seed hop-0 = facts whose BOTH endpoints (subject AND object, case-insensitive substring) appear in probe = question + top-hit contents — 'asserted by the retrieved passage' (string-entities-only would seed ALL facts of a mentioned entity at hop-0 and make the one-hop vacuous). Hop-1 = facts sharing a subject/object entity with hop-0 facts. Exact-substring matching = the kg_query idiom already in rag_service.py:468.
2. PUT TRIPLES IN result['context'] (append a compact 'Knowledge graph (1-hop expansion)' block), not only in a side result['graph'] key — kb rag_query passes context to generation; a side key alone is dead weight for the answer. Keep result['results'] flat top-k in v1 (graph never injects ranked results).
3. CAPS: 12 triples confidence-desc + 10 entities (summarize-don't-dump); expansion in its own try/except so KG failure degrades to an empty graph shape and never breaks flat retrieval.
4. INGEST HOOK ALREADY OK: _extract_kg_claims fires from add_document; VERIFY KG persistence across restart (KnowledgeGraph() is constructed fresh in _ensure_kg — facts may be memory-only per process; empty-KG no-op is the documented degraded mode).
5. BENCHMARK OBLIGATION: no script measures KG-query cost — a small scripts/benchmark_rag_graph.py (p50/p99 query with vs without expansion + avg triples contributed) is the suggested gate; benchmark_bm25.py already covers flat legs.
6. RAG FILES ARE HOT: this cluster (RRF doc, rag_service.py:4 docstring, kg_query traversal) implies concurrent edits to rag_service.py — claim discipline on that file matters this week.

The login story: launch with a named profile, log in once, avion reconnects to the same profile next time — still logged in — and recorded flows complete on top.

title: WIP cap + landing owner: repair the integration half of the methodology
body:
Diagnosis (2026-10-17 discussion, user-prompted): the written methodology (AGENTS.md SOP = kanban intake + contract-first + gated trunk-based) is sound, but its INTEGRATION half collapsed — ~90 cards stuck in review, trunk splits/resets stranded landed work, duplicate parallel implementations of the same card, board accreting faster than it drains (1240->1275 cards in ~2 days).

PROPOSED (foreman analysis — needs user/product shaping before implementation):
1. WIP limit: cap concurrent doing/wip lanes; the board enforces it (new cards queue), not conversation. Kanban's core mechanic, currently absent.
2. Landing owner: one role/session with merge authority whose only job is draining the review column — quiet-window lands, index clearance, cherry-pick ports. Today landing is everyone's afterthought and nobody's job.
3. Intake gate pairing: new-card rate capped by close rate (spawn discipline) — audit findings become notes queued behind WIP, not immediately-actionable cards.
Evidence anchors: review column ~90 entries; 43+'-list crashed-index commits (41 absorbed, forensically swept); search branch 398 conflicts (was 81) proving merge debt grows while quiet; PR #141 opened for an origin CI red whose fix sat stranded locally for 10 days.
